News.title: Woman and three children killed in fire after blaze tore through family home are pictured as heartbreaking tribute paid
News.content:
FIRE TRAGEDY Woman and three children killed in fire after blaze tore through family home are pictured as heartbreaking tribute paid







Next

A WOMAN and three children who were killed in a fire after an inferno tore through a family home have been named and pictured.

Elisha Brabin, 36, Leo Brabin, 16, Ellis Brabin, eight, and seven-year-old Prudence Brabin were named as the victims of the tragic blaze by Merseyside Police.



Emergency services, including six fire engines, descended on a semi-detached property on Stone Square in Bootle, Merseyside at around 3.45am yesterday.

Fire crews arrived to find the property “well-alight” before they bravely entered to search for people inside.



The fire service said in a statement that the victims were tragically found in an upstairs bedroom showing “no signs of life.”

An injured man who was outside the house when fire crews arrived at the scene remains in hospital at this time.



In a tribute issued today, the family said: “Our whole family is devastated by the loss of Elisha, Leo, Ellis and Prudence.

“Elisha was our beloved daughter, wife, mother, sister, aunty, niece and cousin. She was a devoted and loving mother who lived for her children. They were her whole world, and she meant everything to us.



“Our beautiful babies, Leo, Ellis and Prudence, were loved beyond measure and brought so much joy, happiness and love to our family. They filled our lives with laughter and precious memories that we will cherish forever.

“The tragic loss of Elisha and our three precious children has left us heartbroken. They have all been taken from us far too soon. The loss we are experiencing is unimaginable, and the impact on our family will be felt forever.

“As we try to come to terms with this devastating tragedy, we kindly ask that our family’s privacy is respected whilst we grieve and support one another through this incredibly difficult time.

“We would like to thank everyone for their kindness, support and understanding.”

Floral tributes and cards have since been left outside the home by neighbours.



Neighbour Loti Nambobe is taking care of the family’s dog in the aftermath of the blaze.

He told the BBC: “It’s a community. It’s broken. It hurts.”

Nambobe said he saw people trying to get into the home to rescue the family before fire crews arrived.



He added: “There were guys that tried to go in. People were doing everything, honestly. Like everyone here is a family and it’s broken everyone.”

One neighbour, who did not want to be named, said: “We all came out on the front and we could see smoke coming over from the houses.

“The sirens woke me up and there were fire engines in the street.”

Another woman said: “I heard shouting in the early hours but I just thought someone was having an argument, then I came downstairs and saw all the fire engines.”



The family’s next of kin have been informed.

Bootle MP Peter Dowd said: “My heart goes out to the family and friends of the four who lost their lives in a house fire in Bootle.

“Their loss is beyond words. This shocking event will touch everyone in our community.”

An investigation into the inferno, involving both police and the fire service is underway.



The street remains cordoned off by police and fire officers could be seen knocking on doors of neighbouring homes.

Fire engines could be seen arriving at and leaving the scene yesterday.

Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service Area Manager Kevin Longshaw said at the time: “This is a devastating incident, and our thoughts are very much with the family and friends of those who have lost their lives and been injured.

“We will work closely with relevant colleagues to ascertain the cause of the fire, but in the immediate term, we again extend our sincere condolences to those affected by this tragic incident.”

The fire service said in a statement: “Merseyside Fire & Rescue Service (MFRS) attended a house fire in Bootle on Tuesday, 22nd September and can sadly confirm that four people have tragically lost their lives in the fire.



“MFRS Fire Control received a 999 call at 3.38am and crews were immediately alerted, arriving on scene at 3.45am.

“At the height of the incident, six fire engines were in attendance. On arrival at Stone Square, firefighters found a semi-detached house well alight.

“Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus entered the property and began searching the property and fighting the fire.

“A casualty outside the house on arrival of fire crews was taken into the care of North West Ambulance Service and taken to hospital suffering from burns.

“During the course of their search, firefighters discovered four casualties in an upstairs bedroom, showing no signs of life.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Two members of North West Ambulance’s Hazardous Area Response Team (HART) were subsequently committed into the incident and tragically confirmed that all four had lost their lives.

“MFRS and Merseyside Police are now undertaking a joint investigation to establish the cause of the fire.”

News.title: British military using space ray to jam other nation’s satellites as UK takes on enemies in orbit
News.content:
STAR WARS British military using space ray to jam other nation’s satellites as UK takes on enemies in orbit







Next

BRITAIN has unleashed a new world-leading space weapon to neuter enemy satellites.

The ground-based ray gun has been fired in anger over the last year to “deter UK adversaries,” a top defence source revealed.



The system, which does not have a name and is used by the newly formed Space Force, could be used to prevent enemy satellites from tracking UK nuclear submarines, it is understood.

It is referred to at UK Space Command as “3 Squadron’s capability” and it works by jamming satellite signals.



The defence source insisted: “It is world leading, and some.”

They compared it to jammers on fighter jets that “deny the adversary the use their equipment”.

They added: “Let’s say a potential adversary were using their satellites to control a capability against us, we could use this capability to deny their ability to do that.”

Details emerged as the Chief of the Air Staff Sir Harv Smyth warned: “Space has become a warfighting domain and the UK must be prepared.”

Addressing the Air and Space Power Conference in London he accused Russia of “dangerous” manoeuvres in space.

He said: “In May of this year we tracked a series of unusual and significant manoeuvres by five Russian military satellites, moving to within rapid reach of two Finnish commercial satellites.



“These manoeuvres are uncommon and dangerous raising serious questions about Russia’s intent.”

He added: “In June it was confirmed that a Russian satellite constellation had caused disruptions to GPS signals across Europe, Greenland, and Canada, over at least 75 days since 2019.”

The UK’s new satellite jammer was invented by boffins at Porton Down, home of the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory which develops Top Secret future weapons.

Most jammers work by emitting signals to drown out or spoof the enemy messages.

The source added: “It started out as a concept demonstrator.



“As Space Command was stood up we started to explore the possibility of developing it from a science project to a capability.

“We accelerated from a concept demonstrator into a full capability in the last year or so.”

They added: “We use it to deter our adversaries.”

It is deployed with newly formed 3 Space Effects Squadron, the first UK unit “dedicated to disrupting, degrading and denying hostile threats in space,” the MoD said.

The UK has never avowed to have weapons in orbit – unlike the US.



America confirmed for the first time this month that it had, “on-orbit space control weapons”.

The UK Space Force was founded in 2021.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Sun revealed its commander Air Vice Marshal Jamie Thompson was suspended last month over claims of a “serious sexual assault” and theft just weeks after taking command.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: “Britain has to keep pace in the new space race…This century will depend on control of space.”

News.title: Moment couple filmed romping on packed tourist boat as horrified passengers watch through glass door in Venice
News.content:
Next

THIS is the disturbing moment a young couple were caught having sex on a water taxi in Venice.

Footage showed a young woman with her hands against the cabin door and her trousers lowered – while her companion holds her from behind.



Passengers watched in horror as the evening romp took place right in front of them, as the boat very fittingly passed by the most romantic sights of Italy’s Floating City.

At least one took out their phone to record the public fumble, which seems to have lasted only a few seconds before the pair gave up their efforts.



All travellers remained on the opposite side of the glass door, leaving the excited pair to do their business uninterrupted.

No one seems to have snitched on them to staff working on the vaporetto, which are also fitted with CCTV as they are public transport.

Inevitably, the video was shared on social media and has since gone viral, making it a less romantic memory for everyone involved.

And it has eventually made its way to the offices of the taxi management company as well as the local police headquarters.



Local reports said the incident happened on the N1 service from St Mark’s Square towards Piazzale Roma.

Reports differed over whether it took place on Friday or Saturday night.

In Italy, obscene acts in a public place, like this one, can be punished with hefty fines of £25,782, depending on the severity.

The offence can also become a criminal matter if it is committed in the presence of minors.

Authorities can also pursue such cases without a formal complaint being made.



The Sun previously reported on a similar incident in in Sóller, Majorca where locals were left outraged by the lawless behaviour on a public square.

Armed with a phone in his hand, the man appeared to record a video as they engaged in the raunchy act.

A huge church can be seen right behind where the couple were filmed during nighttime.

“For years, people have talked about bringing in high-quality tourism to avoid all this incivility, but in the end, we’re faced with reality, and this is what we have,” a fuming local said.

But it’s not just on the European continent where raunchy tourists can’t keep their hands off each other.



This summer an Australian tourist was deported and banned for a decade from Bali, Indonesia, after he was allegedly caught having sex on a local’s driveway.

Cops claimed to have caught Billy Aspinall, 27, with his pants down after CCTV allegedly showed him engaging in a sex act with a woman.

Balinese locals held a cleansing ceremony at the property to purge it of bad energy following the alleged lewd act.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Aspinall was arrested at the airport and spent two weeks in immigration detention before he was finally deported.

North Kuta chief police commander Ketut Sukadana that acts like this cause major “public concern” and will always be met with “firm action”.

News.title: Sick diver impales critically endangered turtle with speargun ‘before cooking sea critter’ as he’s arrested
News.content:
Next

A SICK diver has allegedly impaled an endangered turtle with a speargun before cooking and eating the critter for dinner.

Disturbing footage from earlier this month shows the diver as he lies in wait for the majestic hawksbill sea turtle.



He approaches the creature from behind, sneaking up behind it as it lies by a coral reef.

The diver brandishes an enormous speargun.



He aims it at the animal at close range, shooting it straight through the neck.

The injured turtle can be seen writhing in pain and flailing in the water.

Horrifying images then show the “animals were allegedly cooked and consumed”, police said.

Cops arrested Chinese diving instructor Wei Shang, accusing him of being the diver in the twisted video.

The horror hunting incident in Piaynemo, eastern Indonesia shocked the local community and environmentalists.

Hunting sea turtles has been banned in Indonesia since 1999, while spearfishing is also illegal inside the protected Raja Ampat marine area.



The footage is thought to have been recorded between September 9 and 11.

Diver Wei was arrested by Indonesian immigration officers at Sultan Hasanuddin International Airport as he prepared to board a flight to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia on September 14.

But he denied being the diver who had killed and eaten the turtle.



He pleaded in a social media video: “I did not kill the turtle. The person in the video is not me.”

Officials are yet to determine if Wei was responsible for the sick slaughter.

Turtles are considered a rare delicacy in certain coastal and island communities, but killing them and eating them is banned in most parts of the world.

The hawksbill sea turtle is classified as critically endangered worldwide.

He was suspended by diving organisation AIDA.



The group said in a statement: “AIDA International is aware of the serious allegations concerning an AIDA Instructor Trainer.

“We share the anger and disgust expressed by our community regarding the killing of a sea turtle, and unequivocally condemn the deliberate killing or any mistreatment of protected marine life.

“The Instructor Trainer has been suspended pending a formal investigation. This suspension is a precautionary measure and does not represent a finding regarding the allegations.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hunting sea turtles has been banned in Indonesia since 1999.

Spearfishing is also illegal in the protected Raja Ampat marine area, known as one of Indonesia’s best diving destinations.

News.title: Argentina’s President makes outrageous demand for UN to help him seize Falklands after Burnham raised islands with Trump
News.content:
Next

ARGENTINA’S president has begged the UN to help him seize the Falkland Islands – in the tyrant’s latest desperate bid at snatching the British territory.

It comes after Argentine players waved a disgraceful banner at the World Cup – and follows weeks of Donald Trump refusing to throw his weight behind the UK over the row.



Argentine leader Javier Milei claimed owning the territory was a “national cause” for his country, before demanding talks with Andy Burnham.

Milei blasted the “useless” UN for not aiding the South American country with the “dispute” during a long-winded ramble in New York today.



He also vowed to continue taking legal action against oil firms operating near the Falkland Islands – which Argentine nationalists call Las Malvinas.

Milei told world leaders: “Las Malvinas are a national cause… I repeat, Las Malvinas are a national cause.”



It is the latest in a series of baseless claims from Milei over the British overseas territory.

His increasingly threatening tirades have come after tensions reaching a boiling point during the World Cup this summer.



Argentina’s players waved a pathetic banner after beating England in the semi-finals falsely claiming the Falklands belonged to Buenos Aires.

The Argentine FA was slapped with a £237,000 fine by Fifa for this and a series of other ugly incidents that took place in the aftermath of the tournament.

In recent weeks, Milei has used raging speeches to declare the region as historically Argentine.



He has claimed in televised speeches several times that the Falklands are Argentina‘s “future”.

Domestic opposition parties have accused Milei of trying to distract the population from his other political woes.

It also comes as Donald Trump repeatedly refuses to rule out the Argentine nationalist’s claims to the islands.

The madcap firebrand is close allies with the US president – who also failed to show support for the UK over the row yesterday.

During the first ever face-to-face meeting between Trump and Burnham, the US leader stopped short once again of giving his full support to Britain on the issue.



Earlier this month, Trump questioned the UK’s ability to defend the Falkland Islands due to its domestic issues like immigration and energy.

Burnham has since hit back and said the UK “will stand firm in the face of any threats” to the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.

The PM said: “I didn’t react immediately when the Argentinian president made his recent comments, but in this forum, I think it’s right for me to set out the position clearly, and the clear position is: we will stand firm in the face of any threats.

“We will defend the right of the Falkland Islanders to self-determination and to remain British.”

He added: “And I just wanted the president to know directly from me, that’s the clear British position, and he very much understood what I was saying.”



Although Trump has repeatedly hinted at giving support to Buenos Aires over the claims, the US previously supported Britain’s campaign to retake the islands after the Argentine invasion of 1982.

Argentina cites its proximity to the Falklands as a basis for its claim, with the islands approximately 300 miles away from the country’s eastern coast.

Britain’s sovereignty over the Falklands is based on its long-term administration of the islands, and on the principle of self-determination for the islanders, who are almost all of British descent.

In 2013, residents voted overwhelmingly in favour of remaining a British Overseas Territory.

Of 1,517 votes cast in the referendum, 1,513 were in favour and only three against.



The Falklands War came in 1982 when Argentina invaded and occupied the islands, along with some other nearby British territories.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The conflict lasted just ten weeks as British troops recaptured Port Stanley and Argentinian forces promptly surrendered.

Despite lasting a short amount of time, 649 Argentine soldiers were killed in the conflict, as well as 255 British service personnel and three civilians.

News.title: Girl, 12, electrocuted by 30,000 volt pylon while taking photos for dangerous new social media trend fighting for life
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HORROR TREND Girl, 12, electrocuted by 30,000 volt pylon while taking photos for dangerous new social media trend fighting for life







Next

A CHILD has been electrocuted with 30,000 volts and left dangling from a pylon while taking photos in a dangerous new social media trend.

The 12-year-old girl was reportedly climbing a pylon to try and take photos to post online.



She suffered serious burns and is now fighting for her life in hospital.

The terrifying accident took place in Navahermosa, near Toledo, in central Spain.



It was reported to emergency services at 6.46pm on Monday.

The girl had touched a power line while scaling the pylon and suffered a massive electric shock, which left her dangling in the air.



Firefighters from Talavera de la Reina, Toledo, rushed to the scene to save the girl.

They shut off the power supply before climbing the tower to rescue her.

Paramedics treated the girl at the scene before she was ambulanced to La Paz University Hospital, Madrid.

She remains in a very serious condition.



Firefighters have warned against a worrying trend of attempting “dangerous and almost impossible challenges” to try and take photos for social media.

They said “A photo is not worth your life”, adding that “no photo, video or post is worth taking the risk”.

Firefighters added that climbing pylons can mean you’re hit with deadly shocks even if you don’t touch a power line directly.

A statement from the fire brigade said: “Operation to rescue a person who had climbed an electrical tower and suffered an electric shock.

“Before beginning the rescue, the electrical risk was managed by confirming that the installation was de-energised and free of voltage.



“Subsequently, the individual was secured and lowered using an aerial ladder truck, with the affected person then handed over to medical services.”

Last year, a two-year-old girl was electrocuted to death on a trampoline in a freak fairground accident in Spain.

Three other children also suffered electric shocks and were taken to hospital.

The kids are understood to have touched a metal mesh fence around the trampoline which had an unearthed electric current running through it.

News.title: Dog walkers warned of deadly parasite lurking in gardens and woodlands this autumn
News.content:
Next

DOGS Trust has issued an important warning to owners over autumnal dangers that could be fatal to pooches.

The UK’s leading dog welfare charity shared the vital advice to mark the official first day of autumn on September 23.



A survey conducted by the charity on 1,008 dog owners found that a large amount are in the dark about the dangers this time of year can pose.

The Dogs Trust data showed that 88 per cent of pup owners are unaware that things like conkers, mouldy fruit and mushrooms can be dangerous or fatal.



Meanwhile, walkers are being warned of deadly parasites like lungworm larvae, that can lurk on slugs and snails and be fatal if consumed by dogs.

In advice to Brits walking four-legged friends this season, Dogs Trust says that keeping an eye out for particular hazards is vital.

Toxic mushrooms and fungi

While not all wild mushrooms found in the UK are harmful to dogs, there are many that are. And it’s not worth a sniff.

“Some fungi can be toxic to dogs and species can be difficult to tell apart. Keep your dog away from mushrooms, using high-value treats to entice them into safety,” Dogs Trust says.

Acorns and conkers

While the droppings from oak and horse chestnut trees are rife during autumn, they are far from harmless for dogs and shouldn’t be thrown for them.

“Nature’s toys are best left where they fall. Acorns and conkers can make dogs unwell and may cause a dangerous blockage if swallowed. Stick to dog-safe toys for fetch,” the charity explains.



Rotting food

Old fruit and other food found along walking routes, from trees or dropped by humans, can also make your canine sick.

Dogs Trust says: ” Mould on any rotting food – from fruit to bread left over after a picnic – can be toxic to dogs, while some pips and stones can cause sickness or a dangerous blockage.”

Slugs and snails

While your furry pet might show interest in wildlife like slugs and snails during walk time, it’s important to keep them away.

The slimy creatures can carry parasitic larvae such as lungworm, which can make dogs very unwell – or even be fatal.

“Slugs and snails can carry parasites that are harmful to dogs. Don’t let your dog eat them or lick their slime trails,” the charity added.



Ticks

Keeping an eye out for ticks on your dog during and after a walk should be a priority, especially after walking through long grass and foliage.

Dogs Trust advises giving pooches a “post-walk once-over” to check for ticks that have clung on.

“Ticks can attach themselves to dogs and may transmit disease or cause irritation. Check your dog after walks, particularly long grass or woodland.”



In a bid to keep dogs safe during autumn walks, Dogs Trust has rolled out sniffable signs to catch dogs attention and alert owners to seasonal dangers.

The Walkies Warning Signs are being trialled throughout a popular walking spot on the borders of the South Downs National Park.

They feature a doggy-safe scent and are placed at eye level for dogs, while a QR code is available for owners to scan to learn more about risks in the area.

Tesse Kimber, senior veterinary surgeon at Dogs Trust, said, “There are many hazards that come with the ‘ruff season’, but also simple and easy ways to keep dogs safe. Our online guide and Walkies Warning Signs mean both dogs and their owners can confidently enjoy every walk.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Some simple steps include being vigilant, keeping your dog on a lead and away from potential hazards, and bringing high value treats with you in case you need them,” she added.



Know the warning signs – lethargy, upset stomach, restlessness and rashes can all be signs of potential ingested toxins. And act fast; get your dog to the vet right away if your dog shows any signs of encountering a hazard.”

News.title: ‘Truly historic’ Hurricane Polo hit rare cat-5 status as winds rocketed to 180mph with threat-to-life without landfall
News.content:
Next

ONE of the most powerful hurricanes in decades is threatening thousands of lives even though it’s unlikely to make landfall.

Hurricane Polo was a Category 5 storm on Tuesday, the highest on the scale, with winds near 180mph before it weakened to a Category 4 on Wednesday in the West Pacific.



The hurricane off the coast of Mexico downgraded on Wednesday, but will remain “a very powerful major hurricane during the next few days,” according to the US National Hurricane Center.

While Polo is predicted to remain offshore, it is expected to bring intense rainfall to the southwestern coastal areas through Thursday.



“This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain,” the hurricane center said.

The storm could bring three to six inches of rain, with some areas across the coastal portions of Guerrero and Michoacán reaching upwards of eight inches.



The Mexican states of Oaxaca, Jalisco and Colima are expected to see two to four inches of rain in coastal areas.

Swells generated by the storm are also expected to affect parts of southwestern Mexico over the course of a few days.

“These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip current

conditions, and coastal flooding,” forecasters advised.

Southern California is predicted to escape the worst of the storm’s wrath, but Hurricane Polo could still stir up trouble with swells along the coastline, which was recently hit by another offshore storm, Hurricane Marie.



Kristen Corbosiero, a professor at the University at Albany’s Department of Atmospheric & Environmental Sciences, told NPR, that Hurricane Polo “is one of the strongest storms ever in the [Pacific] Basin.”

The historic storm could bring tropical moisture to the area depending on the conditions in the upper atmosphere, Bryan Lewis, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Oxnard told the Los Angeles Times on Monday.

Lewis said the biggest concern is high surf and high tides that will coincide next Monday and Tuesday, which could result in coastal flooding.

“After almost an entire summer of southern swell after southern swell, there could be some issues for those vulnerable coastlines,” he said.



Locals are being advised to expect tropical storm conditions and hurricane-force winds at 150mph on Wednesday, which could continue into Thursday.

The US Embassy in Mexico issued a weather alert warning citizens to avoid the water and beaches, saying, “Even if the storm does not make direct landfall, heavy rain may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides.

“Hazardous ocean conditions—intensified by storms—may result in deadly rip currents and rogue waves.”

“So far, the information we have is that (Polo) will not make a direct landfall on the coast,” Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Tuesday.



Polo is expected to move north on Wednesday and take a sharp right to the northwest later in the day as it continues west-northwestward over the weekend.

Locals have begun preparing for the major risks that come with hurricanes, such as high waves and flooding.

Concepción López Villegas told NPR she has been busy preparing her seaside restaurant along the coastline of Lázaro Cárdenas in Michoacán, fearing powerful waves could destroy her small business.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We’re worried and trying to protect our businesses,” she said.

“And of course, we’re sad because it’s our heritage, our legacy that from one moment to another could be destroyed.”

News.title: Bootle house fire: Mum and her three children found dead in bedroom are named
News.content:
Bootle house fire: Mum and her three children found dead in bedroom are named

Elisha Brabin, 36, Leo Brabin, 16, Ellis Brabin, eight, and Prudence Brabin, seven, were found dead after a fire ripped through the home in Stone Square, Bootle on Tuesday

View 6 Images Elisha Brabin, 36, died with her three children (Image: Merseyside Police)

A mum and her three “beautiful babies” have been named as the family who tragically died in a horrific house fire.

‌



Elisha Brabin, 36, and children, Prudence, seven, Ellis, eight, and 16-year-old Leo, were found in the bedroom after the blaze ripped through the property on Stone Square in Bootle, Merseyside on Tuesday.

‌



Her husband, Kane Stephenson, 34, smashed windows as he desperately tried to rescue his family - but suffered serious burns as he was beaten back by the flames. He was taken to hospital for treatment.

‌



Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service said none of the four victims showed any signs of life. Emergency services found the semi-detached house "well alight on arrival".

View 6 Images Prudence Brabin, 7 (Image: Merseyside Police)

A statement from the family said: “Our whole family is devastated by the loss of Elisha, Leo, Ellis and Prudence. Elisha was our beloved daughter, wife, mother, sister, aunty, niece and cousin. She was a devoted and loving mother who lived for her children. They were her whole world, and she meant everything to us.

‌



“Our beautiful babies, Leo, Ellis and Prudence, were loved beyond measure and brought so much joy, happiness and love to our family. They filled our lives with laughter and precious memories that we will cherish forever.

View 6 Images Ellis Brabin, 8 (Image: Merseyside Police)

“The tragic loss of Elisha and our three precious children has left us heartbroken. They have all been taken from us far too soon. The loss we are experiencing is unimaginable, and the impact on our family will be felt forever.

‌



“As we try to come to terms with this devastating tragedy, we kindly ask that our family's privacy is respected whilst we grieve and support one another through this incredibly difficult time. We would like to thank everyone for their kindness, support and understanding.”

View 6 Images Leo Brabin, 16 (Image: Merseyside Police)

Flowers, balloons, photos and teddies have been left at the scene of the tragedy. One neighbour said she was haunted after hearing a woman screaming at around 3.30am. She said: "I heard a commotion and went outside. I heard screaming, the lady was shouting."

‌



Another said Elisha and Kane married two years ago, adding: “They were a lovely family. It’s so sad. They lived for each other. They were besotted with each other. Everyone on the estate went to their wedding. He tried, and the neighbours tried, to get them out. He tried his best to get his family but couldn’t get past the landing.”

A GoFundMe page set up aiming to raise £9,000 for the family says: “Our community has been left heartbroken following a devastating house fire that has tragically taken the lives of members of a family.

View 6 Images Officers seen wearing hazmat suits near the property on Stone Square in Bootle (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



“At a time of unimaginable grief, we want to come together to support the family’s loved ones and help ease some of the financial pressures they may now be facing.

“Every donation, no matter how small, will make a difference. If you’re unable to donate, simply sharing this fundraiser can help us reach more people.

“Our thoughts are with the family, their loved ones and everyone affected by this heartbreaking loss. Thank you for your kindness, support and generosity.”

‌



Fire chiefs say the blaze at the semi-detached property “spread rapidly” in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

View 6 Images Tributes left at the scene (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Neighbour Loti Nambobe, who is taking care of the family’s dog after the fire, said: “It’s a community. It’s broken. It hurts. There were guys that tried to go in. People were doing everything, honestly. Like everyone here is a family and it’s broken everyone.”

‌



He told how neighbours ran into the street to help: “It was scary, horrible to even think about. It was hard, everyone wanted to help. People were throwing bricks to try and smash the window, trying to get ladders up. They were trying everything they could to help.”

A joint investigation involving Merseyside Police and Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service is continuing, with a mobile incident room set up close to the scene.

The Bishop of Liverpool the Rt Rev Ruth Worsley and Bishop of Warrington the Rt Rev Simon Robinson said they were “deeply saddened to hear of the devastating incident”, adding: “Our thoughts and prayers are with their families and loved ones at this unimaginably difficult time.”

‌



Bootle MP Peter Dowd said: “My heart goes out to the family and friends of the four who lost their lives in a house fire in Bootle. Their loss is beyond words. This shocking event will touch everyone in our community.”

He said that police and other emergency services “must be allowed to undertake their investigations into this tragic situation”, adding: “I also want to put on record the outstanding work our emergency services do in such challenging personal circumstances.”

Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service (MFRS) arrived on the scene at about 3:45am on Tuesday and found the semi-detached house “well alight”.

Crews in breathing apparatus went into the house to try to bring the blaze under control and search for anyone inside.

They later confirmed that four people “showing no signs of life” had been found in an upstairs bedroom.

News.title: RAF Valley crash - live: Video shows Hawk jet coming down and exploding on Anglesey
News.content:
The Hawk T2 plummeted to the ground in North Wales moments after taking off, with witnesses reporting a 'big bang' and flames coming from the jet.

An RAF jet crashed in North Wales as witnesses reported seeing flames erupting from the aircraft.

The T2 Hawk aircraft had just taken off from RAF Valley on Anglesey when the jet ran into trouble, with two crew members ejecting using parachutes shortly before it hit the ground. Eyewitness reported hearing an "enormous bang" and seeing a "huge wall of fire" as the jet crashed.

North Wales Police said two pilots are being treated "for what are thought to be minor injuries and at this stage". The force has told the public to avoid the area until further notice.

One witness said: "We watched take-off, we're on shoreside and have watched hundreds take off. I said to my wife it's in trouble as I could see flames as it took off."

A Royal Air Force spokesperson told the Mirror: "An incident involving an RAF T2 Hawk aircraft, flying out of RAF Valley, occurred near Anglesey. An investigation is underway and we will not comment further at this time."

News.title: Met Office issues ‘exceptionally warm’ forecast and names areas facing 28C
News.content:
Met Office issues ‘exceptionally warm’ forecast and names areas facing 28C

Some parts of the UK could see temperatures reach at least 28C on Friday as Met Office weather forecasters say conditions will be 'exceptionally warm' for this time of year

View Image Anomaly maps show temperatures rising above the average in the south-east on Friday (Image: WXCHARTS)

The Met Office says temperatures could rise as high as 28C in some parts of the UK before the end of this week.

‌



Temperatures are expected to rise over the next two days, although forecasts suggest some wet and windy weather conditions are on the cards next week.

‌



Tomorrow will be “largely dry”, the Met Office says, with the mercury rising into the low-20s for much of England and Wales. A cold front will arrive in the north-west by Thursday afternoon, bringing some rain which could lead to mixed conditions over the weekend.

‌



However, temperatures should reach 27-28C in the south-east on Friday. The Met Office has described these conditions as “exceptionally warm” for this time of year.

UK extreme weather alert as Polar Vortex leaves Britain facing deep freeze READ MORE :

Met Office warns of 'Godzilla' super El Nino storms with weeks to go until peak READ MORE :

Temperature anomaly maps for Friday show southern and eastern parts of England shaded in orange. This also indicates that temperatures will rise well above the seasonal average.

‌



Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster Dan Holley said: “Once early fog patches clear in the south, Friday will be exceptionally warm for late September, especially in the southeast closest to an area of high pressure over the nearby Continent.

“A weakening cold front will drift gradually southeastwards overnight and into Saturday, with temperatures falling back closer to average over the weekend.

“This sets up a mixed weekend of weather, much of Saturday will be fine and dry before an increasing chance of rain or showers on Sunday, especially in more western parts.”

Article continues below

Met Office forecast for next week

Unfortunately, the national weather agency says “a period of wet and windy weather” is on the cards for Tuesday and Wednesday next week.

Mr Holley continued: “While details are naturally uncertain at this range, a particularly deep area of low pressure could pass close to the UK during the first half of next week.

“This may bring some wet and windy weather for some, which coupled with high spring tides could bring impacts to some coastal areas in the west.”

News.title: Brit tourist, 71, found dead 'by heartbroken wife' on Greek holiday island
News.content:
Brit tourist, 71, found dead 'by heartbroken wife' on Greek holiday island

The couple were holidaying at the coastal resort town of Hersonissos on Crete's north coast when the man's wife reportedly found him in their hotel room

View Image Hersonissos is a town in the north of Crete (file photo) (Image: Getty Images)

A Brit tourist has been found dead, reportedly by his heartbroken wife, while the couple were holidaying on a popular Greek island.

‌



The 71-year-old British tourist was found in the hotel where the couple had been staying at the coastal resort town of Hersonissos in Crete.

‌



The couple had come to the town on Crete’s northern coast on holiday and were staying at a hotel there when disaster struck.

‌



Local media reports suggest the wife of the victim found the 71-year-old unconscious in their shared hotel room and called the emergency services.

But despite the best efforts of emergency workers, the man was pronounced dead a short time later.

‌



British tourist dies after being pulled from Crete sea during Greece holiday beach trip READ MORE :

The man is yet to be named and authorities are working to establish the exact cause of the incident.

The Mirror has contacted the Foreign and Commonwealth Development Office for a comment.

The news comes just days after a 60-year-old British tourist got into difficulty at the Kato Gouves beach on the northern shore of Crete and tragically died.

Article continues below

The Brit was pulled from the water unconscious and rushed to the General Hospital Venizeleio in nearby Heraklion, where he was sadly pronounced dead, according to Creta Live News.

An investigation into the incident has now been launched by the Heraklion Port Authority, while an autopsy is due to take place to determine the exact cause of death.

News.title: UK grocery store boss extradited to Italy on £40million tobacco smuggling charges after anti-mafia probe
News.content:
UK grocery store boss extradited to Italy on £40million tobacco smuggling charges after anti-mafia probe

EXCLUSIVE: Hasan Ferhat Baybasin, 34, was sent to Genoa accused of masterminding a huge international operation flooding Britain with illegal cigarettes using complex maritime routes

View 4 Images Hasan Ferhat Baybasin has been extradited

A UK grocery store owner has been extradited to Italy on charges of masterminding a £40million international cigarette smuggling network following an anti-mafia investigation.

‌



Hasan Ferhat Baybasin, 34, was held as part of a huge police operation spanning five countries into a network allegedly flooding Britain with illegal tobacco.

‌



Officers seized more than 40 tons of cigarettes worth around £40m along with assets worth over £2m. Baybasin, from Edgware, North London, was extradited to Italy last month after dropping his opposition to the move, the National Crime Agency said on Wednesday.

‌



He had previously appeared at Westminster magistrates court alongside co-defendant Cagdas Duran, 37.

The pair, both directors of the Target Food Store in Radford, Nottingham, had been remanded in custody to face extradition proceedings.

A judge in Genoa, Italy, ordered their pre-trial detention along with three other alleged gang members held in Italy and Poland.

‌



View 4 Images Hasan Ferhat Baybasin (left) and Cagdas Duran are pictured (Image: Europol)

According to the European Public Prosecutor's Office, cigarette smugglers used a number of complex maritime routes to evade customs. Illicit cargo originated in Armenia, going through Dubai and on to Spain before entering Italy at Genoa.

Other routes passed through Georgia, Kenya, the Netherlands and Turkey. The suspects are said to have established a network of accomplices across the world, and the cigarettes were destined for the black market in the UK and other European nations.

‌



They allegedly claimed they were shipping building materials and used containers with false bottoms to hide their illegal cargo.

A corrupt IT specialist is said to have created and managed fake websites and emails as a front for the network while the plotters allegedly used encrypted phones to avoid law enforcement.

View 4 Images Law enforcement search a shipment of suspected illegal cigarettes (Image: Handout)

‌



An HMRC spokesperson said of Baybasin and Duran on Wednesday: "Both subjects in question have been extradited to Italy following the official request and they remain in custody in Italy pending trial."

Baybasin is charged with being a "manager, organiser and financing member of a criminal organisation" established to smuggle tobacco into the EU via the port of Genoa.

He faces three further counts of smuggling cigarettes on separate dates in July, September and October, 2024.

‌



Duran is charged with the same three smuggling counts along with being a member of a criminal organisation tasked with managing the finances.

Baybasin is understood to be a member of a notorious family that founded the Hackney Bombers organised crime gang in North East London. Huseyin Baybasin, 68, became known as "Europe's Pablo Escobar" when he masterminded the export of vast quantities of heroin while leading the network in the 1990s. He has been in custody in Holland since 1998 but has been cleared to begin a pathway leading to his release.

The group, known as Bombacilar in Turkish, has been locked in a bloody war with the rival Tottenham Turks gang which has resulted in at least a dozen murders.

‌



View 4 Images The motorcycle gunman who shot a girl in London is still wanted by police (Image: PA)

A senior figure of the Bombers was the intended target of a shooting at a restaurant in Dalston, North East London, in May 2024 that left a nine-year-old girl with a bullet lodged in her head. Six weeks later, senior Turks member Izzet Eren, 41, was shot and killed in Chisinau, Moldova, in what is believed to be a titfor-tat attack.

An NCA spokesperson said: "Hasan Ferhat Baybasin consented to extradition in early August and has been removed from the UK."

‌



An HMRC spokesperson said of Baybasin and Duran on Wednesday: "Both subjects in question have been extradited to Italy following the official request and they remain in custody in Italy pending trial."

Baybasin is charged with being a "manager, organiser and financing member of a criminal organisation" established to smuggle tobacco into the EU via the port of Genoa.

He faces three further counts of smuggling cigarettes on separate dates in July, September and October, 2024.
