News.title: ‘42 surgeries in 48 hours’: Doctors face extreme pressure in South Sudan
News.content:
Dr Mathiang Agany had no idea what was coming.

On a humid morning in April, scores of patients were rushed into his basic hospital in rural South Sudan after a shoot out between rival gangs. As the most senior doctor, Dr Agany, a maternal health specialist, had to perform 42 surgeries in just 48 hours.

Working alongside a second surgeon, a nurse and an anaesthetist, Dr Agany, 44, carefully extracted bullets from the vital organs of nine patients.

In 22 cases, he glued together fractured bones; and in four others he clamped damaged tissues shut and repaired torn organs.

Over the same 48 hour period, he also delivered seven babies through emergency c-sections.

“You are tired... but you can relax later,” he told The Telegraph over a video call.

“My job [was] to keep people alive”.

Separate to the ruinous four-year civil war in neighbouring Sudan, the violence plaguing South Sudan is inter-communal, a self-perpetuating cycle of cattle raiding, territorial disputes and revenge attacks carried out by armed youth militias from pastoral communities known as Titweng (“cattle guard”).

Young children were among the victims, including a four-year-old boy, whose leg was fractured by a gunshot, and a nine-month-old baby girl whose chest was grazed by the same bullet that killed her father.

Sports.title: ‘She’s been so brave’ – Jamie O’Hara shares emotional update on newborn baby girl in hospital as he vows to ‘spoil her’
Sports.content:
Next

JAMIE O’HARA has vowed to “spoil” his baby girl as he offered a health update.

The former Tottenham star became a father for the fourth time earlier this month as wife Keziah Grubb gave birth.



O’Hara, 39, revealed at the time that his new baby girl had been born premature, weighing in at just 3lb 13 oz on her arrival.

Sixteen days on, O’Hara offered a positive update.



Alongside a picture of his daughter, the talkSPORT star wrote on Instagram: “Our little baby doing well putting on weight and building her strength.

“Hopefully she’ll be home soon, she doesn’t even know how much I’m going to spoil her, she’s been so brave already.”

After his daughter’s birth, O’Hara declared that “life is complete” while gushing over the doctors and nurses that helped deliver her.

He wrote at the time: “We welcomed a beautiful baby girl into the world this morning, mum and baby are doing fine a little earlier than we expected but she done so well to get to 3lb 13.

“The doctors and nurses at Princess Royal have been incredible, my life is complete I got my little girl never thought it was going to happen.

“I’m going to love her with everything in my body, my beautiful wife I’m so proud of you I’m now officially a girl dad, gooooooooood baby thank you to everyone for their support”.



O’Hara wed partner Keziah At St Mary’s Church in Dartford back in April.

He is also dad to sons Archie, 16, Harry, 15, and George, 13, from his previous marriage to Danielle Lloyd.

Harry was born 10 weeks premature, with doctors having to fight to save his life.



In July, O’Hara reflected on what happened while wishing his boy a happy birthday, calling him his “little miracle son” in an Instagram post.

Sports.title: Man Utd flogging pieces of Old Trafford TURF for £125 each with fans offered bizarre ‘one-of-a-kind collector’s item’
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are flogging tiny chunks of TURF from the Old Trafford pitch for £125 each.

The ‘Theatre of Dreams’ unveiled new grass for the first time in 14 years over the summer.



Now the old surface has been cut into 7cm x 7cm chunks, boxed up and shipped off to fans around the world.

The cubes are wrapped in a black box that also contains a picture of the stadium.



United emailed club members and season-ticket holders on Tuesday night to inform them they had “exclusive early access” to the product, which they described as a “one-of-a-kind collector’s item”.

A notice on the website read: “Take home a piece of Old Trafford with this official turf cube, perfect for fans who want a keepsake from one of the most famous pitches in the world.

“Carefully preserved, this piece of turf makes a priceless memento of iconic games played at home and keeps the memories of match days alive.

“Perfect for gifting to passionate Reds, this turf cube makes a great addition to desks or can be displayed in a cabinet with other Manchester United collectibles.”

United offered fans the chance to buy a cube of grass from the previous pitch when it was dug up before the 2012/13 season and the club said the initiative was popular.

About 96 per cent of the Old Trafford pitch is made from natural grass and the other 4 per cent made of artificial fibres stitched deep into the soil.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

On Wednesday, United recorded a £47million pre-tax loss for 2025-26 taking cumulative losses across the past seven financial years to £444m.

United announced three months ago that they had acquired the majority of the land for the construction of a new 100,000-seat stadium 350 metres away from Old Trafford.

United’s full-year financial results, published on Wednesday, revealed £63.5m was spent buying land for their new stadium.

United’s debts remain eye-watering at £1.6BILLION, despite announcing record revenues for the year of £677.6million.

In addition to a long-standing debt of £577.6m, United have liabilities of £473.9m (about £355.5m of which relates to transfer fees owed), and £110m outstanding on their overall debt facility.



Despite recording a full year operating profit of £22.6m, United once again posted an overall loss for the year of £43m, compared to £33m the year before.

CEO Omar Berrada said the club would take a “disciplined approach” to their spending.

Fan protests against the Glazer family have extended to Ineos since last season, with the latest demonstration taking place outside Old Trafford before the Manchester derby defeat to Enzo Maresca’s 10-men.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk in tense spat with Dutch reporter who tells Liverpool captain ‘you aren’t acting your usual self’
Sports.content:
Next

VIRGIL VAN DIJK was involved in a major spat with a Dutch reporter who accused him of “BETRAYING” the national team.

The Oranje’s Round of 32 exit at last summer‘s World Cup, which cost Ronald Koeman his job, was savaged by the Dutch media.



Among the vocal critics of the Netherlands’ exit at the hands of Morocco was De Telegraaf’s Valentijn Driessen, who brutally claimed Koeman and Van Dijk “betrayed” everything the national team “stands for”.

He also suggested that Koeman changed his formation to a back five in order to protect his skipper.



And Van Dijk clearly hadn’t forgotten about Driessen’s scathing assessment when they came face to face at a press conference ahead of the Netherlands’ Nations League clash against Germany on Wednesday.

As he reflected on the Oranje’s early exit, Van Dijk said: “Well, it’s easy to say in hindsight: ‘We should have done this differently.’



“Or, ‘We should have done that differently.’

“One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five.

“That is utter nonsense. The fact is, we simply failed at the World Cup – those are the hard facts.”

Driessen felt compelled to press Van Dijk after feeling called out by the Liverpool defender.

Sports.title: ‘We didn’t care about football’ – Robertson admits Liverpool switched off after Jota death as he defends Isak and Wirtz
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL legend Andy Robertson revealed the team stopped “caring about football” after losing beloved friend and team-mate Diogo Jota last year.

Jota tragically died at the age of 28 along with his brother Andre Silva in a car crash in July 2025, just 11 days after marrying Rute Cardoso with whom he had three children.



The legendary striker’s untimely passing sent shockwaves around the world and especially rocked the Reds – where he spent five years before the fatal accident in Spain and won every available domestic honour.

So much so that Robertson, 32, admitted he and his Liverpool team-mates completely switched off due to the heartbreak.



And the full-back, who left Anfield after nine glittering years this past summer for Tottenham, insists that was the reason star signings like Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak struggled.

The Scotland international is adamant last season’s transfers lacked the necessary guidance – especially from the veterans – due to the grief that took cover the dressing room.

Robertson told Stick to Football brought to you by Disney+: “It’s difficult to describe or talk about, really, because what we went through, it was horrendous. Say if I’m talking about the new signings, they’re coming into a club that is heartbroken.

“They’re trying, and that’s where I felt so sorry for these guys because they’d signed and they were signing for big money and all that, if I’m talking about football. It took them months to settle in because we didn’t care, we didn’t care about football.

“That was the truth of it. We didn’t care about football because you’ve just lost one of your best mates in the changing room.

“That’s why I probably have so much sympathy in football terms towards the new signings, because I think they came into a team that was, like… we were elite in everything that we did for years.



“And maybe we couldn’t be that because of what had happened. And then they started getting quite a lot of criticism.

“That’s why I think these lads will be absolutely fine at Liverpool. I would treat this season as their first season. That’s the way I would do it.”

Liverpool failed to retain the Premier League title and finished fifth, which led to former manager Arne Slot’s dismissal just one year after an incredible maiden campaign.

Robertson insists that was because the entire team “lost their edge” and couldn’t compete with their rivals.



The Tottenham star added: “I think all footballers, we all have that edge, don’t we? And I think when you lose that edge sometimes then you can’t perform to the best. And I think last season we lost the edge.

“I think when I look back on it now, I think we lost that determination a little bit and things like that because I know at times we were maybe going, ‘You know what, what’s the point?’

“Like look at what Jota’s family are going through. Look at his kids. But yeah, we were grieving. It was our mate at the end of the day. He’s not a footballer to us, he was a team-mate, he was a friend.

“So, yeah, for us it was incredibly difficult. The week before he died, I was at his wedding.

“That’s one of the most difficult things you’ll ever go through. Seeing him on the happiest day of his life, and then the next week you’re seeing his family torn apart.”

Sports.title: Tottenham star Pedro Porro set to miss weeks with hamstring injury in blow to misfiring Spurs
Sports.content:
Next

PEDRO PORRO is set to be sidelined for around a month with a hamstring injury.

The World Cup winner sustained the problem in the first half of Tottenham’s 3-2 home loss to Aston Villa on Saturday.



He has withdrawn from Spain duty during the international break and is doubtful to be back in time for the Premier League visit to Manchester United on October 10.

The influential full-back may miss the hosting of Coventry nine days later, in what is gearing up to be a huge match for winless Spurs.



There is hope at present that Porro can be back in time to face London rivals Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on October 24.

It is a blow for boss Roberto De Zerbi, whose Spurs side are bottom of the table despite spending more than £300million in the summer.



Porro, 27, was one of a number of existing players who signed bumper new deals, along with Antonin Kinsky, Lucas Bergvall and Micky van de Ven.

Spurs have no natural right-back cover for Porro since selling England star Djed Spence to Inter Milan in the summer.

Archie Gray is the most likely candidate to fill in for Porro during his lay-off.

The 20-year-old is naturally a midfielder – and sees his long-term future in the middle of the park – but has deputies at right-back in Porro’s absence already this season.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Porro banged the ground in anger after picking up his hamstring problem against Villa and had to be replaced for Gray on 17 minutes.

The Spaniard later wrote on Instagram: “Sometimes you have to stop, take a breath and start again.

“Now it’s time to recover and trust the process.

“I’ll come back stronger, hungrier and more motivated than ever. This is just another obstacle on the road. See you soon.”

Spurs have endured a nightmare start to their season, failing to win any of their first five Prem games and being knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

Sports.content:

MANCHESTER UNITED have made Antonio Conte their top target to replace Michael Carrick as manager, claim sensational reports in Italy.

Carrick, 45, is already facing pressure as boss after enduring a difficult start to the season.

Previous defeats to Brighton, Manchester City and Hull also drew criticism.

The Italian has an impressive 60.4 per cent win rate in English football.

His most recent spell in the Premier League ended in explosive fashion, as he was sacked by Spurs following a scathing post-match rant in March 2023.

Conte won a Premier League title and FA Cup during his spell at Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Cardiff star Krystian Bielik charged with misconduct by FA after appearing to grab young fan by NECK
Sports.content:
EFL SHOCK Cardiff star Krystian Bielik charged with misconduct by FA after appearing to grab young fan by NECK







Next

CARDIFF City’s Krystian Bielik has been charged by the FA with misconduct following his Portsmouth clash at Fratton Park.

The update comes after their Championship game on September 5, where the player was accused of acting in an improper manner around the 71st minute.



The whistle was blown in the 70th minute after Bielik became involved in an altercation as he attempted to retrieve the ball from home fans.

The Cardiff star, 28, appeared to grab a young fan by their NECK, leaving supporters in shock at the shameful episode.



In response to the grab, the fan looked to have slapped the Polish centre-back before being shown the exit by the stewards.

The family of the supporter also departed from the stands.

Police launched an investigation at the time of the incident.

And following the inquiry, Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary revealed the supporter and player have agreed to an out-of-court disposal.

As part of the recompense, Bielik apologised to the Pompey fan – and there will be NO further action taken.

Bielik will now have until September 25 to respond to the FA charge.



Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary told SunSport: “Following an incident involving a Portsmouth FC supporter and a Cardiff player at Fratton Park on 5 September 2026, we have now concluded our investigation.

“After speaking with the complainant and reviewing all available evidence, the matter has been resolved by way of an out-of-court disposal, agreed by all parties involved.

“As part of this resolution, an apology has been provided by the player.

“The matter is now considered closed, and no further action will be taken in relation to this incident.”

Portsmouth launched their own investigation at the time, as highlighted in a club statement.



They said: “Portsmouth Football Club are aware of supporter concerns regarding the incident involving a young fan and an opposition player at yesterday’s match at Fratton Park.

“As this remains a safeguarding matter and is currently under investigation by both the club and the police, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further on the circumstances at this time.

“However, we are aware that a number of claims and assertions are circulating on social media.

“We would urge caution against speculation while enquiries are ongoing.

“The welfare and safeguarding of young people are of paramount importance to Portsmouth Football Club.



“We will continue to liaise with the relevant parties as enquiries progress.

“No further comment will be made at this stage while investigations remain ongoing.”

Pompey collected three points from the Bluebirds, after Conor Shaughnessy and Marezi Marezi both found the back of the net.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bielik escaped a punishment from referee Ben Speedie in the 72nd minute.

But he was not fortunate to survive the entire game without a booking after picking up a yellow in the ninth minute.

Sports.title: Man Utd news LIVE: JJ Gabriel latest as new deadline set after 'agreement reached'
Sports.content:
Former Man United striker Louis Saha has urged Real Madrid and Barcelona to steer clear of highly-rated youngster JJ Gabriel amid growing interest in the teenager.

He said: "Barcelona and Real Madrid should stay away from JJ Gabriel. I don’t think it is good for the game or the nature of the industry. It seems a terrible message to other young players and their advisors too. Success in football needs patience. You need to work for the opportunity and wait for it to come and then, after you’ve played the games and made that impact, it’s a different conversation.

"Doing really well in the academy, that’s great, but it means nothing in the first team. You don’t get to walk in straight away and replace senior professionals like Matheus Cunha or Bryan Mbeumo or whoever else. That is completely unrealistic and it places too much pressure on a young player. He is the son of a former footballer too. They should know better than to put all this risk on him so early.

"Look at Martin Odegaard. He had all the skills. He looked like he could do it all. He went to Real Madrid and never got his chance. Sometimes you need to protect these players from themselves and their advisors. I can’t understand how they don’t see that for themselves."

He added: "Can JJ Gabriel leave Man United and make an impact at another club as Paul Pogba did at Juventus, or like Jadon Sancho when he left Man City for Borussia Dortmund? I think he is in the sort of position on the pitch where it would be a bit easier to make that breakthrough playing as a forward. In that part of the pitch, you can make mistakes and it is fine. He is not a defender where those mistakes can hurt the team more.

"We saw it with Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United when he was young but he was not as young as JJ Gabriel. This is a different situation. There are always exceptions that can be made but the Premier League is a physical competition and JJ Gabriel will get special attention from teams and that will be very hard on him, physically and mentally, no matter what his trajectory could be.

"Paul Pogba and Jadon Sancho were good examples in the past but where are they now in the game? They are no longer in the frame. Not everyone can be Wayne Rooney. He was mature at 16. He had the physique of a monster. JJ Gabriel is not that sort of player, and he will get targeted."

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott enduring second loan nightmare as Liverpool star branded 'overweight'
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott enduring second loan nightmare as Liverpool star branded 'overweight'

Having endured a wasted season at Aston Villa, Harvey Elliott chose Valencia as his next loan destination from Liverpool but things are already off to a bad start

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott's time at Valencia has started badly (Image: Manuel Queimadelos/Getty Images)

"My goal is to regain my self-confidence, play freely and enjoy my football."

‌



Harvey Elliott's stated objective at his unveiling as a Valencia player told the story of a player looking for a fresh start. After a miserable season on loan with Aston Villa, Elliott headed to Spain this summer believing he'd made the perfect choice this time around.

‌



Having made just nine appearances and been given the cold shoulder by Unai Emery at Villa, who didn't play him in order to avoid triggering a £35million obligation to buy clause, and been told he didn't feature in Andoni Iraola's plans at Liverpool, Elliott found a new home - and a manager who did want him.

‌



"I had a few calls with Carlos Corberan, in which we talked about my objectives and what he expected of me as a player," he explained of his loan move at the start of September. "The start of the season has been tricky, but there’s still a long way to go.”

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Elliott must be wondering what he did to be landed with such rotten luck after Corberan was sacked just 10 days after his comments. Valencia entered the international break 19th in La Liga and in turmoil after losing five of their opening seven matches.

Their Liverpool loanee has featured just three times, with all of his appearances coming off the bench and totalling 88 minutes. Already the pressure is ramping up.

Valencia are paying the majority of his wages - which reportedly make him the team's third-highest earner - and so far the 23-year-old midfielder is not living up to his billing. Spanish newspaper Marca reports that he is well above his ‘optimal playing weight’ and has been told in no uncertain terms to improve his fitness during the international break.

‌



View 2 Images Harvey Elliott's fitness has been questioned at Valencia (Image: Jose Breton/Getty Images)

Elliott's Instagram account, where he boasts 2.2m followers, shows a player trying to project an image of calm and focus. "See you after the break Valencianistas! We will continue to work and come back better, Thank you for your support," he posted on Monday before then sharing pictures from training on Wednesday.

As well as winning over the Valencia faithful, Elliott now has a new boss to impress after the club appointed ex-Mexico manager Javier Aguirre to replace Corberan. Like Elliott, Aguirre is only contracted until the end of the season and will therefore waste no time in making decisions.

‌



It is easy to forget, given he made his Liverpool debut aged 16, but Elliott is still in the early stages of his career. He has 149 appearances, 15 goals and 21 assists to his name for Liverpool, where he remains under contract until June 2028.

All is not lost. Despite shunning him, Emery was complimentary of Elliott. "He’s a very good person and player and deserves the best," the Villa boss said in January.

Perhaps being at a struggling club where his services are not discarded but instead desperately needed will prove to be the re-making of him.

Sports.title: Police end Krystian Bielik probe but FA charge Cardiff star after Portsmouth fan clash
Sports.content:
Police end Krystian Bielik probe but FA charge Cardiff star after Portsmouth fan clash

Krystian Bielik has seen a police investigation into an alleged common assault dropped following an apology to the fan, but the Cardiff City player now faces an FA charge

View 2 Images Krystian Bielik clashed with a Portsmouth fan

Cardiff City star Krystian Bielik has been charged with misconduct by the FA after escaping any action from the police for his involvement in an incident with a Portsmouth fan.

‌



Bielik clashed with a Pompey supporter while going to collect the ball for a throw-in during a 2-0 defeat at Fratton Park on September 5. Footage which went viral on social media appeared to show the 28-year-old grabbing the youngster, who had slapped him, by the throat.

‌



The fan was ejected from the stadium following the incident midway through the second half and play was briefly halted by the referee, who did not take action against Bielik.

‌



Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary later launched an investigation into an alleged common assault. But an apology from the former Arsenal defender has seen the case dropped.

A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesperson said: "Following an incident involving a Portsmouth FC supporter and a Cardiff player at Fratton Park on 5 September 2026, we have now concluded our investigation.

‌



"After speaking with the complainant and reviewing all available evidence, the matter has been resolved by way of an out-of-court disposal, agreed by all parties involved.

"As part of this resolution, an apology has been provided by the player. The matter is now considered closed, and no further action will be taken in relation to this incident."

View 2 Images The supporter appeared to gesture that he was grabbed around the throat by Krystian Bielik

‌



However, the ex-Poland international is not in the clear over the incident, with the FA now charging him with misconduct following the conclusion of the police's investigation.

The FA said in a statement: "Cardiff City's Krystian Bielik has been charged with misconduct following the EFL Championship game against Portsmouth on 5 September. It's alleged that the player acted in an improper manner around the 71st minute of the match.

"Krystian Bielik has until 25 September to provide a response."

Article continues below

In a statement at the time, Cardiff said: "We are satisfied with the way that match officials dealt with the situation during the game, having been in full view of it. Player protection will always be of paramount importance to us."

Bielik joined the Bluebirds in the summer transfer window from West Brom and has made six appearances for Brian Barry-Murphy's side. Cardiff have made a slow start to their Championship campaign and sit 21st in the table, with just one win from the opening eight games.

Benjamin Sesko row erupts as Premier League star hits out at Man Utd legends

Benjamin Sesko has withdrawn from the Slovenia squad for the international break with a shin injury, with Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt questioning the seriousness of the issue

View Image Benjamin Sesko's Slovenia team-mate Jaka Bijol has come out in his defence

Benjamin Sesko has been backed by Slovenia colleague Jaka Bijol after Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt cast doubt over the legitimacy of the Manchester United striker's injury. Sesko missed Saturday's clash with Fulham due to shin discomfort.

‌



Michael Carrick later confirmed the forward was managing the problem and would be monitored. United then revealed on Monday night that Sesko had pulled out of Slovenia’s squad for the international break.

‌



A club statement confirmed: "Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan."

‌



Despite that announcement, Scholes and Butt raised doubts about how serious the injury actually was. The former United midfielders also took aim at Carrick's deployment of Matheus Cunha, suggesting the Brazilian is far less influential when used as a false nine, the role he occupied against Fulham.

Sports.title: Christian Eriksen cancels Wolfsburg contract three months after collapsing on pitch
Sports.content:
Christian Eriksen cancels Wolfsburg contract three months after collapsing on pitch

Former Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester United midfielder Christian Eriksen was involved in another terrifying incident when he collapsed on the pitch when in action for Denmark

View 2 Images Eriksen has left Wolfsburg (Image: Getty Images)

Christian Eriksen has had his Wolfsburg contract cancelled at his own request just months after another concerning collapse. The Danish midfielder was in action for his nation Denmark back in June when he collapsed to the floor.

‌



He fell midway through the second half against Ukraine and was transferred to hospital, with the game itself being cancelled.

‌



The scenes were reminiscent to those of his major scare during Euro 2020 where he suffered a cardiac arrest. Eriksen was fitted with a defibrillator in the aftermath but Serie A rules prevented him from playing with Inter Milan at the time.

‌



He resumed his career with Brentford and Manchester United before moving to Wolfsburg. But following Eriksen’s latest incident, the German club have announced that he will be departing despite initially having confirmed he will continue his footballing career.

“For us, it was clear that the decision about his future had to be Christian’s. We wanted to give him that freedom in this particular situation and have now agreed to his request to terminate the contract,” Wolfsburg manager director of sport Dieter Hecking said.

“He has already experienced and achieved a great deal during his extraordinary career. That makes it all the more remarkable how approachable and down-to-earth we came to know him at VfL.

"Despite his short time here, he has left a lasting impression on his teammates, our staff and the fans. We would like to thank Christian and wish him and his family all the very best.”

‌



Eriksen said: “At the moment, it is important for me to be close to my family in Denmark. I’m pleased that we were able to find a solution together. My time in Wolfsburg was marked by many highs and lows.

Eriksen only joined Wolfsburg last summer after departing Manchester United. He made 34 appearances across all competitions across his solitary season, scoring three times and providing ten assists. But that was not enough to prevent the club from dropping into the second tier of German football.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker blacklisted FIFA after their 'uncomfortable' Vladimir Putin request
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker blacklisted FIFA after their 'uncomfortable' Vladimir Putin request

Gary Lineker no longer works with world football's governing body after he was forced to escape a meeting with the President of Russia

View 3 Images Gary Lineker has made a conscious decision not to work with FIFA anymore (Image: The Rest Is Football.)

Gary Lineker has explained why he deliberately stepped away from working with FIFA after an awkward encounter threatened to put him in an uncomfortable position. The former Match of the Day presenter was one of the public faces of the 2018 World Cup draw in Russia, a high-profile event that brought him into contact with some of the biggest names in football.

‌



But away from the cameras, Lineker was also expected to meet Russian president Vladimir Putin. He didn't want to go through with the meeting and instead used his workload as an excuse to avoid it.

‌



The experience promoted a rethink about his relationship with world football's governing body, with the former England striker deciding that keeping his distance from FIFA was preferable given his role in the media.

‌



Speaking on The Rest Is Football podcast, Lineker revealed: "I made the decision quite a few years ago to not be associated with FIFA in any way, deliberately, particularly with going into the fact that I'm in the media.

Gary Lineker claims Premier League transfer could cost Arsenal Champions League READ MORE :

"And, sometimes, whether it was when I worked for the BBC or even now doing this show, I think it's better if you're not influenced from the inside. So I've kept my distance deliberately, I would say, probably since the turn of this decade. It was a deliberate ploy.

‌



"Having done the World Cup draw for them in 2018... and I remember they wanted me to meet Vladimir Putin and I thought, 'I don't want to do that.' And I just told them, 'I'm sorry, I've got so much to do with the script. I'm trying to get it all ready.'

"And then I felt it was a slightly uncomfortable position. And I thought, going down the line, that it's probably better to distance myself."

Lineker wasn't the only famous football figure at the event asked to come face-to-face with Putin. Pele, Diego Maradona, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho and Lothar Matthaus all took the opportunity to pose for photographs with the Russian president during the draw.

‌



View 3 Images Lineker hosting the 2018 World Cup draw (Image: Getty)

The former Leicester, Tottenham and Everton striker did, however, meet FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who has since come under significant pressure following his aborted attempt to sell a portion of the World Cup's commercial rights.

Lineker has also questioned the length of time FIFA presidents are able to remain in office. Infantino has held the position since 2016 and is seeking another term when the next election takes place next year.

‌



He said: "It's ludicrous that someone can be a consistent president of FIFA. I think it needs to be a little bit like maybe American presidents. I think you can serve one term.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino and Vladimir Putin with Diego Maradona at the draw for the 2018 World Cup (Image: Getty)

"It should be just a thing that goes around. I think maybe one term, one World Cup or even two, but no more than that just because otherwise you provoke this sort of behaviour if you get some kind of rogue guy at the top who loses his sense of decency."

Article continues below

Lineker also suggested Infantino would receive a hostile reception should he attend a football match in the UK, claiming: "I think there would be a crescendo of boos, yeah, at the very least. And a few songs. Definitely a few songs that might end in the word 'w*****.'"

He went on to criticise the way power is concentrated around the FIFA presidency, arguing that the organisation needs to move away from what he described as the "oligarchic manner of the president is all powerful," adding: "They basically last as long as they like, because, once they’re in, they can promise every federation so much money."

Sports.title: Eric Cantona teams up with Gary Lineker as Man Utd chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe slammed again
Sports.content:
Eric Cantona teams up with Gary Lineker as Man Utd chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe slammed again

Gary Lineker and Eric Cantona have both slammed Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe over recent days, following his latest comments bemoaning immigration

View 2 Images Eric Cantona and Sir Jim Ratcliffe's politics do not align (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Eric Cantona has joined Gary Lineker in calling out Sir Jim Ratcliffe after the Manchester United co-owner said: "Nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem". The four-time Premier League winner even claims he would not have moved to Old Trafford from Leeds United in 1992 had Ratcliffe been a minority shareholder at the time.

‌



Cantona, 60, is the INEOS founder's favourite player. Ratcliffe, 73, even named the company he established to acquire a 25% stake in United, Trawlers Limited.

‌



It is a reference to Cantona's famous quote: "When the seagulls follow the trawler, it's because they think sardines will be thrown into the sea."

‌

However, the admiration is very much one-sided due to their differing politics. After being asked by well-known United fan Pete Boyle in a video shared on TikTok whether he would have been willing to sign for a club part-owned by Ratcliffe, Cantona said: "No."

After being encouraged to expand on his blunt response to the hypothetical question posed, the interviewee went on to add: "Of course not.

‌



"You know what I think about all of this, with this kind of politics. I cannot understand how someone like this can say something like that when he's one of the club's owners."

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe is not popular with his favourite player Eric Cantona (Image: Bo Amstrup/EPA/Shutterstock)

Cantona continued: "Football is a very popular sport. Football is made - all the greatest players come from different waves of immigration. Everywhere, in France, in England, everywhere.

‌



"In France, for instance, the greatest players all come from different waves of immigration. I made a documentary on that, French Football: An Immigrant History.

"Raymond Kopa, in the fifties, was the son of Polish immigrants who came to France, worked in France, and worked hard in France. And then the Italians, Italians like Platini. And then the Spanish, like me, my mother came from Spanish refugees. I cannot accept this kind of thing."

‌



These comments come days after Lineker branded Ratcliffe a 'not particularly pleasant human being' who is 'even worse than the Glazers'.

He said on The Rest is Football podcast : "I must congratulate the Glazers on finding someone even worse than them that they can blame and getting him in there and getting all the stick: Jim Ratcliffe.

"He's clearly... I don't think he's a particularly pleasant human being, and it's a bit of a shambles of a football club the way it's being run at the moment. So, well done to the Glazers on that one, deflecting everything away from them!"

Sports.title: Arsenal discover penalty error as Premier League panel unanimously agree
Sports.content:
Arsenal discover penalty error as Premier League panel unanimously agree

Arsenal beat Sunderland in the Premier League earlier this month but were on the receiving end of a controversial penalty decision

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta was furious after the penalty was awarded against Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The Premier League's Key Match Incidents panel has ruled it was an incorrect on-pitch decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal earlier this month. The Gunners secured all three points against the Black Cats with a 2-0 victory at the Stadium of Light, with plenty of controversy during the game.

‌



Sunderland were awarded a penalty after Ezri Konsa was judged to have fouled Dan Ballard during a corner, with referee John Brooks pointing to the spot and the decision was checked and upheld by VAR. Enzo Le Fee went on to miss the penalty, with David Raya saving the spot-kick, and Arsenal opened the scoring a few minutes later with a long-range effort from Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



Mikel Arteta was furious with the decision, despite Sunderland missing the penalty, and it has now been the subject of a review from the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel. The panel agreed 5:0 in favour of the wrong decision being made to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal.

‌



However, there was a 3:2 split in favour of there not being enough evidence that supported VAR intervening to overrule the original decision made by the referee. The independent panel is made up of three former players or coaches, one representative from the Premier League, and one from Pro Ref (Professional Game Referees).

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



A statement on the decision read: “The panel unanimously felt that the referee's call of a penalty for a holding offence was incorrect. Although it was a very untidy challenge in which Konsa initially had arms around Ballard, Ballard engages in a holding action, which pulls Konsa onto him, so they both fall to the floor.

“The non-VAR intervention was supported, 3:2, with the majority considering that the on-field decision was not a clear and obvious error, given the combined actions from both players.”

Arsenal’s second goal against Sunderland came from the penalty spot with a strike from Bukayo Saka, who was fouled by Reinildo in stoppage time.

‌



“The on-field award of a penalty was supported with an initial holding action by Reinildo followed by a genuine attempt to challenge for the ball - tripping Saka inside the penalty area,” the statement read.

View 2 Images Sunderland were awarded a penalty in controversial circumstances (Image: Getty Images)

Arteta expressed his anger about the decision to award Sunderland a penalty at the Stadium of Light, with the Arsenal boss labelling the decision as “unbelievable”.

‌



“Look, the first question that we have to discuss is, and this is not acceptable at this level, because it was a beautiful game of football, with two teams, with an atmosphere in this stadium, it was unbelievable,” Arteta told reporters after the game.

“With Sunderland they are so well organised, they are so good in so many phases, they have great players, they create a lot of issues. We have to cope with all of that, because it was a lot in a really difficult week, after Chelsea and Napoli.

“And on top of that, we have to go through what we've done today, that in my opinion is not acceptable. And I watched it 20 times, and I cannot find a way to understand how we even think to give a penalty in that situation, or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don't know what to think, really.”

Sports.title: Does Littler need to change approach to hostile crowds?
Sports.content:
Following Luke Littler's latest run-in with a hostile crowd over the weekend, the Sky Sports Love The Darts Podcast has debated whether it is time for the world champion to change his approach.

Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jonny Clayton ended Luke Littler's clean sweep at the World Series of Darts Finals. Credit: @OfficialPDC.

"It's a real difficult situation," Smith said. "I can't speak for Luke because I'm not him and I wasn't in his position, I wasn't on stage at the time. I didn't really experience the whistling too much. I try not to rise to it because I know you're just going to get more stick.

"My manager once said to me, if you look at Michael van Gerwen, he never reacts, not once will he ever react to the crowd. He'll always thank them and he never really gets too much stick and he's very professional about how he does things. So, I admire him for that and I try and learn off of other people.

"I had a bit with Kevin Doets, obviously the crowd, rightly so, they're cheering their local guy on. Same with Gian [van Veen], they're doing exactly the same, but I think if you're aggressive towards the crowd and you're letting them know that it's affecting you and you're making them unhappy, it's not a good thing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Ross Smith feels he is ready to play in the Premier League.

"I tried to, with Gian, I had more banter with them, you know what I mean? Just like thumbs up to them, but smiling, not in an aggressive way and they sort of laugh with you, it's not a problem.

"I think it's how you can react on stage, if you're aggressive towards them, it's going to create problems for you. But like I said, I can't really comment on Luke because I wasn't playing in the games with Luke and I don't know what he actually went through, but they can be brutal at times."

Nicholson: Maybe Littler can learn from others

Former world championship quarter-finalist Paul Nicholson praised Smith's approach, and suggested that Littler could benefit from learning from some of his rivals.

Nicholson, who himself was known for often having fractious interactions with crowds, also pointed to the way 2021 world champion Gerwyn Price has adapted his behaviour on stage.

Following on from Smith's comments, Nicholson said: "That's a really, really good way of looking at it, what Ross has just said, because from my standpoint, I tried to be aggressive because I wanted to be different and it was something that I had my entire career for, more than 10 years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Paul Nicholson has backed Luke Littler's reduced schedule for the rest of the season.

"Gerwyn Price has taken years to figure it out. Now he gives the smile with the aggression, and the crowd are with him more than they ever have been.

"So, it just goes to show that Ross is looking at this right, in order to make sure that his career is in the right place moving forward.

"So, we learn from mistakes, but we actually learn from what other people are going through as well. We don't want to see Littler not going to events, but maybe he can learn from what other people are doing as well."

What could the rest of Littler's year look like? World Grand Prix* (Leicester) Sept 28-Oct 4 European Championship* (Dortmund) October 22-25 Players Championship 31 (Den Bosch) October 28 Players Championship 32 (Den Bosch) October 29 Players Championship 33 (Leicester) November 4 Players Championship 34 (Leicester) November 5 Grand Slam of Darts* (Wolverhampton) November 14-22 Players Championship Finals* (Minehead) November 27-29 *denotes major

Why whistling is worse than booing for players

Nicholson also explained why Littler and other players may become particularly frustrated at being whistled.

He added: "We have seen Littler have some banter with the crowd, which we're all for by the way, because we want people to have that connection. One of the greatest things about this sport is that there is a connection between the fans and the stars.

"But what we have at the minute is a trend of people using whistling as a way to make themselves feel heard. Dart players don't like it because it's piercing. It gets in your ear and it happens in a very short, sharp way, and it comes from nowhere.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Webster and Michael Bridge discuss Luke Littler's concerns over crowd whistling at the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam, the potential impact on his future and whether more can be done to tackle the issue.

"You don't know if it's going to come when you're throwing a match dart, a leg dart, or even going for a treble. If it comes out of nowhere, it can put you off and your shoulder jolts, and you don't want that.

"A boo is a lesser frequency and it's more mundane, you can handle them a lot better. But these short, sharp whistles, which is what they are, they're horrible.

"And the worst thing is, if it happens once, you are thinking about whether it's going to happen again, and you can't fully focus."

Sports.title: Sky Sports to show England men's tour of South Africa this winter
Sports.content:
Sky Sports and Cricket South Africa have extended their longstanding partnership, with Sky Sports and NOW to exclusively broadcast the England men's three-Test and three-ODI tour of South Africa this winter.

England's three-Test series against South Africa will take place across December and January, marking England's first Test tour of South Africa in seven years.

The series follows England's first-ever home Test series whitewash of Pakistan and will be Stephen Fleming's first series in charge as England men's Test head coach.

The Test series will be followed by three ODIs in January, as England prepare for the ICC Men's World Cup 2027, which will take place across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia in October and November next year.

Sky Sports will broadcast live coverage of a packed schedule of international cricket from South Africa, with Australia men's tour getting under way this Thursday with the first of three ODIs in Durban, followed by three Tests.

The schedule will then continue with tours involving Bangladesh, India Women and Australia Women through to April.

Sky Sports has broadcast cricket from South Africa for more than three decades, including live coverage of every England men's Test series in the country during that period.

The agreement further strengthens Sky Sports' position as the home of cricket, broadcasting all home England men's and women's international and domestic cricket, with the men's Ashes on home soil next summer set to be a major highlight.

Sports.title: Hamilton defends Ferrari amid ‘doom and gloom’ criticism
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari's season can still rank as a "huge achievement" if they finish in the top three of the Drivers' Championship, asking critics to "look at the positives" of the team's year despite recent setbacks.

Hamilton and Ferrari's hopes of winning this years world title have faded in recent races, with the Briton not finishing on the podium since the British Grand Prix at the start of July.

A first race retirement of the season last time out in Madrid saw third-placed Hamilton fall over 100 points back on championship-leading Kimi Antonelli for the first time this season, with the seven-time champion all-but conceding the title.

Antonelli's overall lead at the top of the standings is 81 points over Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

Asked about his own championship prospects heading into weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the season's 15th of a scheduled 23 rounds, Hamilton said: "Well, I mean, he's 101 points ahead of me.

"Just in two races he gained something like 40-odd points on me, and we've been working so hard to gain just a couple of points here and there.

"There is still a long way to go and I think the focus for me is, if we can hold on to second - if not somehow catch Mercedes - for the constructors', I think that would be remarkable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater breaks down the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, including why the race takes place on a Saturday, while doing his best Craig David impression!

"I think it's also just having to think about where we were last year and where we've come to this year and whilst it sometimes seems doom and gloom, you actually have to look at the positives."

Ferrari endured a winless 2025 campaign and slipped to fourth in the Constructors' Championship, with Hamilton himself experiencing a difficult first campaign in red with no podiums for the first time in his career.

But he won for the first time at June's Spanish Grand Prix, with Charles Leclerc triumphing two races later at Silverstone.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton celebrated his first Ferrari victory in style after winning the Barcelona-Catalunya GP, throwing his trophy into the air before the champagne spray began.

Hamilton added: "We've been fighting, we've had wins and podiums, the team have done an incredible job in terms of bringing upgrades, so you really have to acknowledge the good things that we've done this year.

"I know lots of people focus on the negatives. For me, again, if I can battle with George and somehow get ahead of him, which would be very difficult as Mercedes are the leaders... if at the end of the year, managing to stay in the top three, even second, I think would be a huge achievement for us as a team."

Hamilton is 20 points behind Russell, his former Mercedes team-mate, in the standings.

'I believe we can make improvements'

Ferrari have consistently looked competitive early on in race weekends but the team's recent results have often been compromised by operational and strategic issues within their own control.

"I think there's positives to take out of the last few races, it's just they haven't been, I would say, the best in terms of execution and we've not had the best results," said Hamilton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was forced to retire early at the Spanish Grand Prix.

"But the positives we take forwards and we try and learn from the areas we weren't as good. I believe we can make improvements and I think we have.

"I'm excited for this weekend."

Russell: I feel confident I can fight for victories again

The Spanish Grand Prix a fortnight ago also saw Russell fall a season-high margin behind Antonelli, who has won the last two grands prix to take his tally to eight overall in an extraordinary second campaign of F1 so far.

Russell, the pre-season title favourite, has spoken openly about his difficulties in meshing his natural driving style to the all-new 2026 cars but believes the situation is improving, saying in Baku on Wednesday that "I've been making very good progress and feel confident I can fight for victories again".

He underlined the importance of continuing that trend all through the rest of this season ahead relatively stable winter of regulations into 2027.

"I think it is very important to try and resolve some issues, which, as I mentioned before, I think I've been pleased with that progress since the summer break," said Russell.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player F1 drivers share their opinions following the announcement that the Monaco Grand Prix will get a Sprint race next year.

"The race pace, which was a weakness, has been substantially better and has been in the mix every single race since the break.

"And I now feel more comfortable that I can fight for great results.

"Let's see from now until the end of the season how the points could fall out. But next year is going to be pretty similar. Not much has changed with the chassis, not much has changed with the power units. Maybe the tyres are going to be slightly different from what we hear. So, it's important I continue to build."

Although he has effectively ruled himself out of title contention, Russell says his approach to each race weekend will not change.

"I'm going to keep fighting every single race until it's mathematically impossible," he stressed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli says the team has all eyes on its long-awaited upgrade package arriving in Malaysia

"But it doesn't change how I go about my job. I want to try and win every single race and put it on pole every single race. That's my goal.

"That's what I'm working towards every single weekend, and what happens thereafter will be. And there's obviously a huge deficit, but it's not even really a consideration right now. It's just the performance is the biggest priority."

Sports.title: Pirotton vows to be 'matador' against 'money cow' Fisher
Sports.content:
Michael Pirotton is ready to shock Johnny Fisher when they fight at London’s Copper Box Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

The "Romford Bull" is hugely popular with an impassioned fan base, while his Belgian opponent is comparatively unknown.

But Pirotton is convinced he can use that element of surprise.

"I'm nobody in boxing," the Belgian told Sky Sports. "Nobody knows about me.

"That's my only advantage," he continued. "I know I'm supposed to lose.

"In the scenario I'm supposed to lose that fight. He's going to come full of confidence with his people and I know he's training hard. I have to be ready for whatever he brings. I'm going to be ready. I'm ready."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher looks ahead to his fight against Michael Pirotton and praise his support network that has carried him this far

Fisher is a strong, come-forward fighter. "He's really aggressive and I can move. It's a classic heavyweight match-up. A bull against a matador. Let's see who wins," Pirotton said. "The horns in my belly, or if he ends up on the barbecue.

"The pressure is on his shoulders," the Belgian added. "He's just the money cow. He didn't grab anything he had. I know whatever happens I've grabbed everything I have."

He maintains the struggles he's faced in his career will help him outlast Fisher.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Pirotton discusses why he feels more ready than ever to take on Johnny Fisher and discusses what he'll need to do to take the win

"They will find out. I don't brag before," Pirotton said. "But I'm confident. I don't brag before, I dance after, that's what I do.

"I'm glad for everything, that tough journey with some bad stuff happening to me. Because it enfused a deep sense of stoicism in me. What happens is going to happen and I'm still going to be Mike and I'm still going to be proud of what I do.

"I don't have a destination. I just have a path and I'm walking. I'm bleeding now but I keep walking and you're going to see."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher faces off with his opponent Michael Pirotton ahead of their heavyweight clash at the Copper Box on Saturday - live on Sky Sports

Pirotton, who's never been dropped or stopped in his career, does have a warning for Fisher.

"I'm not over and it's not over until I say it's over and Johnny … he's a tough guy, he's strong guy, he's a decent guy, but he can't knock me out," he said.

"I'm able to punch. But I've never been able to punch like I'm really able to punch. And now I feel free to unleash my power."

Watch Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: F1 drivers split over whether Monaco Sprint 'makes sense'
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton and George Russell disagree on the Monaco Grand Prix becoming a Sprint weekend in 2027.

Last week, Formula 1 announced its 2027 calendar and revealed there will be an increase in the number of Sprint events from six to 10, with Monaco holding the alternative format that sees an extra qualifying session on Friday before a 100km Sprint on Saturday.

Monaco is one of the most difficult tracks to overtake at, but F1 highlighted the prospect of two qualifying sessions as an additional chance for "the drivers to show their world-class skill and precision on the narrow streets of Monte Carlo".

"It makes no sense to me but I'm not making the decisions obviously," said Hamilton, who is hoping to fight for the win at this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"On the positive, we get another qualifying session, which is quite cool. But I've always said that Monaco needs something different. I don't think it should be the same race formula that's everywhere else. It needs to be something different.

"We've already included the Sprints, which I think have really brought something new to the sport. But I think we've got to come up with something new for somewhere like that because it's a beautiful place, such a beautiful country, an incredible circuit to drive, but the race is as dull as it gets. I don't know what that is, but a Sprint race is not the answer for it I would say."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater explains why Monaco has been chosen as a Sprint venue for the 2027 F1 season

However, Hamilton's former Mercedes team-mate Russell gave a contrary view when speaking earlier in the FIA press conference in Baku.

"I personally think it's good because we've had Sprints for quite a while, normal race weekends feel quite long-winded and we all want to fight," said Russell.

"As much fun as driving a Formula 1 car around the track is, the enjoyment comes from the competition and that adrenaline you get from a qualifying session.

"Of course the race isn't going to be the most exciting one, but that will be compensated by having a more exciting Friday. Sprint Qualifying is way more exciting than FP2, so I think on the whole it makes sense."

Max Verstappen has been a strong critic of Sprint weekends in the past, stating in 2023 that he "won't be around for too long" if F1 added more to the calendar.

Verstappen has been less vocal in recent years and says he's made his feelings clear to F1 boss Stefano Domenicali.

He said: "Maybe Monaco wanted it [the Sprint], I don't know. For me, I honestly don't care where the Sprints are. I participate, and of course you try to do the best you can.

"I have no emotion attached to winning a Sprint race or not winning it. My focus is always from, when I was a kid, you look forward to the Grand Prix."

"Monaco, I think you just make it a little bit more variable, to be honest. I think it was just a Saturday event in the last few years. Whatever happened on Saturday was basically done," he added.

"I think right now it can mix things around a little bit more. I think it's going to be an interesting weekend. I'm definitely looking forward to it."

Sports.title: Rising cruiserweight talent Roehrig signs with Zuffa Boxing
Sports.content:
Lucas Roehrig has signed a promotional deal with Zuffa Boxing and will fight on Sky Sports.

The cruiserweight talent, only 23 years old, has impressed in his rise through the cruiserweight ranks.

He will fight next on Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena on November 7, live on Sky Sports.

His trainer and mentor is former world champion George Groves. Roehrig has been flawless so far in his professional career.

The young Londoner has won nine fights, never been defeated and has taken five of those wins inside the distance.

Roehrig made his pro debut in 2024, halting former English champion Joel McIntyre in three rounds.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Groves discusses his fighter Lucas Roehrig signing for Zuffa boxing and why we should be excited for his career.

Last year he shut out American prospect Brian Jones over six rounds. From then on, he's continued to box and beat opponents with winning records.

His last two fights have been consecutive stoppage victories, over Adam Kolarik and Faton Tolaj, at York Hall.

"I'm really excited. This is a new chapter for me," Roehrig told Sky Sports News. "Zuffa have come onto the scene and made a big splash, and for where I'm at in my career right now, that's exactly what I want to do too.

"I've been through the levels. I've boxed on Sky shows and on other channels, but I've also boxed on the small hall shows - I haven't skipped a step.

"I think now is the perfect platform, perfect time to fight other prospects - Zuffa have a lot of other undefeated fighters - for me to really make some noise not just in the UK but internationally too."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Groves' boxing protégé Lucas Roehrig picks up the knockout win! But was the first knockdown controversial?

Roehrig is now joining a promotional powerhouse that has a strong cruiserweight stable, including Jai Opetaia, Chris Billam-Smith, Ryan Rozicki and more.

"I've said numerous times that I'm aiming for world titles, that's the main goal, that's why I work so hard and that's why we're going to be taking risks," Roehrig said.

"Our first fight will be November 7. Make a splash, and then from there keep building. There's other belts that I'd love to collect along the way, but the Zuffa belt and the world titles are the end goal."

Zuffa Boxing 11, headlined by Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton, takes place this Saturday live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: 'Scotland was always the one for me' - Binks' pride at first call-up
Sports.content:
"I've wanted to play for Scotland for years, and now the opportunity has come. I'm just really proud."

Defender Luis Binks has played at under-21 level for both Scotland and England, but insisted he did not hesitate when new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli said he wanted him in his first squad.

The Brondby captain is one of six players handed their first full call-ups for the Nations League games against Slovenia, North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Pocognoli has said he will not beg players to choose Scotland, something the 25-year-old agrees with.

"I think if he had to try and convince me, convince anyone, it's probably not the right thing for the player," Binks told Sky Sports News.

"I didn't need any convincing; I was available.

"I wanted to play for Scotland. I've wanted to play for Scotland for years and now the opportunity has come, I'm just really proud.

Image: Robbie Ure (L) and Luis Binks are two of the new faces in the Scotland squad

"It's where you feel your heart is and where you want to go. This was the route I wanted to take."

It is a new-look Scotland under Pocognoli with 12 players who were in Steve Clarke's final squad for the World Cup missing out, only Scott McTominay, Lawrence Shankland and Che Adams through injury.

And while it's a new environment for Binks, there are some familiar faces within the camp.

"It was a few years ago that I was with Aaron Hickey in Bologna and he got called up while we were there.

Image: Aaron Hickey has 22 caps for Scotland

"I could play for the 21s at the time and nothing ever coming up but it was always, Scotland was always the one for me that I wanted to go and play for.

"Going back years ago, under 16s when I went away with Scotland, the vibe was just so good.

"It felt like a proper team, it was just normal lads and you felt like you were playing with your mates so I knew there was always that feeling around it. I wanted to go and be a part of that again."

The Pocognoli era officially gets underway in Ljubljana on Saturday, with a game against Switzerland at Hampden Park three days later.

The squad then fly to North Macedonia on October 3 before returning to Glasgow to face Slovenia again on October 6.

Image: The Scotland players are training in La Manga ahead of their Nations League opener

Scotland were demoted from Nations League A after a play-off defeat by Greece last year and return to the second tier for this year's competition.

"Obviously we want to get to the A group of the Nations League but there are a lot of new faces, a lot of new management, new ways of playing," Binks added.

"I know what it's like because I've got a new manager at my club now and it's taking a bit of time so I imagine it's the same sort of process here.

"It's just about getting the players on board and buying into everything the manager wants to do.

"It's been early days, but I think everyone is fully on board and believes in what we can do as a country."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo vows to play on for Portugal and targets 1,000 career goals
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo said he considered quitting international football after the World Cup, but confirmed he plans to play on for Portugal and hopes to reach 1,000 goals for club and country. Ronaldo, who is 21 goals shy of the milestone, accepted some critics are trying to “kill” him but is determined to carry on.

Ronaldo, who has won 233 caps for his country, captained Portugal in the summer at the World Cup, where they exited to Spain in the last 16. Asked if he considered walking away from international duty, he replied: “Yes, I did. Of course, I’m always thinking about my decisions, my future, the present also. I’m a thinker; you have to think. This is why you see me here now, it means I will continue.

“I had a conversation with our president [Pedro Proenca], with our coach. I still believe that I’m able to help the national team to reach what they want. I think I can give the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football. There is a new young generation, but for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.

“Whenever they say they don’t want me in the national team, I will be the first one to go. When I think I am not adding anything to the team, or that I create an atmosphere, I will be the first to go. I will take my suitcase and leave. The Portuguese count on me. That’s why I’m still here … Just look at the numbers, I’m sure you can make some calculations, I’m still doing well. The day they don’t count on me, no problemo, I will leave. I will always be the No 1 fan of this federation.”

Jorge Jesus, the Portugal head coach who managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, said the 41-year-old would start in his first game in charge, against Wales in the Nations League on Thursday. Jesus, who has succeeded Roberto Martínez, also launched a passionate defence of Ronaldo, drawing applause from many in attendance at Portugal’s City of Football complex in Lisbon.

“Cristiano is a symbol of Portugal and the national team,” said Jesus, sitting alongside Ronaldo at the Portugal federation’s campus. “If he will play the games, he is not entitled to that, it is up to the manager to decide.”

Ronaldo cut a relaxed figure on stage alongside Jesus. “For me the most important thing is I know what I am,” he said. “I know what I do to be here, I know what I have done to have the success that I have had. I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired … in 10 years.

“I’m happy with myself. It doesn’t matter if I play tomorrow, if I’m rested for the next game, for me the most important thing is that I feel good. The people around me, they trust in my work. Focus on the people who love Cristiano, not the people who criticise me, so I am a happy person.”

Asked directly about the criticism, Ronaldo triggered laughter from many in the room by replying: “I cannot be 100% honest, sometimes I have to be politically correct.” He added: “I do understand that some TV channels like to criticise me, they’ve tried to kill me – with a shotgun – but I can still move away from it. Anyway, I am used to it. I have been doing this for more than 20 years, I’m quite used to it. What I can control, I will. What I can’t, I won’t.”

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo attends a training session before the Nations League group stage match against Wales. Photograph: Rodrigo Antunes/EPA

On Thursday Ronaldo will return to José Alvalade Stadium, where he began his career with Sporting, before joining Manchester United in 2003. It is Portugal’s first game in Lisbon since beating Ireland in a World Cup qualifier last October.

“It’s a special feeling because it was there where my beautiful history started,” Ronaldo said. “I’m very proud about that, to play for the national team after so many years, playing where I practically was opened to the world … It was a beautiful moment.

“It is always a pleasure to play for the national team, to wear the colours of Portugal. After so many years, it is [still always] like the first time. I will step on to the pitch with passion, emotion. I hope we can get off on the right foot. Because it’s at Sporting, it does feel a bit more special.

“It would be the cherry on the top of the cake to score my 1,000th goal with the national team. It would be the culmination of a beautiful story. I said I wanted to reach that target and I will reach that target. But I don’t have an obsession. If you are obsessed with something, you won’t get it … Just enjoy. Carpe diem, enjoy the day.”

Sports.title: Manchester United report seventh straight annual loss and sell fans £125 grass clumps
Sports.content:
Manchester United have reported an annual loss for the seventh successive year, taking the club’s combined losses to £444m since 2019.

The financial results were released as it emerged United are raising revenue by selling small clumps of grass from the Old Trafford pitch to fans. United relaid the playing surface for the first time in 14 years this summer, and an email to fans has offered them the chance to buy 7cm x 7cm clumps of turf for £125.

The £43m pre-tax loss for 2025-26 is a significant increase on the £33m for the previous 12 months, with compensation paid to the sacked manager Ruben Amorim a contributory factor along with the decision to increase the club’s borrowing facility by £93m to help fund the redevelopment of Old Trafford.

United’s continued losses come despite record revenue of £677.6m – up 1.7% on the previous 12 months – and the implementation of a major cost-cutting regime by Sir Jim Ratcliffe under which hundreds of staff have lost their jobs.

In discussing United’s results on an investor call the chief executive, Omar Berrada, said the club’s summer transfer window, during which they spent £155m on three players, had been planned with “financial sustainability in mind” in an indication that the budget will continue to be tight for the manager, Michael Carrick.

That is underlined by the fact that United’s wage-bill dropped to £301m, down 3.6% on the previous year, more than £100m lower than Manchester City’s.

While United reported operating profits of £22.6m for the 12 months to 30 June 2026 the increase in revenue was more than offset by the cost of financing the club. Net finance costs more than tripled to £69.2m from £21.2m in the previous year, partly owing to foreign-exchange movements, and the club refinanced several loans, increasing their net debt from £471.9m to £577.6m.

United sources have said the refinancing provided funding for the £63.5m purchase of a plot of land next to Old Trafford required to build their proposed new 100,000 capacity stadium, the first major investment in a complex project that could end up costing more than £2bn.

Berrada said the results demonstrated “the underlying strength of our business, particularly in a season without European football” and said: “This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years. It also proves Manchester United’s enduring popularity and commercial strength. While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable.”

United are confident their financial outlook will improve over the next 12 months owing to the club’s return to the Champions League and the start of increased sponsorship deals with the training-kit partner Betway and shirt-sleeve partner SumUp, which will bring in £20m and £22m a year respectively. The club is forecasting revenue of between £740m and £760m for 2026-27.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Madrid, Mourinho and the fight for neutrality in row with Javier Tebas
Sports.content:
A LIGA OF ITS OWN

While football managers moaning about referees to deflect from their own teams’ shortcomings is nothing new, few do performative, wounded, righteous indignation with quite the same brooding intensity and petulance as José Mourinho. It’s been more than two decades since his moaning preceded a pile-on from angry fans whose threats forced the Swedish referee Anders Frisk into early retirement and in the interim, a steady stream of red cards, touchline bans and mournful post-match monologues have rendered his rap-sheet for badgering officialdom longer than a roll of Andrex toilet paper. On Sunday, Mourinho was at it again, following his 10-man Real Madrid side’s 2-1 defeat at the hands of their bitter city rivals Atlético. He arrived at his post-match presser armed with a sheet of A4 featuring screen-grabs of two tackles made by Atlético players that he felt should have resulted in red cards. “We can save ourselves the bother of the press conference because the story is right here,” he harrumphed, waving his piece of paper in front of assembled hacks before embarking on a paranoid tirade about Spanish match officials continuing to have it in for the put-upon, plucky underdogs of Real Madrid.

Luckily for daily football emails tasked with providing mildly amusing #content in the bleak and desolate early days of international breaks when nothing much is happening, the story didn’t end there. On Tuesday, the serially outspoken La Liga president Javier Tebas weighed in on Social Media Disgraces in response to an article in a Spanish publication called El Debate. In it, Tomás González-Martín suggested that, by failing to pander to the likes of Madrid, referees were damaging the league on whom they rely for a living, a league González-Martin claims has no value without Madrid. “Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy,” thundered Tebas. “But this article goes further: it claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’. What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.”

While Tebas was right to defend his officials against accusations of institutional bias when it comes to Real Madrid and to angrily rail against the notion that commercial considerations should be factored into their decision-making process, he almost certainly aimed his guns at the wrong target. By targeting an opinion piece written by a random hack rather than the comments made by Mourinho, he left himself open to accusations of partiality towards Madrid. Not that the club see it that way. “Our club considers it intolerable that the president of La Liga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid,” they moaned in an official statement. “Given this inappropriate and persistent behaviour, we believe that the professional football competition in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and realising its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality.” More specifically, a leader whose fundamental duty of neutrality is tilted in favour of Mourinho’s Madrid.

“You can always play the ​moralist, but I think everyone would say yes to that. I ​don’t want to ‌have to work ​any more after my ​career. I didn’t need to after City either, but now I can also set up future generations of my family well. If this choice means my grandchildren can also live comfortably, why wouldn’t I do it?” – Tijjani Reijnders makes the rare admission that he’s a footballer moving somewhere for the money, having joined Al Qadisah in Saudi Arabia from Manchester City on a deal worth a reported €100m over four years.
