Sports.title: "Free agent" Ocon talking to other teams with Haas yet to confirm F1 2027 line-up
Sports.content:
Esteban Ocon declared himself a "free agent" as Haas is yet to confirm its driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season, but did not rule out potentially staying at the team.

Although the Frenchman has been enjoying much improved performances of late, which have gone largely unrewarded as Haas' performance has slipped away from its early-season points-scoring form, Ocon's seat has been under threat for some time.

Haas has been using its testing of previous cars (TPC) programme to identify a potential partner for Oliver Bearman next season, with Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, reigning F2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli, and current reserve Ryo Hirakawa in the frame.

Ocon confirmed that he was looking for other options for 2027, while Haas continues to assess its driver pairing for next year.

Recent rumours have surfaced suggesting that the team is leaning towards Camara - currently the reigning F3 champion and second in this year's F2 standings - although team boss Ayao Komatsu stated during the Spanish GP that he had "maybe five" drivers in contention.

"Yes, at the moment I am definitely a free agent for next year," Ocon stated. "There are things in discussion that are out of my control and there are certain topics that are out of my control. So I will keep pushing until the end of the year and see how it goes."

Asked if staying at Haas was an option, Ocon remained tight-lipped and responded: "Let's see."

Esteban Ocon, Haas Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Ocon added that he was pleased with his performances of late, having suffered this season with an inconsistent car in the early stages of the season.

It is unclear if this is an aerodynamic sensitivity issue or a parts quality control problem; Komatsu has suggested both could be causes, and that the team is still investigating the issue at hand.

"We know it's been an ongoing issue," he said. "It's reassuring that I'm doing a good job. Obviously, my performance hasn't been an issue this year.

"I've performed every time I had the car. I've been the last one to score in Monaco. I was almost scoring in Madrid. There's been a lot of times where I've performed when the car was underperforming. It's been clear.

"Everybody in the team has been following that very closely, trying to fix the problem. We haven't been hiding from it. But it's been quite disappointing at times, obviously, to have these kind of problems."

Bearman was asked if he felt ready to step up as the team leader should Ocon depart, and the Briton stated that he'd learned a lot from his team-mate across the almost two years spent together as team-mates.

Esteban Ocon, Haas F1 Team, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

He pointed to Ocon's feedback in the engineering room as something that he'd taken inspiration from, along with his own improving performances on-track.

"I've been here for, well, this is my second year driving as a full-time driver, but also I've been one year as a reserve for Haas, also did a few races and FP1s the year before that, even in 2023, I did my first FP1. So I have a really good level of experience with the team," Bearman said.

"I feel like I've improved a lot in terms of my on-track performance, but also how I describe what I'm feeling in the car and things like that. And that's something I certainly learned a lot from someone who's very experienced like Esteban. So on that side, it's been really good learning for me.

"Even if I compare my feedback to 12 months ago, I'm not sure I would have the confidence to just rely on my own feedback. But I feel like I've made a good step in that regard, and it's just a normal learning process, really."

Sports.title: The initial plan for F1's next engine regulation in 2030
Sports.content:
Formula 1 stakeholders have reached an agreement on the main elements of the next engine rules cycle.

The FIA and F1 engine manufacturers have opted against a naturally aspirated option, partly because of noise restrictions at street circuits, with a smaller and simplified electronics package.

A push-to-pass overtake mode is also under consideration, along with a possible debut in 2030.

While discussions are still ongoing, the engine set to define the next technical cycle in F1 has largely taken shape. Meetings between the FIA and the manufacturers will continue to finalise the remaining details, but a substantial agreement has been reached on the key points with the focus on a simpler and lighter power unit, one that is considered closer to the traditional concept of a racing engine.

A return to V8 engines

F1 is set to move to 3.0-litre V8 architecture, but one of the issues that most divided the engine manufacturers was whether to retain the turbocharger.

The possibility of opting for a naturally aspirated engine was also on the table, a solution that would have delivered a sound particularly appealing to fans nostalgic for F1 in the early 2000s.

Fernando Alonso, Renault R25, leads Michael Schumacher, Ferrari F2005 Photo by: Motorsport Images

However, the turbocharger element will remain as part of the power unit configuration, but the reasons behind the decision go beyond purely technical considerations.

A naturally aspirated 3.0-litre V8 would have reached noise levels that would cause a major problem with some of the current F1 venues.

The issue concerns street circuits in particular: Melbourne, Miami, Madrid, Singapore, Baku and Las Vegas are venues where noise-emission restrictions are in place, and the arrival of cars significantly louder than the current generation could create major difficulties that would be impossible to overcome and potentially even put some events at risk.

This has led to the decision to retain a smaller turbocharger, a compromise that should still make it possible to achieve a considerably louder sound than that of the current power units, while keeping noise levels within limits applied at some F1 circuits.

Smaller electrical motor and lighter power units

The new V8 will not be completely detached from electrification either. The new rules look set to include a simplified 100kW electric motor, a considerably lower output than the 350kW current generation of power units.

The aim is to maintain a technological link with the automotive industry without replicating the complexity that has characterised the latest generation of power units. The direction emerging from the discussions is clear: electric power will remain part of F1, but with a less dominant role within the overall package.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

Another area where the lessons of recent years appear to have been taken on board concern the weight of the overall power unit. The target set for the new power unit is highly ambitious: to produce a complete unit weighing at least 50kg lighter than the current power units.

Push-to-pass and 2030 introduction being considered

Some aspects still need to be finalised. Among them is the system that will give drivers an additional power boost to assist overtaking manoeuvres.

There appears to be no intention to bring back the DRS used until the end of the 2025 season. The solution currently under consideration is closer to the push-to-pass philosophy adopted in IndyCar: a temporary increase in power that the driver could deploy under specific circumstances.

This will be one of the areas the FIA and the engine manufacturers still need to reach a definitive agreement on.

When the new regulations will be introduced in F1 also remains open, with the plan to debut the new rules in 2030 an option, which would bring forward the end of the current technical rules cycle that began by one year.

Reaching a decision will require all parties to find common ground, but the issues that have emerged with the current generation of power units have accelerated a broader discussion that goes beyond individual technical details. After pushing hard on technological complexity, F1 appears keen to return to a more traditional concept of a racing engine.

Sports.title: What would you like to ask Emerson Fittipaldi?

Sports.title: Hadjar to partner Verstappen at Red Bull for F1 2027
Sports.content:
Red Bull has confirmed it will field an unchanged Formula 1 driver line-up in 2027, with Isack Hadjar staying put alongside Max Verstappen.

Hadjar stepped up in 2026 after a rookie season at sister team Racing Bulls, and has impressed with his speed in what has historically been a difficult second Red Bull seat.

The Frenchman, who is making his return in Azerbaijan this weekend after missing three races through injury, will stay on board for another campaign in 2027 alongside Verstappen, who recently signed a contract extension to 2030.

"We’re very excited to continue our journey with Isack," said Red Bull team boss Laurent Mekies.

"Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.

"From the very beginning, Isack immersed himself in the team, spending every minute at the factory with his engineers to develop the car, always eager to learn and improve.

"You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat."

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Despite sitting out Zandvoort, Monza and Madrid, Hadjar still holds eighth in the standings, boosted by a first Red Bull podium in Monaco to complement his maiden podium in 2025, as well as a streak of seven consecutive top six finishes in what has largely been F1's third or fourth quickest car.

"I am really excited to continue with Oracle Red Bull Racing," the 21-year-old said. "There are so many talented people at the factory, and you’re aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I’ve been able to justify the faith they’ve had in me.

“I’m constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead."

Racing Bulls is yet to confirm its own driver line-up for 2027, with incumbents Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad having both impressed this season while the squad also has junior driver Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings.

Sports.title: What were Leclerc's "other opportunities" before signing new Ferrari deal?
Sports.content:
Every time Ferrari and Charles Leclerc agree to extend their relationship in Formula 1, the news comes against a background of allusions to other suitors Charles has spurned to remain with his true love.

"For that, I'm also lucky to be in the position where I've got my manager," he said on a recent episode of F1's Beyond the Grid podcast when asked how seriously he had considered a life away from Ferrari.

"And my manager is here to let me know about what are the other opportunities, what's going on around. And so I didn't have any personal talks, but my manager did.

"I mean, it's his job to be honest with me and to give me the full picture of what's going on in the paddock and what opportunities we might have. So, yes, there were other opportunities. But at the end of the day, we sat down with Ferrari and we made it happen quite quickly."

If Leclerc has a special relationship with Ferrari, the same can be said of his manager, Nicolas Todt: son of Jean, the former rally co-driver who masterminded Peugeot's rally and endurance programmes before leading Ferrari to world domination in the Michael Schumacher era, then shifted into politics as FIA president for over a decade. Todt Jr also managed long-time Ferrari driver Felipe Massa and still superintends the affairs of James Calado, a Le Mans winner with the Scuderia. He has a great many drivers on his books at all stages of the career ladder, and is a consummate player in the paddock.

But what Todt Jr enjoys to a greater extent at Ferrari than anywhere else is the ear of influential figures further up the food chain than the team principal – although he is a key ally of Fred Vasseur, having co-founded the ART GP organisation with him over two decades ago. Indeed, it's understood that Todt was instrumental in the removal of former team principal Mattia Binotto and his replacement by Vasseur in January 2023.

Nicolas Todt and Fred Vasseur Photo by: Getty Images

Having a manager so plugged into the senior echelons of power enables Leclerc to get what he wants with plausible deniability, such as Binotto's departure at a time when Ferrari's recovery trajectory underwent a major wobble, and the peculiarly communicated removal of Xavier Marcos as Leclerc's race engineer early in the 2024 season. He would not have quite the same influence if he were to shift to another team.

Equally, his influence depends not just on his performance but also his market value. If Ferrari has Leclerc locked into a contractual "golden prison", as our Italian colleague Roberto Chinchero puts it, then threatening to go elsewhere is no longer a lever he can pull.

Nobody doubts Leclerc's speed or commitment. Arguably he often over-commits, especially if the car isn't good enough. If the Ferrari is only 90% or 95% as good as the frontrunning car, Charles will try to make up the shortfall himself in the form of risk. That's why the Tifosi place him in the same rarefied space in their hearts as Gilles Villeneuve.

In recent seasons Leclerc's prime options outside Ferrari have been with Mercedes, Red Bull and McLaren, whose leaders have had to weigh up the performance benefits Leclerc would bring against the change in equilibrium it would cause. Nicolas Todt has certainly been busy doing the rounds of those teams over the past couple of years, but there is a tendency in the F1 media to get rather too excited when a driver's manager is spotted in another team's motorhome.

Sometimes a casual chat is just a casual chat. Sometimes a deal may actually be in progress, though the likelihood of this happening in plain sight is quite low. Often such encounters are staged in public purely to suit each party's agendas: for the team principal, to show their drivers they have other options on the table; for the manager, to show his client has interest from elsewhere.

To manage the internal equilibrium when it announced in January 2024 that Lewis Hamilton would be joining the following season, Ferrari also signed Leclerc to a long-term deal that theoretically reached until the end of 2029 with options, but which was also understood to have included a break point in 2026. On Leclerc's side this was to cover the possibility of Ferrari making a mess of the new technical regulations.

Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton Photo by: Getty Images

Instead, a more complex picture has emerged in which Ferrari has engineered a competitive car, and has been able to add performance to it in the form of upgrades – which hasn't always been true in the recent past. But it has also suffered operational misfires and blown several chances to score more points.

The dynamic in the other leading teams has also changed, though. When Leclerc signed up for the long term in 2024, this was partially because Todt knew Hamilton's move was coming, and had approached Mercedes with a view to Charles filling that vacancy. But when the break clause came into view early this season, Mercedes was perfectly happy with its line-up. The same could be said of McLaren, where Todt is also understood to have held discussions on and off with leaders including Andrea Stella and Zak Brown. When Todt was doing the rounds late last season, McLaren had two drivers in contention for the world championship.

It's also understood that Aston Martin made an approach at the end of last year, but this was at a time of yet more underperformance and internal wrangling in that benighted organisation, when recently installed managing technical partner Adrian Newey had MD and team principal Andy Cowell ousted. Given a choice between Ferrari and a farrago, Leclerc wisely chose door number one.

"I don't want to give up on my ultimate goal, which is to become a world champion with Ferrari," Leclerc said.

"And I believe in the project. I believe in every single person of the team. I think we are in a year where we've been showing innovation. We are very aggressive also in the production plan and in the upgrades we are bringing and that gives me lots of hopes for the future.

"Fred is a big reason on why I have signed again as well. I believe in Fred 200%."

Next time his contract is up for renewal, Leclerc will be over 30. Will he still have as many other opportunities then?

Sports.title: Ocon confirms he is a “free agent” for 2027 as rumours link Camara to Haas | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Esteban Ocon looks set to leave Haas at the end of the season as the driver admitted he is a “free agent” for 2027.

The 30-year-old joined the team from Alpine last year. He was out-scored by rookie team mate Oliver Bearman last year and lies behind his team mate in the standings.

“At the moment I’m definitely a free agent for next year,” said Ocon in Baku. “[There are] all these discussions and there are certain topics in the background that are out of my control at this moment. So I’m focused on the track, trying to deliver the best I can and getting the result that this team deserves.”

Neither Haas driver has scored since Ocon’s ninth-place finish in Monaco.

Ocon said he’s been “really happy with my personal performance” lately. “I think I’ve been getting the maximum out of the car for quite a while now and we’ve never doubted about it.

“Of course, when the car is working, it helps [you] to get something better. When the inconsistencies of the cars are here, where you struggle more, you don’t look as good.

“But I know that I’m exploiting the maximum of the package that I have every single time. So that’s strong.

Ocon ran 10th at the last round in Madrid prior to his pit stop, but fell to 11th at the finish.

Sports.title: Antonelli has “perfect driving style” for 2026 cars – Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is enjoying an extraordinarily successful second season in Formula 1 because his driving style works perfectly with the current generation of cars, says his team mate.

George Russell is Antonelli’s closest rival at the top of the championship standings, but the second-year driver is 81 points ahead. This is a sharp contrast to last year, when Russell out-scored Antonelli by 319 points to 150.

While Russell said Antonelli’s ability was clear before this season, he believes the reduction in aerodynamic downforce and grip this year has played to his team mate’s strengths.

“Of course Kimi is extremely talented,” said Russell. “He’s an incredible driver and has been fast in his whole career.

“I think his driving style is very similar to what he had last year and I think with just how things have fallen this year, it’s kind of the perfect driving style for these cars.”

Russell believes the same is true of other drivers, including Lando Norris, who is the only driver to have won more than one round this season.

“If you look last year, there are definitely trends,” said Russell. “If you look at Brazil last year, Kimi had a really strong race and Lando won in Brazil, and they’re two drivers who are always very strong on the low grip tracks and they’re two drivers who are arguably the best-performing drivers of this season.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“He’s an amazing driver and he was of course doing extremely well last year as well. Let’s see next year if it changes or not, but certainly his natural driving style suits very well for this regulation.”

Charles Leclerc echoed Russell’s view that Antonelli’s potential was clear despite his patchy rookie campaign last year.

“I wish I knew, but clearly he’s doing something that works very well,” said Leclerc. “But to be honest, it’s not that it comes as a complete surprise.

“If I look at Kimi going through the junior ranks, I think it was quite clear for everybody that he had something very special. If you look obviously at his first year in Formula 1, I think he probably faced challenges – it is not up to me to go into detail, I don’t know, but surely he had some struggles in the first year – but this year has been extremely impressive. I mean, from the first race to now, he’s been perfect and driving at a very high level against a driver that I rate extremely high as well, which is George. So he’s doing an incredible job.”

However Leclerc said there is only so much he can tell about Antonelli’s qualities from outside the Mercedes team.

“To [tell] you exactly why he’s so fast, and why he is outstandingly fast this year compared to last year, is very difficult for me. We are all here analysing the data of everybody but we can only go up to a certain amount of detail, then you really need the data of the actual car to dig into more detail.

“So it’s difficult. But his laps look a lot on the limit but somehow he manages to do the lap when it counts and that’s been very impressive to watch.”

Sports.title: Hadjar says injured wrist is “still going to be painful for a while” after comeback | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar says he is still in pain from his injured wrist as he returns to racing this weekend.

The Red Bull driver, who has missed the last three rounds, said his wrist is “good enough to drive, so that’s all I need.”

He said no surgery was required on the injury and a pre-event simulator session indicated it is now strong enough for him to be able to drive.

“I have a small fracture on the outside of the wrist and it’s just quite a long process,” said Hadjar. “I didn’t need any surgery so it’s all natural and it takes some time.

“It’s still going to be painful for a while. It’s going to be six weeks.

“It says that it’s strong enough at the moment to resist the tensions. I had a test on the sim, it went well. I think it’s a similar environment as the cockpit. It’s actually, if anything, nearly identical. So if it’s fine on the sim, with the adrenaline on track and everything, I think I should be okay.

“It’s just been the training sessions have not been fun because I’ve been doing basically nothing with the left limb, so it’s been a bit boring.”

Hadjar confirmed he spoke to multiple Moto GP champion Marc Marquez, who has broken many bones during his career, notably in 2020 when he made an early return from one injury only to sustain another. Hadjar said Marquez told him: “Not to race.”

Red Bull confirmed today Hadjar will continue to drive for them next season. Hadjar said the news is “good, it is nice, but it is natural.”

“I’m not here to be hopeful,” he explained. “I’m here to show what I do on track and naturally, the rest comes, so it’s normal in a way.”

Sports.title: Excessive focus on battle between Ferrari drivers is “not fair” – Leclerc | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc says too much attention has been paid to the on-track battle between him and his team mate, particularly since their clash at Monza.

The Ferrari driver has already admitted he went too far in his first-lap battle with Lewis Hamilton when he forced his team mate wide at turn two.

“Turn two in Monza is something that I’ve said repeatedly is not something that we want to see ever happen again,” said Leclerc. “And that [was] going too far on my side.

“But I’ve been through it already. I think it’s pretty clear that we don’t necessarily have to write [rules of engagement for] those things, I think it’s clear enough.

“But again, I feel like it’s being over-discussed and over-analysed when it’s about the red cars, and that’s not really fair.”

He alluded to incidents between the McLaren and Mercedes drivers during the final laps of the same race. “In Monza, if you look at the four top teams, three of them had fights like this with a car finishing in the grass, and at the end of the day, the only thing we are speaking about still now is the red car, which I don’t think is fair.”

Leclerc said both drivers have exceeded the limits of what is acceptable at times but he is happy with how they race wheel-to-wheel.

“Of course there’s been moments where I went too far, where Lewis went too far, but I think the key in that is to discuss,” he said. “I’ve been with Ferrari since 2019 now and I know how everything we do is over-analysed, over-discussed and very often the conclusions that are taken after those kind of fights are the wrong ones.

“We only need to speak with Lewis to understand, we’ve been doing that all our life. We both want to win and there’s competition but we also want to win as a team and to make Ferrari come out on eventually. So that is the priority.

“I enjoy fighting with Lewis and that’s what is exciting in Formula 1 is to be fighting against the best and Lewis is definitely up there. So for me it’s a big challenge, but I’m enjoying it.”

Sports.title: “Money fears” delay F1’s decision on whether Middle East races will happen – report | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula One Management is delaying its decision over whether to cancel the final two rounds of the season due to concerns over money, according to a report in The Times.

F1 will not receive its huge fees from the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grand prix promoters if it calls off the races. If the promoters make the decision to cancel, they will bear the costs.

But the longer F1 leaves the decision, the harder it may be to organise a replacement for either race. Cancelling a race would reduce the number of points available and could affect the championship situation, potentially even deciding it. Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the championship by 81 points with 233 available.

Domenicali has indicated F1 has a plan to replace the Abu Dhabi finale if that cannot go ahead. This is believed to be a race at Imola in Italy.

F1 has already cancelled the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian grands prix as a result of the war. A replacement for the former, titled the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, will take place next week at the Sepang International Circuit.

Earlier this month FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said the governing body will be guided by local promoters on whether the events could go ahead.

“Being from that part of the world, we can’t jump the gun and just say, that’s it, we are cancelling and then cancel,” he said.

“Are we going to allow our people, our staff, the drivers or the teams to go at risk? No, of course not. We will not. But we’ll have to also listen to the governments and to the local promoter there.”

Sports.title: Red Bull confirms Hadjar will remain as Verstappen’s team mate in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull has given a vote of confidence to Isack Hadjar, extending his contract to drive for the team again next year.

Hadjar made his debut in Formula 1 last year with Red Bull’s second team, Racing Bulls, before being promoted to their leading squad this year.

“Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track,” said team principal Laurent Mekies, “especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.”

Although Hadjar did not compete in the last three rounds due to injury, Hadjar made an impressive start to life at Red Bull, taking a podium finish in his sixth appearance in Monaco. Before being forced out due to injury he had scored 71 points to Verstappen’s 109.

Red Bull has struggled to find an effective team mate to pair Verstappen with. The team handed Sergio Perez a two-year contract extension during 2024 but dropped him at the end of the year for Liam Lawson. Perez’s replacement lasted just two rounds at the start of last year before Red Bull dropped him. Yuki Tsunoda, who replaced Lawson, ended the season with the largest points deficit to a team mate ever seen in F1, leading Red Bull to make another change.

Mekies said Hadjar performed well from the outset after moving up to Red Bull. He will race for the team this weekend in Baku for the first time since the Hungarian Grand Prix in July.

“You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat,” said Mekies. “The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can’t wait to see him back out on track.”

Hadjar said he is “really excited” by his new deal. “From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I’ve been able to justify the faith they’ve had in me,” he said. “I’m constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead.”

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Stalls Zuffa Boxing As Layoff Drags On
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson says a fight announcement is coming. Nearly eight months after he beat Teofimo Lopez, the opponent matters more than the tease.

“Even my haters begging for a fight announcement 😂 I love yall it’s coming lol,” Shakur posted on X.

The Lopez win gave Shakur the strongest moment of his career. He controlled a major fight at Madison Square Garden and had the crowd’s attention afterward, when he brought Conor Benn into the ring and called him “food.” That confrontation made a Benn fight look like an immediate possibility. It went nowhere.

Shakur then spent months discussing a fight with WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney at 144 pounds. Haney’s side said it accepted the proposed weight, but no fight followed. Shakur holds a WBO title at 140, yet he sought a welterweight champion three pounds below that division’s limit while his own challengers waited. Fans are entitled to ask which division he actually intends to fight in.

Zuffa Boxing signed Shakur during the layoff. Dana White paid for a fighter whose win over Teofimo had made him more valuable, but Zuffa has yet to put him in one of its rings. Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela, another Zuffa fighter, called for the fight. Shakur rejected it.

The WBO has already indicated that a mandatory defense is due. It should follow through with a formal order and a clear timetable if Shakur’s next fight does not satisfy that obligation. A champion’s search for a bigger payday cannot leave the rest of the 140-pound division waiting indefinitely.

The Zuffa brass thought they were purchasing the premier American pound-for-pound star right after his masterclass against Teofimo Lopez. Instead, they bought eight months of dead air, endless social media bickering, and an asset that bleeds public interest by the week.

A luxury car loses thousands the minute you roll it off the dealer lot; Shakur Stevenson has been parked in the driveway collecting dust, losing resale value with every single tweet.

What must drive Dana White mad behind closed doors is the refusal to cooperate with company business. In the UFC model, in-house matchups are the lifeblood of the company. Jose Valenzuela stepped up to hand Zuffa a ready-made fight featuring a dangerous, aggressive puncher against their prized technician. Shakur turned him down. Turning down internal company fights while angling for safety catches against Devin Haney at 144 pounds shows an athlete trying to run matchmaking from his couch.

White and the executive room would be entirely justified in pulling the plug, swallowing their pride, and sending Shakur right back out to free agency to waste somebody else’s time and money.

Handing Shakur an ultimatum list is the exact kind of hardball Dana White needs to play. If Zuffa lets him dictate terms, negotiate catchweights, and cherry pick soft touches after an eight-month vacation, they surrender control of their own promotional venture. Giving him three names with a take-one-or-walk clause would instantly test his nerve.

Ernesto “Tito” Mercado belongs right at the top of that sheet. Mercado is a wrecking ball with legitimate dynamite in both hands, stopping 18 of his 19 opponents. He attacks the body with nasty intent, walks through fire, and possesses the kind of brute physical strength that makes safety-first technicians sweat through twelve rounds. The light welterweight division has become a ghost town filled with inactive beltholders and sparring partners, making Mercado the only genuine killer at 140 with the punch to crack Shakur’s defensive shell.

Shakur wants no part of a heavy-handed pressure fighter who will force him to run for his life. Dragging elite sharks up from 135 would apply maximum heat. Andy Cruz is pure agony for Shakur. Cruz boasts Olympic gold credentials, textbook Cuban ring craft, and the punch placement to neutralize Shakur’s potshotting style. Cruz represents the one fighter who can beat Shakur at his own game, outboxing him from the outside while forcing the pace.

Floyd Schofield brings the explosive athletic threat Shakur previously avoided when their scheduled Riyadh bout dissolved. Schofield possesses blazing hand speed, sharp combinations, and the hunger of a young lion with nothing to lose.

Forcing Shakur to sign against Mercado, Cruz, or Schofield would strip away the diva behavior in seconds. If he refuses all three, White can rip up the contract, write off the sunk cost, and show the boxing world that Zuffa refuses to be held hostage by fighters who prefer typing to throwing punches.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Calls Daniel Dubois Easier Than Itauma
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois stopped Filip Hrgovic in 2024, but Hrgovic believes a rematch would be easier for him than his recent win over Moses Itauma. His argument comes down to speed and stance. It leaves out what Dubois did after Hrgovic found him.

During their initial clash in 2024, Hrgovic discovered zero trouble finding Dubois with flush right hands. He landed them repeatedly, and it meant nothing. Dubois absorbed that punishment, marched forward through the artillery, and chopped Hrgovic down in the eighth round after ripping the Croatian’s face apart with heavy lacerations. Dubois proved that hand speed and southpaw angles mean very little when an iron-chinned puncher refuses to back down.

“I think fights against Kabayel and Dubois would be easier than this fight,” Hrgovic stated to talkSPORT Boxing. “Stylistically, speedwise, they will be much easier fights because they’re not so fast. They’re not southpaws. They’re easier to box.”

That is insane logic from an experienced fighter. Itauma faded badly down the stretch because he is a young fighter lacking professional mileage. Dubois operates as an entirely different animal. Dubois applies unrelenting physical pressure, throws heavy leather through the guard, and relishes violent exchanges. Hrgovic found the target in their first bout; he simply lacked the firepower to keep the bigger puncher off his chest. The damage Dubois inflicted on Hrgovic’s scar tissue will reopen in an instant if they share a ring again.

Hrgovic admitted he contemplated retirement in the immediate aftermath of his war with Itauma, showing the mental and physical toll of top-tier prizefighting. Heavyweights contemplating walking away are already feeling the wear on their tires.

Before Hrgovic can even daydream about a lucrative unification payday with Dubois, he must deal with mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez. The slick Cuban possesses the ring discipline and counter-punching ability to derail those stadium dreams in an instant. If Hrgovic treats dangerous contenders as mere stepping stones while chasing a Dubois rematch, he will quickly discover that getting demolished twice by the same man is a dreadful career strategy.

The IBF is historically ruthless about stripping champions who attempt to sidestep their mandatory obligations, and Frank Sanchez already took step-aside money once so Hrgovic and Itauma could contest the vacant title.

Sanchez and his team have zero incentive to sit on their hands again. They smell blood; they know Hrgovic absorbed heavy punishment to get that belt, and they want their shot. Treating Sanchez as an afterthought is dangerous matchmaking arrogance. Sanchez may lack the raw fanfare of Dubois, but the Cuban possesses real ring IQ, sharp counter-punching, fast hands, and defensive discipline.

He does not brawl recklessly or empty his gas tank in three rounds like Itauma did. If Hrgovic enters the ring sluggish, overconfident, or nursing physical mileage from his previous war, Sanchez will happily box circles around him, pile up rounds, and snatch that IBF belt before Hrgovic ever sniffs a unification payday. As for an Itauma rematch, Frank Warren and Queensberry are not foolish to take that risk. Itauma showed he is currently an explosive, three-round frontrunner who melted under sustained veteran pressure.

Throwing a 21-year-old right back into the same firefight that just broke him mentally and physically would be silly. Itauma needs rebuilding against mid-tier opposition to learn pacing and distance control before he ever shares a ring with Hrgovic again. That leaves Hrgovic in a bind. The Dubois rematch is where the massive payday is, but Dubois is tied up with his own business, and Hrgovic cannot legally get to that fight with the IBF belt around his waist unless he handles Sanchez first.

If Hrgovic tries to bypass Sanchez, he gets stripped, loses his leverage, and ends up walking into a Dubois rematch as a battered contender rather than a reigning champion. He has to take the dangerous, low-reward Cuban fighter, and if his head is already in a stadium fight with Dubois, Sanchez is exactly the type of technician to ruin the entire script.

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Says Conor Benn’s Comeback Pays 100% More Than Hearn Offered
Sports.content:
Conor Benn took a two-round thrashing from Ryan, yet his management still secured a lucrative deal for his next fight. Keith Connolly revealed Benn has a guaranteed purse for a return bout, a sum more than 100% higher than Eddie Hearn’s original offer for a Rolly Romero clash.

Connolly did not reveal either figure. His comparison still raises an awkward question for Zuffa: after paying Benn to face Garcia, what kind of fight justifies paying him substantially again?

“In the deal that we made for Conor, we have a substantial comeback number,” Connolly told talkSPORT. He said the payment was negotiated to give Benn a comeback fight in which he can get a win. Connolly also said Zuffa cannot drop Benn under the contract because of the Garcia defeat.

Connolly did his job for Benn. Give him an easy opponent, and he probably gets the win, but who’s going to be impressed after Ryan took him out in two rounds? Put him in with someone who can punch, and Zuffa risks paying a big guarantee to watch Benn lose again.

Benn can still sell a fight in Britain. He’s Nigel Benn’s son, he has a following, and there’s another Chris Eubank Jr. fight to make. But Ryan exposed the part of the sales pitch that said Benn belonged with the best welterweights. He’d looked poor in several fights since coming back; getting stopped in two rounds in his first world title shot made that much harder to sell his fights.

Connolly expects Benn to fight Chris Eubank Jr. a third time, and that’s Zuffa’s best chance of making money on his return. British fans know the family rivalry, even after Ryan stopped Benn in two rounds. Beating an easy opponent first might give Benn a win, but it won’t erase what happened against Garcia. Connolly made sure Benn gets paid either way.

Zuffa bought a circus act, and now they are stuck footing the bill for the cleanup. Dana White thought he was purchasing an elite British star with crossover appeal. Instead, Ryan took two rounds to turn Benn into an international laughingstock.

Now Zuffa holds a contract guaranteeing Benn millions for a return date, with nowhere left to hide him. They cannot put him in with an actual contender at 160 or 168 because any legitimate puncher will put him into retirement. They cannot put him on pay-per-view against an imported tomato can because fans will not pay fifty dollars to watch an unranked punching bag fall down in ninety seconds. That leaves Chris Eubank Jr. as the only escape route.

The promotional idea for a third fight between these privileged sons of famous British legends has completely changed. Nobody with working eyes believes this is a meeting of championship contenders. The athletic intrigue disappeared the moment Ryan landed his right hand, and Benn hit the deck.

The only angle left to sell is morbid curiosity. British boxing fans will tune in for one simple reason: to watch Benn get knocked out again. The novelty of the family rivalry is gone. It has turned into a pure demolition watch party. Eubank has every physical advantage, and he knows Benn cannot take a punch from someone with genuine power. If Zuffa pulls the trigger on the trilogy, they are selling tickets to an execution.

Benn-Eubank Jr. III can do strong business in the UK, but it will not generate the kind of money Zuffa needs to break even on the massive guarantees they handed out.

The British domestic market operates on nostalgia. UK ticket buyers will pack a stadium like Tottenham Hotspur again simply because of the family names. The problem is the pay-per-view numbers and international interest. Benn getting humiliated by Ryan inside two rounds destroyed any illusion that he is an elite global star. Overseas buyers in the United States will not pay sixty or seventy dollars for a domestic grudge match between an exposed welterweight and an aging middleweight.

Sports.title: WBC Orders Carlos Adames to Face Meiirim Nursultanov Next
Sports.content:
Meiirim Nursultanov was supposed to fight for an interim belt Saturday. Instead, he is going straight to Carlos Adames for the full WBC middleweight title.

The WBC ordered Adames to face his mandatory challenger next, Dan Rafael reported Tuesday. If the two sides cannot make a deal, a purse bid is scheduled for October 20. The winner must then fight interim champion Jesus Ramos Jr.

Nursultanov was set to face Ramos on Saturday’s PBC card before Ramos was hospitalized and withdrew with what PBC described as food poisoning. The WBC had previously said the winner of that fight would challenge Adames. Ramos had a sound reason to withdraw, but Nursultanov was ready to fight and should not have to wait for his title opportunity because the bout fell through.

The change gives Nursultanov more than a new opponent. He can fight for the full belt without first risking a loss to Ramos, and the WBC order gives him a deadline for negotiations. He still has to beat Adames, a difficult champion, but he no longer has another fight between him and the title shot he has sought.

Adames, meanwhile, has a mandatory to deal with rather than an open choice of opponents. Nursultanov offers a hard fight without the obvious payday of a marquee name. If the camps cannot agree on terms, the purse bid could also take control of the promotion out of their hands. That makes October 20 a meaningful date for both fighters, though an order is no guarantee the fight gets made.

Ramos keeps his claim to the winner, but his wait could stretch well beyond this fall. First, Adames and Nursultanov have to negotiate, fight, and recover. The WBC has given all three men a sequence; now it has to see that sequence through. Adames is completely trapped in boxing purgatory. He is the ultimate poster child for high risk, zero reward.

When Adames went to Riyadh and took Hamzah Sheeraz to school, he exposed the British fighter for everyone to see. He walked out of Saudi Arabia with a controversial draw while Sheeraz packed his bags and bolted straight out of the division to super middleweight rather than dare run that back. That fight cost Adames his golden ticket. If he had been given the decision he clearly earned, he would have commanded the massive purses and respect of an undisputed or marquee kingpin in Riyadh Season shows. Instead, he got left holding an empty bag.

Calling out Janibek Alimkhanuly and Osleys Iglesias was pure desperation to find someone with a pulse, but both routes were dead ends. Janibek has his own promotional mess and brings virtually no ticket sales or mainstream buzz to make the risk worthwhile for either side. Iglesias is a monster who punches like a mule and brings even less commercial appeal. Nobody with options wants to look in Adames’ direction because he is awkward, hits hard, possesses an iron chin, and cannot sell out an arena on his own name.

Now the WBC has boxed him into a corner. Instead of landing a lucrative unification or a recognizable name, Adames gets Meiirim Nursultanov. This is the classic who needs him scenario at its absolute worst. Nursultanov is a stone-cold Kazakh grinder with deep amateur seasoning who will make every second of every round physically miserable. If Adames wins a grueling decision, nobody outside the hardcore fanbase will care, and the casuals will not give him an ounce of credit. If he gets clipped or outpointed, his entire career plummets off a cliff.

Adames wanted the glory, the rematches, and the unifications. Instead, the boxing business did what it always does to guys without fanbases: shoved him into a basement fight against a dangerous mandatory where he has everything to lose and almost nothing to gain.

Sports.title: Gene Tunney Made Jack Dempsey Chase His Title
Sports.content:
Jack Dempsey’s left hook was most dangerous when he could weave inside and plant his feet. Gene Tunney spent their September 23, 1926, fight making both steps difficult. In the rain at Philadelphia’s Sesquicentennial Stadium, Tunney took the heavyweight championship by unanimous decision over ten rounds.

Dempsey had not defended the title since his 1923 knockout of Luis Firpo. Tunney had remained active and had already fought Harry Greb five times. The layoff invited questions about Dempsey’s timing, but Tunney gave him an immediate, practical problem: getting close enough to throw with full force.

Tunney watched Dempsey come forward and met him with straight punches. A right hand on one of the champion’s early rushes showed the danger of lunging in without making Tunney give ground first. When Dempsey tried again, Tunney changed his position and made him start the attack over. The champion was still dangerous at close range, but he could rarely keep Tunney there.

The rain made the canvas slippery for both men. It is tempting to blame Dempsey’s trouble closing the distance on his footing, yet the wet ring did not stop Tunney from punching and repositioning. Tunney’s timing was the more visible obstacle: he caught Dempsey on the way in, then denied him the stationary target his hooks needed. Contemporary accounts described the fighters slipping on the canvas as the rain grew heavier.

Tunney also refused to spend ten rounds merely fleeing. He stood his ground when he had the opening, drove Dempsey back at times and worked his body as well as his head. Dempsey’s attacks came in bursts, followed by pauses while he searched for another way through. That gave Tunney repeated chances to regain the distance he wanted.

By the final round, Dempsey’s left eye was badly swollen and he was still trying to force his way inside. Tunney continued to meet him with punches. Referee Tommy Reilly and judges Mike Bernstein and Frank Brown awarded the challenger a clear decision.

Dempsey’s three year absence may have cost him sharpness. The fight cannot measure how much. What it showed was Tunney denying him a sustained attack for ten rounds. Dempsey never stopped trying to reach him; Tunney kept making him pay for the attempt.

Stanley Weston / public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Backs O’Shaquie Foster to Pressure Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley is picking O’Shaquie Foster to defeat Emanuel Navarrete, but the call comes attached to an urgent reality check. Foster cannot spend thirty-six minutes waiting around for an immaculate counterpunch. Navarrete throws volume in bundles, keeps men moving in reverse, and steals rounds from guys who are content to admire their own defense.

The two meet October 24 in San Antonio with three super featherweight titles on the line.

Navarrete brings an unorthodox, lunging assault that presents a massive trap. He leaps into wide hooks, throws uppercuts from his knees, and squares his stance right in the line of fire. Foster owns the hand speed to slice Navarrete down the middle while those feet are still airborne. The opening vanishes instantly if Foster retreats instead of planting his feet to fire.

“You ain’t getting no points for no damn defense,” Bradley said on his channel when detailing the habit Foster has of letting opponents throw punches without paying an immediate tax.

Foster cannot afford to tuck behind a high shell while Navarrete clubs away at his elbows and shoulders. Those heavy thuds count in the eyes of ringside officials, particularly in Texas, where aggressive punch output always gets rewarded. Foster already tasted that bitter lesson during his robbery loss against Robson Conceicao, where he landed the cleaner counters yet gave away the visual contest.

The real blueprint involves ripping straight to Navarrete’s midsection and forcing him to drag his feet in reverse. Navarrete lacks the balance or footwork to operate on his back foot, but Foster must put hands on him early to make that happen. If Foster surrenders ring real estate and searches for single counters, he hands Navarrete the exact grinder bout he wants.

Sitting back and relying on defense against Emanuel Navarrete as the B-side is professional suicide. Navarrete is an established ticket seller, a fan favorite, and an all-action Mexican slugger fighting in front of a heavily pro-Navarrete Texas crowd. Every time Navarrete unleashes an ugly four-punch flurry that bounces off Foster’s gloves and forearms, ten thousand people in the arena are going to scream as if someone just got dropped. Judges hear that roar, see the constant forward march, and instinctively score the round for the aggressor.

Foster’s biggest flaw is that he falls in love with making guys miss by an inch without making them pay for it. He treats the sweet science like an academic exercise where simply not getting hit clean is enough to bank three minutes. It is not. That exact minimalist habit burned him against Robson Conceicao in Newark, where Foster clearly outboxed the guy on pure contact quality, threw far too little, and watched the belts get handed to the man who simply looked busier.

The similarities between Foster and Shakur Stevenson expose the exact problem. Shakur gets away with his safety-first style because he commands ring generalship with an authoritative, southpaw lead hand that physically dictates the distance. Shakur controls the geography of the ring so thoroughly that his opponents stop throwing because they feel stupid missing. Foster does not control real estate that way. He retreats in straight lines, covers up, and lets his opponents dictate where the action takes place while he waits for a clean counter window.

Against an awkward buzzsaw who throws 80 punches a round from his knees, his hips, and odd ceiling angles, waiting for the perfect counter means giving away forty seconds of every minute. Navarrete’s punches are heavy and crude. Even when they land on the shoulders, they physically push a retreating fighter back.

Foster does not need to get reckless and swing for the fences, but he absolutely must stand his ground and fire first. If he allows Navarrete to initiate every single sequence and just tries to slip and counter in spurts, he will walk back to his corner after twelve rounds feeling like a master boxer, only to hear the ring announcer read out scores that send him home empty-handed.

Sports.title: Rocky Marciano’s Greatest Win Almost Got Away
Sports.content:
Jersey Joe Walcott was ahead on the scorecards when Rocky Marciano caught him with a right hand in the 13th round on September 23, 1952. That punch made Marciano heavyweight champion. Seventy-four years later, the rounds before it offer a better way to judge him than his perfect record alone.

Walcott knocked Marciano down in the first. He was the older man, but he was also the reigning champion, and his skill gave Marciano trouble deep into the fight. Marciano kept pressing until Walcott made one mistake he could punish. It took him nearly thirteen rounds to find it.

The familiar criticism is that Marciano beat aging champions. There is truth in the ages: Walcott was 38 when Marciano took his title, and Joe Louis was 37 when Marciano stopped him in 1951. Louis was past his best. Walcott’s age, though, does little to explain a fight he was winning before Marciano knocked him out. Marciano gets too much credit if every famous name on his record is treated as a prime opponent. He gets too little if the Walcott fight is dismissed by reading a birth date.

Their rematch lasted one round. Marciano’s next title defense, against Roland LaStarza, took eleven. LaStarza had pushed him to a split decision before Marciano won the championship; in their second meeting, Marciano stopped him. Ezzard Charles then took Marciano the full fifteen rounds before losing their first fight. Three months later, Charles badly cut Marciano’s nose in the rematch, but Marciano finished him in the eighth.

Marciano’s final opponent, light heavyweight champion Archie Moore, dropped him early. Marciano got up and knocked Moore out in the ninth round on September 21, 1955. He retired after that fight with six successful title defenses and a 49–0 record.

The record tells us Marciano never lost. The Walcott fight tells us something harder to capture in a number: he was hurt, behind, and still dangerous enough to change the result with one punch.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley’s Yoenli Hernandez Defense Heads to Purse Bid
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley’s first defense as WBO middleweight champion is headed toward the fight he hoped to delay. Talks with mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez have failed, with a September 29 purse bid set to decide who stages the bout.

Bentley had a unification with IBF champion Aaron McKenna in reach. The WBO blocked it, ruling that its overdue mandatory obligation passed to Bentley when he was elevated to full champion. The sanctioning body also rejected a proposed title fight with Conor Benn. Bentley has the belt, but little freedom to choose what comes next.

Bentley has every reason to be frustrated. McKenna offered a UK fight with commercial appeal and, on paper, a more manageable opponent. Instead, he must face Hernandez, a highly regarded Cuban who brings far less name recognition and a serious risk of taking his belt. Bentley earned the interim title in the ring, but gained the full championship through elevation. If Hernandez beats him, there is no guarantee he finds another route to a world title. The McKenna unification and the bargaining power that comes with being champion would be gone.

Hernandez is a two-time amateur world champion, but Bentley has the deeper professional experience. He went twelve rounds with Janibek Alimkhanuly; Hernandez has yet to fight twelve as a professional. Bentley’s best chance is to close the distance with discipline, work to the body, and make Hernandez fight at a pace he cannot set himself entirely. Loading up on single punches would give the challenger time to move and score between Bentley’s attacks.

Hernandez’s August win over Francisco Daniel Veron offers a useful caution, though not a ready-made plan. Veron kept pressing and reached the final bell, but two judges gave Hernandez the fight by wide margins; the third scored it even. Pressure alone did not erase the Cuban’s cleaner work.

The purse bid adds another uncertainty. If a promoter outside Bentley’s camp wins, the champion may have to defend away from home. The WBO’s $200,000 minimum bid says where bidding starts, not what either fighter will earn.

Bentley wanted McKenna and a chance to add a second belt. Now he must beat Hernandez to keep the first one. For a champion who waited years for this position, that is a steep price for a fight with so little commercial upside.

Facing Yoenli carries massive tactical risk, but it remains the only move that preserves Bentley’s championship equity. Even if Hernandez outboxes him, Bentley at least collects a champion’s 75 percent purse bid share and goes down swinging with his career earnings maximized. If he vacates out of self-preservation, he surrenders the title for zero dollars, forfeits the McKenna unification anyway, and brands himself as a champion who ran from his mandatory.

In professional boxing, getting outpointed by a world-class Cuban amateur hurts, but surrendering the belt in a conference room without getting paid ruins a career far worse.

Without the WBO belt, Bentley reverts instantly to being a tough, high-risk, low-reward domestic gatekeeper. At thirty-one years old, clawing back up the sanctioning body rankings could take years, with no guarantee of ever receiving another title shot.

Ghana News.title: Parents of missing baby at Asafo Market arrested over false accusation against woman
Ghana News.content:
The Ejisu Divisional Police Command has arrested the parents and an uncle of a five-month-old baby allegedly stolen at the Asafo Market in Kumasi after they falsely accused a woman of being responsible for the theft.

The baby was reportedly stolen from the Cape Coast Bus Terminal section of the Asafo Market, at the area known as Opera Site, in the early hours of Sunday, September 20, 2026.

The parents, Freda Owusu and Emmanuel Acheampong, lodged a formal complaint at the Asokwa Police Station on the day of the incident, prompting police to launch a manhunt.

Subsequently, the Ejisu Divisional Police Command arrested a woman, identified as Aliya Salomey, who was travelling with a baby on board a VIP bus heading towards Accra.

According to police, her interaction with the infant aroused the suspicion of fellow passengers, who lodged a complaint at the Ejisu police station upon reaching the town, leading to her arrest.

She was held in police custody and later granted bail after her husband appeared at the station and testified that she was his wife and that the baby belonged to them.

According to the Ejisu Divisional Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Samuel Kofi Gamson, no official report of a missing child had been filed at the Ejisu station at the time the suspect was granted bail.

Later, Freda Owusu, her husband Emmanuel Acheampong, and Mr. Osei Kuffour, a relative of Freda Owusu, went to the Ejisu Divisional Police Command and claimed that the woman who had been granted bail was the one who stole their baby.

Police showed the family a picture of the baby who was in the custody of suspect at the time of her arrest.

The family identified the child in the picture as their missing baby and also identified a photograph of Aliya Salomey as the alleged thief.

The family also circulated the claim on social media that the baby found with Aliya Salomey was their missing child.

Following the complaint, the Ejisu Divisional Police intensified efforts and re-arrested Allah Salomey for further investigations.

An identification parade was subsequently conducted in the presence of the complainant’s family to determine the identity of the child in the suspect's custody.

After the parade, the parents admitted that the baby was not their missing child.

"The complainants, upon physical inspection during the identification parade, admitted that the baby is not theirs, contrary to their earlier claim when they were shown a photograph," a police source told JoyNews.

The development has left the family in a difficult legal situation.

The parents and their uncle were subsequently arrested for providing false information and defaming Aliya Salomey, after they had earlier insisted, including on social media, that the child in her custody was theirs.

The three suspects remain in custody at the Ejisu Divisional Police Command and will be screened and processed in accordance with the law.

Meanwhile, police say arrangements are being made to conduct a DNA test on the baby found in the custody of Aliya Salomey to scientifically establish maternity before she is formally cleared of the child-stealing allegation.

Meanwhile, investigations into the whereabouts of the missing baby continue.

Police have appealed to the public to provide credible information to the Asokwa or Ejisu Divisional Commands to help find the child.

Ghana News.title: Ghana–Russia Center CEO launches book on youth diplomacy in Moscow
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Russia Center for Commerce and Relations, John Aggrey, has launched a book series examining the role of young people in international relations.

The book, "Generation Diplomacy: Youth Shaping International Relations" was unveiled at HSE University in Moscow on Monday, 21 September 2026, during an event held alongside a roundtable on civil society and youth participation in public diplomacy.

The launch, according to Mr Aggrey, coincided with the anniversary of the birth of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah.

The event was hosted by Dr Viacheslav Ivanov, Chief Expert at the university’s Centre for Studies of Civil Society and Nonprofit Sector, who also wrote the book’s foreword.

“This book is a vital testament to the power of youth,” Dr Ivanov said. “They are not simply inheriting the future; they are actively constructing it, often with tools and strategies that were unimaginable to previous generations.”

Mr Aggrey said young people were increasingly shaping diplomacy through innovation and cooperation across borders.

The book launch with students from HSE University in Moscow

“The most impactful diplomacy of the future will be driven by the unity, innovation, and unwavering spirit of the youth,” he said. “Young people are not just participants; they are the architects of a new global dialogue.”

The book explores how young people use social media, online platforms and emerging technologies to advocate for causes, mobilise communities and build understanding across cultures.

Mr Aggrey delivered the keynote address at the accompanying roundtable, titled Civil Society in African Countries and Youth Participation in Public Diplomacy.

Ziona Ayorkor Holm, Head of Business and Innovations at the Ghana Russia Center for Commerce and Relations, also spoke about opportunities for young people in tourism diplomacy, commerce and women’s innovation.

Ghana News.title: Afenyo-Markin hands over as head of Ghana’s delegation to ECOWAS Parliament
Ghana News.content:
The Minority Leader, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, on Wednesday officially handed over leadership of Ghana’s Delegation to the ECOWAS Parliament to the Deputy Majority Leader, George Kweku Ricketts-Hagan.

The handover took place on the sidelines of the 2026 Second Extraordinary Session of the ECOWAS Parliament underway in Accra.

Mr Afenyo-Markin, the Third Deputy Speaker of the ECOWAS Parliament, would, however, continue to serve as a member of Ghana’s delegation to the regional body until 2028.

In his remarks, Mr Afenyo-Markin assured the new head of delegation of his full support and cooperation to ensure continuity and effective representation of Ghana’s interests.

He called for a stronger, people-centred approach to West African integration, insisting that the benefits of regional cooperation must be felt directly by citizens.

He said the true value of integration should be measured by the opportunities available to young people, the ease with which citizens and businesses can move across borders, and the collective ability of member states to confront challenges that no individual country can tackle alone.

“Regional integration must be understood beyond treaties, protocols, and meetings of institutions,” he stressed, adding that its value must be felt in communities across the region.

The week-long programme, being held from Monday, September 21 to Sunday, September 27, also serves as the Second Extraordinary Session of the ECOWAS Parliament of 2026, bringing together ECOWAS parliamentarians, government officials, diplomats, international organisations and civil society.

The seminar is on the theme: "Climate Change as a Factor of Environmental Degradation, Population Displacement and Growing Insecurity in the ECOWAS Region."

On climate and security, Mr Afenyo-Markin cautioned against reducing every conflict in the region to climate change, but noted that environmental pressures could intensify existing vulnerabilities such as poverty, competition over land and water, and weakened livelihoods.

He emphasised the need to take the work of the ECOWAS Parliament closer to the people, recalling decentralised engagements previously held in Liberia in 2019 and Winneba in Effutu in 2021.

He reaffirmed his commitment to the objectives of the ECOWAS Parliament and the broader vision of a more integrated, peaceful, and prosperous West Africa.

The ECOWAS Parliament, also known as the Community Parliament, is the legislative arm of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

It serves as a forum for dialogue, consultation, and consensus for the people of West Africa to promote regional integration.

Ghana News.title: EOCO never personally invited me – Manhyia South MP on chaotic arrest at High Court
Ghana News.content:
Manhyia South Member of Parliament Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah has disputed the Economic and Organised Crime Office’s (EOCO) account of Wednesday’s attempted arrest, insisting that he was never personally invited by the anti-graft agency.

His comments come hours after EOCO said its officers attempted to arrest him as part of lawful steps to secure his attendance in connection with an ongoing investigation.

In a statement, EOCO said it had invited Mr Baffour Awuah on two occasions in February 2026 to assist with its investigation, but the invitations were not honoured.

However, the MP has rejected that claim, describing EOCO’s statement as false.

His comments come after a February 27, 2026 letter from EOCO surfaced following Wednesday’s incident.

The letter, signed by EOCO Acting Executive Director Raymond Archer, was addressed to Nana Baffour Awuah in his capacity as Senior Partner of Sarkodie Baffour Awuah and Partners.

It referenced an earlier invitation dated February 10, 2026, and stated that the invitation had been addressed to him in his capacity as Senior Partner of the law firm.

EOCO, in that correspondence, disagreed with the forwarding of the invitation to the Clerk of Parliament and warned that failure to honour the invitation could result in measures to compel his appearance.

But the MP's latest response suggests a dispute over whether the invitation was directed at him personally or at the law firm and whether he remained in the position in which EOCO addressed the correspondence.

He said the Office subsequently dealt with his Managing Partner regarding the settlement negotiation case his firm executed, which was private in nature, involving a savings and loans company.

"From that time, they have been dealing with Theresa, and they have never dealt with me," he said on Ekosiisen on Asempa FM.

The disagreement follows a confrontation outside the Accra High Court on Wednesday, September 23, when EOCO officers attempted to arrest the MP shortly after he left the court premises.

EOCO later said the arrest was not completed after the situation escalated and officers assessed that proceeding could have endangered public safety.

The Office maintained that its investigation involving Mr Baffour Awuah remains active.

It also acknowledged that the MP subsequently went to the precincts of Parliament to seek sanctuary, despite the House being on recess.

EOCO said it recognises and respects the constitutional privileges and immunities afforded Members of Parliament and would operate within the Constitution and applicable laws.

It nevertheless maintained that membership of Parliament does not, by itself, bring an investigation to an end or place an individual beyond the reach of the law.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s public service faces risky future amid politicisation, talent exodus – Prof Akuoko
Ghana News.content:
Sociologist Prof. Kofi Osei Akuoko

Sociologist Prof. Kofi Osei Akuoko says Ghana’s public service is at risk of losing the institutional capacity needed to deliver essential services as political interference, skilled worker exits, fiscal pressures and declining public trust continue to take a toll.

Prof. Akuoko says country is facing a public-service crisis in which responsibilities are expanding as the capacity of institutions to absorb pressure is shrinking.

He made the submission at the 10th Annual Ghana Sociological and Anthropological Association Conference at the University of Cape Coast.

Speaking on “Ghana: The Risky Future of the Public Service,” Prof. Akuoko said the warning should not be dismissed as a short-term problem.

He described the public service as the backbone of critical services including healthcare, education and land administration, but warned that its ability to cope with growing demands is being weakened.

Political interference

At the heart of the problem, according to Prof. Akuoko, is the politicisation of public-sector appointments, recruitment, promotions and transfers.

He said changes in political power have repeatedly been followed by transfers, reassignments and, in some cases, the effective removal of career officers perceived to be linked to the previous administration.

The consequence, he warned, is a public service where some young officers may begin to see political connections as more important to career advancement than competence.

“Every time a change of government is followed by a purge of technical staff rather than a change of political appointees only,” he said, the separation between public office and the person occupying it becomes weaker.

Prof. Akuoko also cited research indicating partisan bias in public-sector hiring following changes in the governing party.

He said informal referrals and so-called protocol arrangements could also determine who gets access to some public-sector jobs, potentially shutting out qualified young people without influential connections.

Talent is leaving

Another major concern is the steady departure of skilled professionals from the public service to the private sector, international organisations and jobs abroad.

Prof. Akuoko said the problem extends beyond the widely documented migration of doctors, nurses, engineers, statisticians, planners, IT specialists and mid-career administrators.

"The professionals most likely to leave are often those with the skills and mobility to find alternatives, leaving public institutions with a narrower pool of talent even as the complexity of their work increases," he noted.

Wage pressures deepen the problem

Ghana’s fiscal constraints are also putting pressure on the public service.

Prof. Akuoko said the country’s debt restructuring and IMF-supported programme have placed the public-sector wage bill under sustained pressure.

He cautioned that wage compression and recruitment freezes could hit new entrants and middle-grade officers hardest.

That, he said, threatens the very layer of the public service needed to transfer institutional knowledge from experienced officers to younger recruits.

Prof. Akuoko’s prescription

Prof. Akuoko is calling for a comprehensive approach to public-service reform rather than isolated interventions.

He wants government to strengthen open and competitive recruitment, rebuild the middle layer of experienced officers and protect career professionals from arbitrary political transfers.

Professional development and genuine merit-based advancement, he added, must become part of the reform agenda.

For Prof. Akuoko, the problems cannot be addressed separately.

“Politicisation, talent loss, fiscal pressure, digitalisation, decentralisation, youth expectations and public trust are interconnected and can reinforce one another,” he said.

He is therefore urging policymakers and researchers to approach public-service reform as one integrated national undertaking.

Despite the warning, Prof. Akuoko says the situation is not irreversible.

“Ghana’s public service has rebuilt its capacity in the past, but doing so again will require deliberate reforms that take the country’s social and institutional realities into account,” he noted.

Ghana News.title: EOCO must go through Speaker before seeking to arrest Baffour Awuah – Dafeamekpor
Ghana News.content:
The Member of Parliament (MP) for South Dayi, Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, says the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) should have approached the Speaker of Parliament before allegedly attempting to arrest Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah at the Accra High Court.

In a post on X hours after videos of the alleged arrest emerged, Mr Dafeamekpor described the reported attempt to arrest the MP within the court precincts as “absolutely unacceptable” if EOCO had not followed what he said was the established procedure for dealing with parliamentarians.

He cited Article 117 of the Constitution, which addresses the service of civil and criminal processes on the Speaker, MPs and the Clerk to Parliament.

Mr Dafeamekpor acknowledged that the provision applies while they are travelling to, attending or returning from parliamentary proceedings, but argued that the procedure for arresting an MP had come to require an approach through the Speaker.

“Where a law provides a procedure for a right to be exercised, it’s only that procedure that must be followed,” he wrote.

Mr Dafeamekpor said Parliament would resist any attempt to breach what he described as the established protocol between the House and law enforcement agencies.

He also argued that such incidents could harm Parliament’s standing, particularly while it was hosting an ECOWAS Parliament conference in Accra.

He stressed that his objection was to the procedure, rather than any lawful investigation of Mr Baffour Awuah.

“If the Hon Baffour-Awuah is alleged to have committed any offence, for which EOCO requires his presence, by all means, let the law speak but let the law follow lawful procedure,” he wrote.

Mr Dafeamekpor’s account describes an attempted arrest. The circumstances of the incident and EOCO’s position have not been established in the material provided.

Ghana News.title: GTBank supports paediatric cancer care with donation of medical equipment to Ridge Hospital
Ghana News.content:
Guaranty Trust Bank (Ghana) Ltd [GTBank] has donated medical equipment to the Paediatric Oncology Unit of the Greater Accra Regional Hospital, Ridge-Accra, as part of its commitment to supporting improved healthcare delivery and better outcomes for children undergoing cancer treatment.

The items, which were officially handed over to the Management of the Paediatric Oncology Unit, under the Department of Child Health at a brief ceremony held on Friday, 11th September 2026, include four (4) recliner chairs for outpatient chemotherapy, ten (10) chemotherapy spill kits, five (5) extended-cuff nitrile gloves, four (4) Benefusion UVP infusion pumps, two (2) syringe pumps and ten (20) Central Line compound and normal kits.

The donation is aimed at supporting the Unit in strengthening its capacity to provide quality and timely care to paediatric oncology patients, while contributing to a more conducive environment for healthcare professionals and the children and families they serve.

Speaking on behalf of the Managing Director, Mr. Thomas John, at the handover ceremony, the Divisional Head of Corporate Communication and Experience, GTBank Ghana, Agnes Owusu-Afram said the Bank recognizes the critical role healthcare institutions play in improving the quality of life of children and their families battling with this condition.

“At GTBank, we believe that our responsibility to society extends beyond banking. We are committed to supporting initiatives that create meaningful and lasting impact, particularly in areas as healthcare where timely intervention and adequate resources can make a significant difference. It gives us pleasure to again contribute this medical equipment to the Paediatric Oncology Unit and believe that they will support the dedicated medical team in delivering even better care to children battling cancer.”

The Head of the Paediatric Oncology Unit, Greater Accra Regional Hospital, Dr. Nihad Salifu, expressed appreciation to GTBank Ghana for the donation, noting that the equipment would provide valuable support to the Unit and ultimately benefit the children receiving care.

“This is not the first time that GTBank has been here. They have been good partners of the Paediatric Oncology Unit since its establishment; they have been a dedicated provider of medical equipment and logistics; and today they are here to do another round of equipment donation to augment our work. Some of these equipment are the first of their kind in the entire hospital.

We are very grateful for this generous and timely intervention. Paediatric Oncology care requires significant resources, and donations such as this go a long way in enhancing our ability to provide quality care to our patients, and, most importantly, contribute to improving the experience and outcomes of the children and families who depend on this Unit.”

Head of the Department of Child Health, Greater Accra Regional Hospital, and Paediatric Intensivist, Dr. Charlyne Kilba also underscored the importance of the donation.

“This donation has come to indeed fill a great need and gap. We are overwhelmed by this gesture. People will think that chairs like these are not critical, but we have to remember that these children experience nausea, lightheadedness and all kinds of conditions during chemotherapy. Moving from our small chairs to these recliner seats, for instance, will ensure they are relaxed, comfortable and less traumatized while receiving treatment. These monitors and infusion pumps will also enable us to deliver precise doses at precise rates, which is really important for us as healthcare professionals. God bless GTBank for this big gesture.”

The donation forms part of GTBank Ghana’s broader Corporate Social Investment initiatives, through which the Bank continues to support impactful interventions in healthcare, education, community development and other areas that contribute to sustainable social development.

Guaranty Trust Bank (Ghana) Ltd is a leading financial institution committed to providing innovative financial solutions and creating sustainable value for its customers, shareholders and communities. Through its corporate citizenship initiatives, the Bank continues to support interventions that contribute to the social and economic development of Ghana.
