Lima will host the 50 Best Restaurants 2026 from 2 to 4 November, the first edition held in South America. PromPerú, the state export and tourism promotion agency, projects about US$2 million in immediate local spending.

Three Days of Food in the Peruvian Capital

The programme runs from Monday 2 to Wednesday 4 November 2026. It opens with a welcome lunch, and the 50 Best Talks forum follows on Tuesday 3 November.

The awards ceremony takes place on Wednesday 4 November at the Teatro Municipal de Lima. The new list is revealed there and streamed live on the organisers’ YouTube channel.

PromPerú expects about 1,200 chefs, food journalists, content creators and industry figures from more than 34 countries. Local restaurants will also host visiting chefs in ticketed 50 Best Signature Sessions.

This is the awards night itself, not a side event or a regional spin-off. The 2026 winner will be named on that stage in Lima.

Who Announced It, and When

The organisers named Lima as host on 10 July 2026. That was a change of plan, since Abu Dhabi had been announced for this year first.

The detailed programme was presented in Lima on Monday 21 September 2026. Teresa Mera, executive president of PromPerú, led the launch with chefs Virgilio Martínez and Mitsuharu ‘Micha’ Tsumura.

Rogers Valencia, Peru’s foreign trade and tourism minister since late July, spoke by video message. Rikki Tidball, events director for the organisers, also sent a recorded message.

What the US$2 Million Figure Really Means

PromPerú projects about US$2 million in immediate economic activity around the event. The estimate covers lodging, food, transport, production services and entertainment.

Its breakdown includes more than 700 international air tickets and about US$400,000 in hotel bookings. It also counts more than US$300,000 in food and roughly US$300,000 in local production work.

This is a projection, not prize money and not an audited result. No winning restaurant receives cash, and the final total will depend on who actually travels.

PromPerú also points to the organisers’ reach online, with more than four million social media followers. It says their site draws 8.8 million users a year.

Peru’s Place on the 50 Best Restaurants 2026 Stage

Four Lima restaurants sit in the current list, which was published in Turin in June 2025. Maido is No.1, Kjolle No.9, Mérito No.26 and Mayta No.39.

Central, which won the top spot in 2023, is now in the Best of the Best hall of fame. Restaurants that have been voted No.1 are no longer eligible for the annual ranking.

Maido joins that group at the Lima ceremony, so it will not be ranked again. Mil, in Cusco, sat at No.75 on the extended 51–100 list.

Has Lima Done This Before?

Lima hosted Latin America’s 50 Best Restaurants in 2013 and 2014, according to Peru’s trade and tourism ministry. Those were regional awards, not the global edition.

The regional ceremony moved to Mexico City in 2015. The global list has been unveiled in cities including Singapore, Antwerp, London, Valencia and Turin.

Peru has promoted its cooking abroad as a tourism draw for two decades. This is the first time the global ceremony comes to the country.

What Hosting Has Meant for Other Cities

Roberta Garibaldi, a food tourism professor at Italy’s University of Bergamo, studied earlier editions. Her analysis put direct benefits for Valencia in 2023 at about US$5 million.

That figure rested on more than 800 international flights, 5,500 hotel nights and over 10,000 meals. She valued the media coverage at about US$106 million in advertising terms.

Those numbers are one analyst’s estimates, not official accounts. The same study argued the biggest gain is long-term visibility rather than three days of takings.

Turin hosted the 2025 ceremony and drew more than 1,300 guests over four days. Piedmont’s regional government backed the bid and used the week to promote the wider area.

Why This Matters If You Live In or Invest In Peru

Hotels, restaurants, taxi firms and production agencies in Lima can expect a busy first week of November. If you plan to eat out or travel then, book early.

For investors, this is a marketing moment for Peru’s food and hotel sector, not a guaranteed return. PromPerú hopes it lifts average visitor spending over time, but that is a hope rather than a result.

Ticket prices, the full guest list and the 2026 rankings have not been published. The order stays secret until the night itself.

How to Follow It From Anywhere

The ceremony will be streamed live on the organisers’ YouTube channel. Three awards, plus the extended 51–100 list, are announced before the main night.

PromPerú says one in five foreign holiday visitors names food among their reasons for choosing Peru. Those travellers stay about 12 nights in the country.

Lima will stay in the food world’s conversation long after the plates are cleared. For now, the city has about six weeks to get ready.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where are the awards held?

The programme runs from 2 to 4 November 2026 in Lima. The ceremony is on Wednesday 4 November at the Teatro Municipal de Lima.

Is the US$2 million a prize for the winner?

No. It is PromPerú’s projection of immediate local spending on hotels, food, transport, production and entertainment.

Which Peruvian restaurants are on the list now?

Four, all in Lima: Maido at No.1, Kjolle at No.9, Mérito at No.26 and Mayta at No.39.

Sources: The World’s 50 Best Restaurants host-city announcement, 10 July 2026; PromPerú statement and programme launch, 21 September 2026; Andina; Gestión; Il Sole 24 Ore; El Peruano.

World.title: ArtRio 2026 Closes in Rio With 50,000 Visitors, Organizers Say
World.content:
BRAZIL · CULTURE

Key Facts — What happened ArtRio 2026 ran from 16 to 20 September at Marina da Glória in Rio de Janeiro.

— The crowd Organizers put attendance at about 50,000, against about 55,000 reported for 2025.

— The money R$67.7 million (US$13.2 million) is an estimate of the fair week’s impact on Rio.

— The catch That figure is not gallery sales, and it is the organizer’s own estimate.

— Who took part More than 80 galleries, exhibitors and institutions, mostly Brazilian, joined the fair.

— What is missing No audited attendance count and no total for art sold have been published.

The headline number is not the value of art sold — it is the fair’s own estimate of what the week brought the city.

Marina da Glória in Rio, where the fair ran from 16 to 20 September

ArtRio 2026 closed on Sunday 20 September at Marina da Glória in Rio de Janeiro. Organizers said about 50,000 people visited the 16th edition of the art fair.

What ArtRio 2026 reported at the close

ArtRio 2026 ran from Wednesday 16 September to Sunday 20 September at Marina da Glória, on Rio de Janeiro’s waterfront. It was the fair’s 16th edition.

The organizers said about 50,000 people came. They also counted more than 80 galleries, exhibitors and institutions, Brazilian and foreign.

The fair is produced by Dream Factory, whose president is Duda Magalhães. Maria Luz Bridger is the artistic director.

Those numbers come from the fair’s own closing release. Brazilian outlets, among them Diário do Rio, published it on 22 September.

That release is a claim by the organizer, not an audit. No independent count of visitors or of sales has been published.

What the big money figure really measures

Headlines placed R$67.7 million (US$13.2 million) beside the fair’s name. The figure is not the value of the art that changed hands.

In the organizer’s own wording, it is an expected economic impact on the city during the week of the event. That is a forecast, not a till receipt.

Such estimates usually cover hotels, restaurants, transport and shopping by visitors. The method behind this one has not been published.

Currency conversions here use about 5.11 reais to the dollar, the rate on 23 September 2026. A weaker real would trim the dollar value.

The organizers also said sales were higher this year. They gave no total, so that claim cannot be checked.

How ArtRio 2026 compares with last year

The 15th edition ran from 10 to 14 September 2025, also at Marina da Glória. Organizers then reported about 55,000 visitors.

For that year they put the fair week’s impact on the city at around R$130 million (US$25.4 million). The 2026 estimate is roughly half as large.

No explanation for the gap has been made public. The two estimates may simply rest on different assumptions.

Gallery counts moved too. The 2025 edition listed 65 galleries plus institutions, while reports this year ranged from 76 galleries to more than 80 exhibitors.

The organizers did not say how many countries were represented. Most exhibitors were Brazilian, mainly from Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo.

What actually sold on the floor

Dealer-level prices give a firmer picture than any single headline number. Brazil Journal, a business outlet, collected them from galleries during the fair.

Galatea sold a 1981 oil painting by Roberto Burle Marx for R$900,000 (US$176,000). Pinakotheke sold two works by José Pancetti at R$350,000 (US$68,500) each.

Galleria Continua sold a large painting by Cristina Canale for US$80,000. Vermelho said its stand sold out on the first preview day.

Much of the trade sat between US$10,000 and US$80,000. Dealers described the market for established modern masters as slower and more selective.

Gustavo Rebello Arte placed a 1947 work by Gyula Kosice with an asking price of R$700,000 (US$137,000). The buyer was an executive at an international bank who collects in Buenos Aires.

Who came, and why the fair cares

Sheikha Al-Mayassa bint Hamad Al Thani, who chairs Qatar Museums, visited on 15 September. Bridger described it as the fair’s first visit by a collector of that weight from the Middle East.

Curators from Madrid’s Reina Sofía museum, Turner Contemporary in England and the Wexner Center for the Arts also came.

Visits like these matter to galleries because museums buy slowly but publicly. A work placed in a museum lifts an artist’s standing for years.

The fair donated Emi, a work by the Brazilian artist Nádia Taquary, to the Museum of Modern Art in Rio. It came from the Portas Vilaseca gallery.

ArtRio 2026 also opened the city’s new art and culture week, run with Rio’s culture department. That programme listed about 450 events.

What it means for expats and investors

For readers living in or invested in Latin America, the lesson from ArtRio 2026 is about labels. An impact estimate and a sales total are not the same thing.

Rio’s culture calendar does move money through hotels, restaurants and taxis. How much, in this case, rests on a forecast the fair has not explained.

What is not known is easy to list. There is no audited attendance figure, no total value of art sold, and no published method behind the estimate.

Anyone weighing a gallery stake, an art purchase or a hospitality bet should ask for dealer-level numbers. For parts of this fair, those exist and are specific.

If ArtRio publishes a fuller account later, the picture will be easier to judge. Until then, the safest reading is a solid fair in a cautious market.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does the reported 67.7 million reais (about US$13.2 million) figure actually mean?

It is the organizer’s estimate of the fair week’s impact on Rio’s economy, about US$13.2 million. It is not the value of art sold.

How many people visited the fair?

Organizers reported about 50,000 visitors. That is below the roughly 55,000 they reported for the 2025 edition.

When and where was ArtRio 2026 held?

It ran from 16 to 20 September 2026 at Marina da Glória in Rio de Janeiro. It was the fair’s 16th edition.

Sources: ArtRio’s closing release for its 16th edition, as published by Diário do Rio, 22 September 2026; Brazil Journal; The Art Newspaper; Agência Brasil; ArtRio’s 2025 closing figures as reported by Brazilian media.

World.title: JPMorgan Uruguay Office Under Study as Family Offices Crowd Montevideo
World.content:
URUGUAY · BANKING

Key Facts — What was said JPMorgan’s Southern Cone chief told Bloomberg Línea the bank is weighing an office in Uruguay.

— Who he is Facundo Gómez Minujín runs JPMorgan in Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia.

— Where it stands JPMorgan serves Uruguay from Buenos Aires and from teams in the United States and Switzerland.

— The boom Licensed advisers and portfolio managers held US$47.29 billion for 88,298 clients at the end of 2025.

— The catch No decision, no registration and no opening date have been announced by the bank.

— What is needed A representative office must register with Uruguay’s central bank; a branch needs government authorization.

Uruguay’s licensed wealth firms now manage US$47.29 billion for 88,298 clients. A global bank says it is looking, not deciding.

Montevideo; the bank covers Uruguay from Buenos Aires today

A JPMorgan Uruguay office is under study, not decided, the bank’s Southern Cone chief said on 23 September 2026. JPMorgan itself has announced no plan, no site and no timetable.

What JPMorgan’s regional chief said

Facundo Gómez Minujín is JPMorgan’s chief executive for Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia. He told Bloomberg Línea on 23 September 2026 that the bank is weighing a presence in Uruguay.

Speaking in Spanish, he said Uruguay gives the bank “a lot of peace of mind”. He described the country as full of family offices, and its financial industry as very strong.

He was blunt about the weak spots too. Uruguay had stopped growing at attractive rates, he said, and a long argument over pension reform had slowed investment.

JPMorgan Uruguay office: what is not confirmed

JPMorgan has issued no statement of its own about opening in Uruguay. No registration, lease or opening date has been made public.

The remarks came in a media interview, not in a company announcement. So far it is an idea under review, not a commitment.

The bank’s private bank website lists Uruguay among the southern Latin American markets it covers. Those clients are served by teams based in the United States and Switzerland.

What a family office is

A family office is a private firm that manages one wealthy family’s money and affairs. Its work usually covers investments, tax, property, succession and sometimes charitable giving.

A multi-family office does the same job for several unrelated families at once. Neither type is a retail bank, and neither takes deposits from the public.

Most of Uruguay’s wealth firms sit in Montevideo, many inside free zones that exempt them from most taxes. Uruguay XXI, the state investment promotion agency, says about 60% of them work from those zones.

How big the boom is, in numbers

The Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU) licenses two kinds of wealth firm: portfolio managers and investment advisers. At the end of 2025 there were 74 managers and 102 advisers.

Together those 176 firms ran 174 offices in Uruguay and employed 1,036 people. They looked after 88,298 clients, 22.5% more than a year earlier.

Assets under management reached US$47.29 billion at the end of 2025, up 12.2% in a year. Uruguay XXI puts the 2020 figure at US$28.89 billion.

Where the money comes from

Argentine residents are the largest group by far. They accounted for 39,613 clients and US$26.44 billion, or 55.9% of all assets under management.

Uruguayan residents came next, with 36,692 clients and US$5.15 billion. Brazilian residents numbered 2,350, holding US$1.87 billion.

Another 9,643 clients were resident elsewhere, with US$13.84 billion. The BCU says much of that sum sits in investment funds set up abroad.

The tax and residency rules behind it

Since 2020 a new tax resident has been able to choose an 11-year break on foreign investment income. That covers the year of the move plus the ten years after it.

Uruguay’s 2025–2029 budget law changed who qualifies, for anyone arriving from 1 January 2026. Access now needs more than 183 days a year in the country, or a qualifying investment.

The property route asks for more than 12.5 million indexed units, about US$2 million. The fund route asks for at least 625,000 indexed units, about US$100,000 a year, for production or innovation projects.

Tax residency itself is separate, and easier to reach. One route is property above 3.5 million indexed units, about US$575,000, plus 60 days a year in Uruguay.

Dollar values for indexed units use 23 September 2026 rates. On that day one US dollar bought about 40.2 Uruguayan pesos.

What Uruguayan regulators require

A foreign bank can open a representative office in Uruguay only after registering with the BCU. Such an office may promote and facilitate business for its parent.

It may not carry out financial intermediation, credit or currency operations. It may not take money, securities or precious metals from anyone.

A bank or a branch is a much bigger step. It needs authorization from the executive branch, granted on a favorable report from the central bank.

The Superintendency of Financial Services must then clear it to begin operating. Registered representatives may also act as investment advisers once they are listed.

What this means for expats and investors

A JPMorgan Uruguay office would change nothing today for people already banking there. No account, fee or service is affected by a bank thinking out loud.

The wider trend is real, though, and rivals have already moved. Itaú opened its first private banking office outside Brazil in Uruguay in August 2026.

That service is aimed at clients with at least US$2 million, and BTG Pactual bought HSBC’s local business. More competition can mean better terms, but that is not guaranteed.

What is not known is whether JPMorgan will register anything, and when. A BCU filing, or a statement from the bank, would be the first hard sign.

Until one appears, the measurable story is Uruguay’s steady pull on regional wealth. That pull looks set to keep growing quietly, whatever one bank decides.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has JPMorgan confirmed a JPMorgan Uruguay office?

No. Its Southern Cone chief said the bank is weighing one, but JPMorgan has announced no decision, no registration and no date.

What is a family office?

A private firm that manages the money, tax, property and succession of one wealthy family. A multi-family office does the same for several families.

How big is Uruguay’s wealth industry?

At the end of 2025, 176 licensed firms managed US$47.29 billion for 88,298 clients, according to the central bank.

World.title: Chile-Australia Strategic Partnership Takes First Step in New York
World.content:
CHILE · BUSINESS

Key Facts — What happened Chile and Australia agreed to start work towards a Strategic Partnership, without signing anything.

— Who and where Foreign ministers Francisco Pérez Mackenna and Penny Wong met at the UN in New York.

— The catch No treaty, no memorandum and no funding were announced, so the mining pledges stay general.

— Mining link Australian firms already run Escondida, the world’s biggest copper mine by output, in northern Chile.

— The cable Humboldt will link Santo Domingo in Chile with Sydney, about 14,800 kilometres away.

— What comes next Cable installation is due to start late in 2026, with service from 2028.

Two foreign ministers agreed in New York to begin the work. Nothing was signed, and the two headline items sit at very different stages.

The port of Valparaíso; the Humboldt cable is due to land nearby at Santo Domingo

Chile and Australia agreed on Tuesday 22 September 2026 to begin building a Chile-Australia strategic partnership. Their foreign ministers met at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, and signed no document.

What the Two Ministers Actually Agreed

Chile’s foreign minister, Francisco Pérez Mackenna, met Australia’s foreign minister, Penny Wong, on Tuesday 22 September 2026. Chile’s foreign ministry said they agreed to begin the path towards a Strategic Partnership.

The Chile-Australia strategic partnership is a political upgrade, not a legal one. No treaty was signed, no memorandum of understanding was published, and no joint declaration was issued.

The contrast was visible in Chile’s own week in New York. A day earlier the same minister signed terms of reference with Morocco to open free trade talks.

Chile and Australia already have a free trade agreement and share membership of the Trans-Pacific trade pact known as the CPTPP. In November 2025 the two governments issued a joint statement marking 80 years of relations.

The Mining Part, in Concrete Terms

Pérez Mackenna described the mining element as cooperation, not a contract. He pointed to better industry practice, more investment, and joint work as producers of critical minerals.

The minerals involved are copper and lithium on the Chilean side. Australia’s strengths are iron ore and lithium, so the overlap sits mainly in lithium and copper.

The mechanism is investment, not regulation or research funding. Australia’s BHP operates Escondida in northern Chile, with Rio Tinto and Japan’s JECO Corporation as the other shareholders.

Rio Tinto, an Anglo-Australian company, has separate lithium agreements with Chile’s state firms Codelco and Enami. No new project, fund or research programme was announced this week.

Trade between the two countries is still modest. Chilean exports to Australia reached US$235 million from January to August 2026, led by gold, central bank figures show.

The Humboldt Cable and the Chile-Australia Strategic Partnership

The Humboldt cable is the most concrete item the two ministers discussed. It is a Google project built with Desarrollo País, Chile’s state infrastructure company.

One leg will run about 14,800 kilometres from Santo Domingo, near Valparaíso, to Sydney. A second leg will link Santo Domingo with Panama City over about 6,500 kilometres.

The whole system is more than 21,000 kilometres long and passes through French Polynesia. Chile’s government puts the investment at more than US$300 million; industry estimates are near US$400 million.

Google and Desarrollo País signed the contract for Humboldt Connect, the venture that will sell capacity, in June 2025. Google funds most of the build.

A regional coastal commission in Valparaíso approved installation and operation on 19 June 2026. Installation is expected in the last quarter of 2026, with service from 2028.

Australia’s role is as the landing country, not the financier. The cable is expected to come ashore at Maroubra Beach in Sydney.

The timetable has slipped more than once. Service was first promised for 2026, then the first half of 2027, and is now set for 2028.

Why a Pacific Data Cable Matters to Chile

Today most data between South America and Asia travels through the United States. Humboldt would be the first direct route between the two regions.

A direct route cuts the distance and the delay, known as latency. It also adds a second path if another cable is damaged.

That matters for money, not only for engineering. Cheap, fast and reliable capacity is what data centre operators look for before they commit.

Chile wants to be the region’s digital gateway, and already hosts a Google data centre and cloud region. It also plans land links so Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil can use the route.

What It Means for Expats and Investors

Nothing in the Chile-Australia strategic partnership changes taxes, visas or investment rules today. It is a signal of direction, not a new set of rights or obligations.

For mining investors, the practical effect is easier official contact between Santiago and Canberra. That can help with introductions and meetings, though it guarantees no project.

For technology firms and remote workers in Chile, the cable is the item to watch. Better links to Asia could support data centres, cloud services and faster connections.

Chile is also bidding for Valparaíso to host the secretariat of the new High Seas Treaty. The ministers raised that bid in the same meeting.

What Is Not Yet Known

There is no date for signing a partnership document, and no venue has been named. The full scope of the partnership has not been published.

The mining element has no project list, no budget and no timetable. It is not known whether it will cover research, regulation or only investment promotion.

Australia has not announced any funding for the Humboldt cable. The next real test is simple: whether cable laying starts before the end of 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did Chile and Australia sign anything?

No. The two foreign ministers agreed to begin work towards a Strategic Partnership, without a treaty, a memorandum or a joint declaration.

What is the Humboldt cable?

It is an undersea cable from Google and Desarrollo País linking Chile to Sydney and Panama City. Installation is due to start in late 2026.

Does this change anything for investors now?

Not yet. No project, budget or rule change was announced, so the effect today is diplomatic rather than commercial.

World.title: Guyana Gas-to-Energy Plant Targets December First Fire at Wales
World.content:
GUYANA · ENERGY

Key Facts — What happened Guyana is preparing to fire the first turbine at its Wales gas plant in December.

— How big Phase One is designed for 300 MW, from four gas turbines and two steam turbines.

— The money The state contract was US$759 million, plus a US$97 million settlement with the contractor.

— The catch The promised 50 percent cut in power bills only comes once 228 MW is running.

— Who it affects Households, businesses and investors that depend on Guyana Power and Light supply.

— What comes next Three more gas turbines are due about three months after the first one.

The 300 MW project is two years late and has cost more than planned. A first turbine test is set for early December, but cheaper power comes later.

Georgetown; the Wales gas plant is meant to cut power bills once it reaches 228 megawatts

The Guyana gas-to-energy plant at Wales is being prepared for a first turbine firing around 4 December 2026. Only about 57 megawatts (MW) is expected by year end, well short of the 300 MW design.

What the Guyana gas-to-energy plant is

The Guyana gas-to-energy plant sits at Wales, on the West Bank of Demerara, in Region Three. It is a combined-cycle station rated at 300 MW under Phase One.

The design uses four gas turbines and two steam turbines, the Department of Public Information said. A natural gas liquids (NGL) plant is being built on the same site.

Gas comes ashore through a 12-inch pipeline built by ExxonMobil from the Stabroek Block offshore. The line is designed to carry up to 120 million cubic feet of gas a day.

About 1,300 people are working on the site. Roughly 425 kilometres of new transmission lines are being built to move the power.

December first fire and the 57 MW target

Minister of Public Utilities and Aviation Deodat Indar said teams are working towards about 4 December for first fire. That is the moment gas is burned in a turbine for the first time.

The first Siemens turbine is expected to add about 57 MW to the national grid. Weeks of testing follow before power can reach customers reliably.

Indar said the other three gas turbines should follow about three months later, lifting gas-fired output to 228 MW. The two steam turbines are expected a few months after that, reaching 300 MW.

Siemens Energy has been chosen to run and maintain the plant. Its deal covers five years of operation and twenty years of turbine maintenance.

Gas will flow through the offshore pipeline for the first time at that test. The line has stood unused for about 21 months.

The cost, the contractor and the US loans

The state signed a US$759 million contract with the Lindsayca and CH4 joint venture in December 2022. Delivery was first promised for the end of 2024.

A dispute ended in a US$97 million settlement, a 12.8 percent rise on that contract sum. The Office of the Prime Minister put the wider state budget at US$1 billion, capped at US$1.1 billion.

The Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) approved US$527 million for the project in December 2024. The loan was signed in Georgetown in January 2025.

EXIM chairman John Jovanovic said on 21 September 2026 that the bank could lend up to US$550 million. That money would go to a second, privately financed phase at Wales.

ExxonMobil is paying for the offshore pipeline, which sits outside the government’s budget. Guyanese outlets put the whole scheme, state works and pipeline together, at about US$2 billion.

When electricity bills should fall

Prime Minister Mark Phillips said in August 2026 that the promised 50 percent cut arrives at the end of Phase One. He defined that as 228 MW of gas-fired power.

So the December milestone will not lower bills by itself. President Irfaan Ali has said some communities are already receiving phased reductions.

Opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed questioned the December start in mid-September, citing unfinished substation and transmission work. The government says the schedule still holds.

The contractor has asked for more money to finish the job. Ali said in mid-September that no extra payment was under discussion.

Exxon’s Trinidad block is a separate story

ExxonMobil also holds Block TTUD-1, or Trinidad and Tobago Ultra Deep 1, off that country’s east coast. The block covers 7,165 square kilometres and was awarded by Trinidad’s government in August 2025.

Exxon operates the block with 90 percent and Occidental Petroleum holds 10 percent. A large seismic survey ended in August 2026, six weeks early, Energy Minister Roodal Moonilal said.

Exxon exploration head John Ardill said on 21 September 2026 that drilling could start in late 2027 or early 2028. He has said Exxon wants to move faster in Trinidad than it did in Guyana.

That comparison is about Exxon’s own pace, not a race with Guyana’s government. The block lies in Trinidad and Tobago’s waters, and Guyana holds no stake in it.

What the Guyana gas-to-energy plant means for expats and investors

Power costs and reliability shape the price of everything from rent to restaurant meals in Georgetown. A working plant would ease both, but the gain arrives in stages.

Anyone weighing a Guyanese project should plan for grid limits through 2027, not for cheap power at once. Two rented power ships are still filling part of the gap.

What is not known is whether first fire holds to December, and when 228 MW actually arrives. The final bill for Phase One is not settled either.

Guyana will learn a great deal in the next three months, and the turbine test will be the clearest signal yet.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Guyana gas-to-energy project?

It is a 300 MW gas-fired power station and a natural gas liquids plant at Wales, West Bank Demerara. It burns gas piped ashore from the Stabroek Block.

When will it start producing power?

A first turbine firing is targeted for about 4 December 2026, adding roughly 57 MW. Full 300 MW output is expected later, in stages.

Will electricity bills fall in December?

No. The government says the 50 percent cut follows once Phase One reaches 228 MW.

Sources: Guyana Department of Public Information site updates, 8 and 22 September 2026; Export-Import Bank of the United States; Office of the Prime Minister of Guyana; Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of Energy and Energy Industries; Kaieteur News; Demerara Waves; Trinidad Express; Upstream.

World.title: Brazil Market Moves: NG.CASH Funding, Franklin ETFs, B3 Bitcoin Futures
World.content:
BRAZIL · BUSINESS

Key Facts — What happened NG.CASH raised US$15 million, Franklin Templeton listed five funds on B3, and B3 opened dollar bitcoin futures.

— Who led it Blockchain Capital led the NG.CASH investment, lifting total funding since 2021 above US$65 million.

— The new funds Five Franklin Templeton depositary receipts track US shares, India, Taiwan, bitcoin and ether.

— The contract B3’s BTC future covers 0.01 bitcoin, is priced in dollars and settles in cash.

— The catch The Franklin receipts are marked for qualified investors, and the NG.CASH crypto licence is still pending.

— What comes next Brazil’s central bank has yet to rule on the NG.CASH crypto licence application.

Blockchain Capital backed a São Paulo fintech, Franklin Templeton listed five funds on B3, and the exchange opened a dollar-priced bitcoin future.

The B3 exchange in São Paulo, where the new futures contract and the Franklin receipts trade

One-stop reference Company Intelligence Every listed company in Latin America — financials, ownership and structure for 1,450+ companies across 26 exchanges, in one place. Browse the directory →

Three Brazil market moves in three days point to foreign interest in the country’s financial plumbing. NG.CASH raised US$15 million led by the US fund Blockchain Capital, the São Paulo fintech said on Wednesday.

NG.CASH raises US$15 million from a US fund

NG.CASH announced the US$15 million strategic investment on Wednesday 23 September 2026. Blockchain Capital, a US venture firm focused on digital assets, led it.

The company did not name a stage such as seed or Series B. It also named no other investor in the announcement.

Total funding since the 2021 founding now passes US$65 million. NG.CASH began as an offshoot of a YouTube channel that now has 20 million subscribers.

Earlier backers include NEA, which led a US$26.5 million Series B round last year. Exame reported that this is Blockchain Capital’s first investment in Brazil.

What the fintech does and what it still needs

The platform says it serves more than 10 million users, most from middle- and lower-income households. Its credit products include Crédito CLT, a payroll-linked loan, and Pix Crédito.

NG.CASH holds two Banco Central do Brasil licences, one for a direct credit society and one for a payment institution. An application for a virtual asset service provider licence is still being processed.

Brazil’s central bank set rules for virtual asset companies earlier this year. NG.CASH already offers bitcoin and ether trading on its app.

The company is targeting R$1 billion (US$195.7 million) in credit originated by 2027. Currency conversions here use 23 September 2026 rates, about 5.11 reais to the dollar.

Franklin Templeton lists five funds on B3

Franklin Templeton announced its entry into Brazil’s market for depositary receipts of exchange-traded funds on Wednesday. B3 listed five of them, quoted in reais, with a standard lot of one receipt.

A Brazilian depositary receipt, or BDR, is a local security backed by a foreign-listed fund. It lets people in Brazil buy foreign funds in reais without sending money abroad.

The tickers are EZBC for the Franklin Bitcoin ETF and EZET for the Franklin Ethereum ETF. USPX covers the Franklin US Equity Index ETF, FLTW the FTSE Taiwan fund and FTIN the FTSE India fund.

USPX tracks the Morningstar US Target Market Exposure Index, which covers the top 85% of the US market. EZBC and EZET hold bitcoin and ether directly.

B3’s listing notice marks the five receipts for qualified investors. Under Brazilian rules those are generally people with more than R$1 million (US$195,700) invested.

B3 opens a dollar-priced bitcoin future

B3 started trading the dollar-denominated bitcoin future on Monday 21 September 2026. The exchange set the date in circular 059/2026-VPC, published on 15 September 2026.

The ticker is BTC and each contract covers 0.01 bitcoin. Prices are quoted in US dollars per bitcoin, with a minimum move of US$5.

Contracts expire every month, normally on the last Friday. Settlement is in cash against the Nasdaq Bitcoin Reference Price – Settlement index.

B3 also opened BC1, a calendar spread that rolls a position from one expiry to the next.

The older contract, BIT, is quoted in reais per bitcoin and also covers 0.01 bitcoin. Its minimum move is R$20 (US$3.91).

That is the main difference between the two. A BIT price mixes bitcoin’s move with the real–dollar rate, while BTC strips the currency out.

What the Brazil market moves show about foreign appetite

Two of the three steps involve foreign firms. Blockchain Capital and Franklin Templeton are both American, while B3 is the Brazilian exchange itself.

The NG.CASH announcement gives a reason in plain terms. It says venture firms are increasingly looking past a crowded US market toward large markets such as Brazil.

“Brazil is exactly the kind of market we believe will produce them,” said Kinjal Shah, a general partner at Blockchain Capital. She was speaking about category-defining fintech companies.

Three announcements in three days do not make a trend. They do show two large American firms choosing Brazil’s regulated market in the same week.

Why this matters for expats and investors in Latin America

For foreign residents in Brazil, the Franklin receipts are the most practical change. They let you hold US, Indian, Taiwanese, bitcoin and ether exposure in reais through a local broker.

Franklin Templeton has not published the fees charged on the Brazilian receipts. The underlying US fund USPX charges 0.03% a year, and a local wrapper can add costs.

For traders, the BTC contract takes the currency element out of a bitcoin position. That helps if you think in dollars, though margin and leverage rules still apply.

Brazil has had listed crypto funds since 2021, earlier than its neighbours. Other foreign managers have added products since.

What is not known

NG.CASH did not name a round stage or any investor besides Blockchain Capital. It gave no date for a decision on its crypto licence.

Fees on the Franklin receipts have not been published. B3 has not reported how much the new bitcoin contract has traded since Monday.

The next hard numbers will come from B3’s volume data and the central bank’s licence decisions.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did NG.CASH raise, and who led it?

NG.CASH said on 23 September 2026 that it raised US$15 million in a strategic investment led by Blockchain Capital. Total funding since 2021 now passes US$65 million.

Which Franklin Templeton funds now trade on B3?

Five depositary receipts: EZBC for bitcoin, EZET for ether, USPX for US shares, FLTW for Taiwan and FTIN for India. They are quoted in reais and marked for qualified investors.

How does B3’s new bitcoin future differ from the old one?

BTC is quoted in US dollars per bitcoin, while BIT is quoted in reais. Both cover 0.01 bitcoin and settle in cash on the last Friday of the month.

Sources: NG.CASH announcement via PR Newswire, 23 September 2026; B3 circulars 059/2026-VPC and 039/2026-PRE and B3 trading-session notices; B3 Bora Investir; Franklin Templeton fund documents; Valor Econômico.

World.title: Colombia Clearing House Stake Rises to 75.28 Percent
World.content:
COLOMBIA · BUSINESS

Key Facts — What happened The Bogota exchange raised its holding in the country’s central clearing house to 75.28 percent.

— How much It bought 522,694,382 shares from Banco de Bogotá, adding 1.02 percentage points.

— Who holds what 54.88 percent is held directly and 20.41 percent through the Deceval depository.

— Why it matters The Colombia clearing house stands between buyers and sellers in every trade it handles.

— The catch No price was disclosed, and no fresh approval from the financial regulator was needed.

— Also this week A supermarket banking report involving Davivienda still has no company statement behind it.

The Bogota exchange bought a small block of shares from Banco de Bogotá and tightened its hold on the market’s risk hub.

Banco de Bogotá sold the shares that lifted the exchange’s clearing-house stake

One-stop reference Company Intelligence Every listed company in Latin America — financials, ownership and structure for 1,450+ companies across 26 exchanges, in one place. Browse the directory →

The Bolsa de Valores de Colombia has lifted its Colombia clearing house stake to 75.28 percent of the share capital. It bought 522,694,382 shares from Banco de Bogotá and told the financial regulator on Monday 21 September 2026.

What the exchange actually bought

Colombia’s financial regulator, the Superintendencia Financiera, received a notice from the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia on 21 September 2026. The exchange said it had bought 522,694,382 shares in the Cámara de Riesgo Central de Contraparte de Colombia.

The seller was Banco de Bogotá, the flagship bank of the Grupo Aval group. The purchase added 1.02 percentage points to the exchange’s holding.

The exchange now holds 54.88 percent directly, or 28,135,127,626 shares. A further 20.41 percent sits with Deceval, its securities depository subsidiary.

Together that comes to 75.28 percent of the clearing house. Neither company published the price paid.

What a clearing house does, in plain words

A central counterparty steps into the middle of a trade once a buyer and a seller have agreed a price. It becomes the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer.

So if one side fails to pay or deliver, the other still gets what it is owed. The clearing house takes the hit and chases the money.

To make that safe it collects collateral, known as margin, from its members every day. It also nets trades, so far less cash has to move.

In Colombia that job belongs to the Cámara de Riesgo Central de Contraparte. It clears standard derivatives, swaps, government bonds, dollar trades and shares.

Why owning the Colombia clearing house matters

The Colombia clearing house is quiet plumbing, but it is where market risk is measured and pooled. Its rulebook decides who may clear and how much collateral they post.

At the end of 2025 the open positions it stood behind reached a record 368 trillion pesos (US$115 billion), counting both sides. Currency figures here use 23 September 2026 rates, about 3,200 pesos to the dollar.

An owner holding three quarters of the shares has a strong voice on fees, access rules and technology. That voice is not unlimited, because the rulebook and the regulator still bind the board.

The exchange already controlled the clearing house before this purchase and registered that control with the Bogota chamber of commerce. The exchange itself belongs to nuam, the holding company merging the Santiago, Lima and Colombia markets.

The regulator’s role, and what it did not approve

Colombian law normally makes a buyer ask the Superintendencia Financiera before taking 10 percent or more of a supervised company. The regulator weighs the buyer’s record, standing and suitability.

The exchange said this deal fell under the exception in article 88, paragraph three, of the financial system statute. That exception covers a buyer already cleared by the regulator within the previous three years.

Such a buyer must also have a clean disciplinary record and must notify the regulator before trading. On that basis, no new approval was required this time.

An earlier round of buying, which took the direct holding to 55.98 percent, did carry the regulator’s authorisation. The exchange filed a similar share-purchase notice on 5 August 2026.

The Davivienda and Éxito supermarket report

A second Colombian banking story this week rests on much thinner ground. On 23 September 2026 the broadcaster Red+ Noticias said Davivienda customers can use Grupo Éxito supermarket tills as banking agents.

It named Éxito, Carulla, Surtimax, Super Inter and Surtimayorista stores. Grupo Éxito ran 463 stores in Colombia at the end of March 2026.

The report said shoppers can withdraw cash from Davivienda or DaviPlata accounts and pay loan instalments at the till. It listed a cap of 9,000,000 pesos (US$2,813) per transaction at Éxito.

Neither Davivienda nor Grupo Éxito has published a statement. No launch date, contract or fee schedule has been made public by either company.

Supermarket tills acting as bank agents are not new here. Grupo Aval’s banks began doing this in Éxito stores in 2010, and Bancolombia followed in 2016.

What this means for expats and investors

If you hold Colombian shares or bonds, this clearing house is what makes your trade complete. Tighter single ownership can speed decisions, but it also concentrates them in one board.

Fees and collateral rules set there feed through to what your broker charges. The clearing house publishes its own circulars, which are a better guide than headlines.

For people living in Colombia, the supermarket story would matter more day to day. Until the two companies confirm it, treat the details as unconfirmed.

The price of the share purchase has not been disclosed, and Banco de Bogotá has not said why it sold. The terms and start date of any Davivienda arrangement are also unknown.

The exchange’s next filings, and any word from the two companies, should answer both questions soon enough.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does a central counterparty clearing house do?

It steps between the two sides of a trade. It becomes the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, so one default does not spread.

Did the Superintendencia Financiera approve this purchase?

No fresh approval was needed. The exchange relied on a legal exception for buyers already cleared within the previous three years, and filed notice on 21 September 2026.

Can Davivienda customers bank at Éxito tills today?

One Colombian broadcaster says yes, for withdrawals and loan payments. Neither Davivienda nor Grupo Éxito has confirmed it, so ask in store before relying on it.

Sources: Bolsa de Valores de Colombia relevant-information filing to the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, 21 September 2026; Cámara de Riesgo Central de Contraparte 2025 management report; Estatuto Orgánico del Sistema Financiero, article 88; La República; Valora Analitik; Red+ Noticias; Grupo Éxito first-quarter 2026 results.

World.title: Ecuador Curfew and Industrial Power Plan Are Two Separate Orders
World.content:
ECUADOR · SECURITY AND ENERGY

Key Facts — The Ecuador curfew Decree 498 suspends movement from 00:00 to 05:00 in El Oro, Guayas, Los Ríos and Manabí.

— How long The night restriction runs from 17 to 30 September 2026, inside a 60-day state of exception.

— The arrests Interior Minister John Reimberg said 901 people were held for crimes in the first week.

— The power order The energy ministry told 185 high-voltage industrial users to cut grid use one working day a week.

— Why power Water at the Mazar reservoir has fallen fast, and the government wants it to last until December.

— The catch The two orders share no legal link, and neither authority has said one caused the other.

One order is about crime. The other is about water in a reservoir. They are not the same policy.

Guayaquil, in one of the four provinces under the night curfew
