World.title: Iraq’s exports hit $19.55 billion in Q1 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Figures released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) showed that the country’s exports reached $19.55 billion in the first quarter of 2026, compared to imports of $10.27 billion.

Hydrocarbons continued to account for the significant bulk of Iraq’s exports, exposing the country to larger global energy dynamics.

Iraq’s crude oil exports totaled $18.64 billion, petroleum products $762.2 million, and other exports $148.5 million.

The state sector’s imports totaled $1.35 billion, and the private sector’s imports reached $8.92 billion, according to the National Iraqi News Agency (NINA).

Iraq’s trade balance indicated a surplus of $10.82 billion, according to figures from the CBI that compare exports with imports.

The country’s exports during the first quarter of 2026 are lower than those of the fourth quarter of 2025, which stood at $21.62 billion.

Iraq’s export capacity during the first quarter of 2026 experienced significant headwinds due to rigorous OPEC+ production limits and interruptions related to maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Golan will remain Syrian, vows President al-Sharaa at UN
World.content:
United Nations – Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa insisted at the UN Wednesday that the Golan Heights region will remain Syrian after Colombia last month recognized Israeli sovereignty over the strategically important territory.

“Any attempts that violate our sovereignty, violate international law, will be stopped. Golan will remain Syrian territories,” al-Sharaa said at the UN meeting of world leaders in New York.

Colombia’s new hard-right government in August recognized Israel’s claim over the Golan Heights, which it captured from Syria in 1967.

The United States had until then been the only country to recognize Israel’s annexation of the territory in 1981.

The United Nations maintains that the plateau is Syrian territory under Israeli military occupation.

In July UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres reiterated that the Golan Heights were part of Syria, describing Israeli occupation as “totally unacceptable.”

Al-Sharaa also used his second turn at the UN rostrum to denounce repeated Israeli strikes on his country since the fall of former dictator Bashar al-Assad.

“Israel is launching attacks against Syria. There have been 500 air strikes, more than 1,200 incursions, and 300 detentions. This is at odds with the orientation we’re seeing at global level,” he said.

“It is reminiscent of a era that we thought was long gone.”

World.title: Iraq urges Iran to defuse regional tensions through dialogue
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized to his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, on Wednesday the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.

Hussein’s remarks took place during his meeting with Araghchi in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.

Hussein stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension, prevent escalation, and maintain regional stability.

Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.

The two sides discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.

The two ministers emphasized the importance of supporting diplomatic efforts aimed at preventing escalation, defusing tensions, and fostering opportunities for dialog and peaceful solutions.

World.title: China’s Yu, 13, wins third gold with latest Asian Games record
World.content:
Tokyo – China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a hat-trick of Asian Games golds on Wednesday with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, two years out from the Los Angeles Olympics.

The school girl powered home in an Asian Games-record 4min 28.56sec to make it a clean sweep from her three individual events in Tokyo, following victories in the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, also in Games-record times.

She beat the previous 400m IM Games record set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014 by almost 4.5 seconds.

It was the fourth-fastest time in the world this year, with world record-holder Summer McIntosh owning the top three.

Yu is shaping up to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

She has been the talk of swimming since becoming the youngest medallist in world championships history last year with bronze for China’s relay team aged just 12.

She also finished just outside the medals in fourth in three world individual events.

She has embellished her growing reputation this year, notably with a victory over multiple American Olympic champion Regan Smith in March.

She has dominated this week in Tokyo and gave another glimpse of her immense talent in the 400m IM.

Yu took the lead straight from the start and set off on a procession towards the finish line.

She finished 3.95sec clear of silver medallist Ke Wenxi of China, with Japan’s Mio Narita finishing third.

As well as international news headlines, her Asian Games exploits have caused a sensation back home.

Her back story, such as being spotted by chance by a swimming coach at a water park, and her struggle with interviews, have gone viral.

Asked if answering questions was the hardest part, she replied with a giggle this week: “Every time I just want to float off somewhere else.”

World.title: China’s Xi heads to US for talks with Trump: state media
World.content:
Beijing – China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald Trump, state media said.

The highly anticipated talks come as the two countries confront rising fears about increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems, and as both sides look to ease tensions on trade.

Xi “left Beijing by special plane”, accompanied by his wife Peng Liyuan, his right-hand man Cai Qi, and foreign minister Wang Yi, among others, state broadcaster CCTV said.

Trump is due to personally meet Xi on his arrival at Joint Base Andrews, before their meetings on Thursday, according to the White House.

The US leader was greeted by China’s vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.

Xi and Peng will attend a ceremony at the White House on Thursday morning, which will include a military flyover.

The two leaders are due to hold talks and Trump is set to host Xi for a state dinner at the White House in the evening.

The visit will wrap up on Friday morning where the two presidential couples will have tea at the White House then visit the National Archives to round out the trip.

The White House said that the visit marks “a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries.”

But the meeting between the two leaders could touch on multiple points of tension, with Trump telling reporters that he will be “discussing almost everything” with Xi.

Trump’s Iran war casts a long shadow, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran — despite reports that Beijing supplied Tehran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.

A trade war is of even greater concern and the world’s two largest economies are still seeking to mitigate the fallout from Trump’s global tariffs.

The threat of war over the island of Taiwan — which China claims as its territory — looms large as well.

– Leverage –

Analysts, however, have tempered expectations by cautioning there might not be many concrete deals announced.

Preliminary talks between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns, but released little in the way of detail.

Bessant said at the time that the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”

“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.

The son of jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai made an appeal to Xi from Washington that his 78-year-old father be released.

Trump said in May, however, that he had discussed Lai’s fate with Xi and his release was unlikely.

But Beijing did release the founder of an underground church, Ezra Jin, after Trump raised his case with Xi.

China’s negotiating arsenal includes its dominance in the supply of rare earths, critical materials used for high-tech products that are vital to US manufacturers.

Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths.

World.title: Iraq to restructure financial policy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi confirmed on Tuesday that the government is moving forward with restructuring the country’s financial policy.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Director of the Middle East and Central Asia Department at the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Jihad Azour, on the sidelines of his participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, which opened on Tuesday in New York.

The meeting addressed developments in the global economy and the repercussions of the crisis currently affecting the region, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The discussions also addressed the effects on markets, supply chains, and inflation rates, in addition to the impacts on energy consumption and oil prices.

Al-Zaidi highlighted that the government is focused on expanding automation systems and is gradually shifting toward a program-and-performance-based budget as part of the 2027 budget initiative.

Azour reaffirmed the IMF’s willingness to continue working with Iraq and support the path of economic and fiscal reforms, contributing to the country’s financial and economic stability.

The IMF projected in July that the Iraqi economy will be the most hit by oil and transportation disruptions in the Middle East and Central Asia in 2026.

The IMF also predicted a robust economic rebound in 2027, when energy market conditions improve and commerce resumes.

The anticipated fall in 2026 will mainly result from the disruption in oil production and distribution, especially by countries that depend heavily on energy exports, but the recovery in 2027 will be brought about by a reduction of these shocks and resumption of business activities.

World.title: Central Integrity Court sentences MP Alia Nassif to seven years for illicit gains
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court sentenced sitting lawmaker Alia Nassif Jasim to seven years of imprisonment on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, after convicting her of illicit enrichment and ordering the restitution of over 61 billion Iraqi dinars alongside an equivalent financial fine.

According to an official statement issued by the Federal Commission of Integrity, the judicial ruling was delivered in person under the provisions of Article 19, Paragraph 2, of the amended Commission of Integrity and Illicit Gains Law No. 30 of 2011.

The judicial ruling mandates that the convicted parliamentarian return the entire proven value of the illicit enrichment, which encompasses 14,239,590,000 Iraqi dinars and 12,442,500 U.S. dollars, which collectively exceed 61 billion Iraqi dinars at current valuation metrics.

Pursuant to Article 19, Paragraph 4, of the integrity statute, the court also imposed an equal financial fine matching the full restitution amount, effectively doubling the monetary penalty levied against the lawmaker.

The court handed down an additional sentence of three years of rigorous imprisonment against Nassif for concealing assets and falsifying mandatory financial disclosure declarations under Article 19, Paragraph 5, ordering the application of the heavier seven-year custodial sentence in accordance with penal procedure standards.

Judicial authorities simultaneously upheld freezing orders placed on all her movable and immovable assets and granted the Federal Commission of Integrity the explicit legal right to claim additional civil damages once the ruling attains final, irrevocable status.

World.title: Hadjar extends Red Bull contract for 2027 F1 season
World.content:
Paris – Frenchman Isack Hadjar will continue to partner Max Verstappen at Red Bull for the 2027 Formula One season, the team announced on Wednesday.

The 21-year-old has impressed in his debut year at the team after being promoted following a strong rookie campaign with its junior outfit Racing Bulls in 2025.

Hadjar has missed the last three races with a wrist injury, but still sits eighth in the drivers’ standings with 71 points.

He posted a run of seven consecutive top-six finishes, including a podium in Monaco, before being sidelined.

“There are so many talented people at the factory, and you’re aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max,” Hadjar said in a statement.

“I’ve been able to justify the faith they’ve had in me. I’m constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead.”

Hadjar will return to action this weekend at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Partnering Verstappen, who recently extended his contract until 2030, at Red Bull has proved a tough job for several other drivers in recent seasons.

Sergio Perez was dropped after finishing 285 points behind the Dutchman in 2024, while Liam Lawson was axed after just two races last year and replaced by Yuki Tsunoda.

“He (Hadjar) has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula One season, which made extending his contract an easy decision,” said Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies.

“The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can’t wait to see him back out on track.”

The vessel had 20 Indian seafarers on board, with the surviving crew evacuated by the Royal Navy of Oman and brought ashore.Sonowal said directions had been issued to maritime authorities to coordinate with Omani authorities and the ship management company for the immediate and safe repatriation of the surviving Indian crew.âThe government will ensure that the mortal remains of Suraj Yadav are brought home with full dignity, and every possible support is extended to his next of kin,â Sonowal said.The ministry of external affairs condemned the attack and said continuing incidents targeting commercial shipping in the region were âdeeply worrisomeâ.âOf the 20 Indian seafarers on board, 19 have been rescued, while 1 Indian national tragically lost his life.We offer our deepest condolences to the family of the deceased,â the MEA said.The ministry said its embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with Omani authorities for the early repatriation of the Indian seafarers. India has been pushing for dialogue

Black Sea shipping remains key concern

Russia yet to back proposals

India has emerged as one of the countries whose proposals are being considered for restoring safe commercial shipping in the Black Sea, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying Egypt, India and Turkey have outlined options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine.Speaking to leaders at the United Nations on Wednesday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to support a maritime truce based on the proposals and that Russia now needed to respond.âWe are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere,â Zelenskyy said.The remarks came at Ukraine's Crimean Platform summit on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, ahead of a UN Security Council meeting on Russia's war in Ukraine.The reference to India's role comes amid New Delhi's efforts to remain engaged with both Moscow and Kyiv and encourage an end to the conflict.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said earlier this month that India had been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and was exploring ideas that could contribute to mitigating and eventually ending the war.âWhat we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict,â Jaishankar said during his visit to Warsaw.Jaishankar has also said India's position is that the conflict should end through dialogue and diplomacy.During his visit to Kyiv earlier this month, he met Zelenskyy and Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha, with discussions including possible approaches to ending the conflict.âIf India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there,â Jaishankar said in Kyiv.According to Reuters, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Turkey had proposed options to restore safe navigation for merchant vessels in the Black Sea, where cargo movements have been severely disrupted by attacks on ships and port infrastructure by both sides.Ukraine has been seeking ceasefires covering attacks on energy infrastructure as well as shipping in the Black Sea. Kyiv has also expressed concern that Russia could target power and heating facilities with missiles and drones during the winter.The disruption has also affected countries dependent on grain supplies from the Black Sea region. Reuters reported that wheat importers in Asia, the Middle East and Africa have faced difficulties securing supplies, while global wheat prices have risen.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to ensure safe shipping and food security if Russia was prepared to take steps towards de-escalation.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said after meeting Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov on Wednesday that both Russia and Ukraine had expressed interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy.The Kremlin has not publicly backed the proposals.Ahead of the Rubio-Lavrov meeting, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there were currently no grounds for broader peace talks, while maintaining that Russia remained open to negotiations.âFor now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks,â Peskov said.Zelenskyy also said he was ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump.The latest developments come as India continues its diplomatic engagement with both sides.Jaishankar met US secretary of state Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Wednesday and discussed the Ukraine situation, as well as India's concerns over the US Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.

World.title: 'Judiciary plays second fiddle to govt in judges' appointment’: SC Justice Datta defends collegium system
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Describing the argument that âjudges appoint judgesâ as a "myth,"

Justice Dipankar Dutta said on Wednesday that the judiciary, in fact, plays âsecond fiddleâ to the government in the appointment of judges.

âThis court is left to wonder why, even after the judiciary has been relegated to playing second fiddle to the executive in the matter of appointment of judges, is there still a clamour to induct an outsider at the stage of selection,â PTI quoted Justice Dipankar Datta as saying. According to the judge, the argument, coming from the executive, was a âfeeble attempt to deflect attention from its own dereliction and failureâ, rejecting the governmentâs attempt to draw a parallel between the absence of an âoutsiderâ in the collegium system of judicial appointments and the CJI's removal from the three-member Election Commission appointment panel headed by the prime minister.

To underscore his âsecond fiddleâ argument, Justice Dipankar Datta pointed to the governmentâs âselectiveâ implementation of collegium resolutions, saying this undermines their sanctity. While acknowledging that the government approves a majority of the names recommended by the collegium, he noted that at least one is invariably withheld.

âThe sanctity of a collegium resolution is lost each time the executive implements it selectively, albeit approving the majority of those recommended while withholding at least one.





Undeterred by such peaceful approvals and regardless of the fate of those not cleared by the executive, the collegium chooses to proceed seemingly to avoid a head-on conflict with the executive, and is left with the option to keep the institution running.

The collegium thereby avoids a constitutional crisis,â Justice Datta said.

On the âsweeping generalisationâ that the collegium acts as a âlaw unto itself,â Justice Datta pointed to the detailed consultative process involved in judicial appointments, including the roles played by the central and state governments, intelligence agencies and other bodies in vetting credentials.

He also noted that every appointment involves the formal â and final â approval of the President of India.

âIt has become fashionable nowadays to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice, conveniently forgetting that aberrations are exceptions and not the norm, and that no system can guarantee infallibility of human choice. The uninitiated and the unversed unknowingly have thus been made to believe that the collegium of the Supreme Court and the collegium of the high courts comprise judges, who appoint judges,â Justice Datta stated.

âDespite all its opacity and imperfections, the collegium system still remains the most viable option for safeguarding independence, as envisioned under Article 50 of the Constitution by its framers,â he added.

Justice Datta made the observations in a split verdict delivered by a bench that also comprised Justice Satish Chandra Sharma.

The bench was hearing a batch of petitions challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the Chief Justice of India from the panel responsible for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

World.title: Jaishankar 'reiterates India’s interests & concerns’ over Russia sanctions act in talks with Rubio
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar brought up Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA) in a meeting with US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Wednesday.

The two officials met on the sideline of United Nations General Assembly session.

"Good to meet Secretary Rubio of the US. Reiterated Indiaâs interests and concerns with regard to SRIA.

Also discussed the Gulf and Ukraine situations," said Jaishankar in a statement on X.

Rubio also confirmed the meeting on X mentioning the bilateral ties. "Great to meet with Indian External Affairs Minister in New York today. Together, we are building on the US-India strategic partnership and coordinating on key regional priorities and upcoming multilateral efforts."

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, signed by US President Donald Trump, expands Washingtonâs powers to impose sanctions and tariffs on Russia and countries that continue significant purchases of Russian oil and gas. A key provision gives the president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from the five largest importers of Russian petroleum or natural gas, subject to conditions in the law.

World.title: EC 'dissent' row: Opposition seeks CEC's arrest, fresh polls in states; BJP lauds 'pure democracy' - top developments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The reported objections raised by two Election Commissioners to decisions linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls triggered a major political confrontation on Wednesday, with opposition parties demanding action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.

The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically rather than under a âdictatorialâ system.

The political row followed a media report which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process and electoral rolls.

The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that the reported objections indicated a breakdown in its functioning.

It said differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations and maintained that its decisions, including those concerning SIR, had been taken unanimously.

Opposition demands CEC's removal, arrest

Opposition parties, which have been criticising the EC over the SIR exercise, seized on the report to renew their demands for action against Gyanesh Kumar.





Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reiterated his âvote choriâ allegation against the Election Commission, describing it as âa crime against the people of Indiaâ and an attack on the Constitution.

âThe BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,â Rae Bareli MP said.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said 73 Opposition Rajya Sabha MPs had submitted a fresh notice on April 24, seeking Kumar's removal.

He questioned whether the Rajya Sabha chairman would decide on the pending notice since the Monsoon Session of Parliament had not yet been prorogued.

Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal went further, demanding that Kumar be removed and arrested.

âGyanesh Kumar should be immediately sacked and jailed,â Thackeray said.

He also demanded that the last elections in Maharashtra, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu be nullified and fresh polls held in the three states using ballot papers.

Kejriwal demanded that the entire SIR exercise be cancelled, all changes made under it be reversed and the voter list from three years ago be restored. He also called for Kumar's arrest and registration of a sedition case against him.

TMC MP Derek O'Brien said, âImpeach CEC to save democracy.â

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also demanded Kumar's arrest and said he had âno moral authority to continueâ.

âThis is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and the BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,â Banerjee said.

Fresh polls demanded in Bihar, West Bengal

The Opposition's demands also extended to fresh elections in states where polls have already taken place.

RJD leader and Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav demanded fresh elections in Bihar and West Bengal, alleging that the electoral mandates in the two states had been compromised through electoral fraud and institutional manipulation.

âThe opposition did not lose elections on the ground; the results were orchestrated by PM Modi and Amit Shah. In 2020, we were defeated through manipulation, and the same script was executed in 2025. Voter lists were purged, money was distributed, and counting was manipulated. The electoral outcomes in Bihar and Bengal are fraudulent, and we demand that fresh, transparent elections be held,â he said.

Yadav also questioned changes to the rules governing the preservation of voting and counting records, alleging that the period had been reduced from one year to 45 days.

He said this could make it difficult for parties to approach courts without access to election-related evidence.

DMK president M K Stalin demanded Kumar's resignation and an immediate halt to the SIR exercise. He also sought a fair probe âinto everything that transpired within the EC and those responsible should be held accountableâ, according to news agency PTI.

Stalin alleged that the report had raised doubts about the results of Assembly elections held after the SIR exercise and said his party had consistently opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls in the name of SIR.

Akhilesh, Omar question EC functioning

Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said governments formed during a period when the Election Commission was not functioning impartially were âunconstitutionalâ.

âThis means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,â Yadav said.

He alleged that interference in the poll panel amounted to âtramplingâ democracy and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.

Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said the Centre and the Election Commission needed to take corrective steps to prevent people from losing faith in elections.

âCorrective action needs to be taken somewhere. Otherwise, if people lose faith in elections, what remains of a democracy? Elections are the very foundations of a democracy. If people lose faith in elections, why would they even participate in them? I feel the Election Commission and the government of India need to reflect on this,â Abdullah said.

He also said the report raised questions about the functioning of the poll panel and referred to his earlier concerns over the electoral process.

BJP says EC differences show âpure democracyâ

The BJP rejected the Opposition's allegations and defended the reported differences between the Election Commissioners.

Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said differing views during official deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically.

âThe media reports saying that the election commissioners shared differing views in official deliberations is a reflection of pure democracy,â Patra said.

âIf there is no communication and exchange of views among the election commissioners who conduct polls, the opposition parties would allege 'dictatorship' and call them 'yes men' of the government,â he said.

Patra said the Election Commission's response showed that neither the poll panel nor other constitutional bodies were functioning under a âdictatorial ruleâ.

âThis shows that the Election Commission (EC) and all other constitutional bodies are functioning in a democratic manner and upholding the democracy of the country,â he said.

EC says all decisions were unanimous

Responding to the media report, the Election Commission said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body.

âThe ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions.

The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour,â it said.

The commission said all official orders, decisions and administrative directions carried full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures.

It added that operational queries or inputs raised by members during the drafting stage were part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights and improving electoral processes.

The EC further said differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberation before a final decision was taken.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âNot only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorised to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system,â it said.

The commission said focusing on specific internal notes and observations over 10 months while overlooking its wider body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives presented only one part of the picture.

It said it had taken numerous decisions, issued instructions and introduced around 40 new initiatives and electoral reforms, including electoral-roll revision and SIR across the country.

âAll these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year,â the EC said.

The commission also pointed to the conduct of elections in Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal during the period and said it remained committed to carrying out its constitutional duties.

World.title: 'Unwarranted': India rejects OIC's Kashmir references, slams outfit for giving platform to Pakistan
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit back at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) over references to Jammu and Kashmir in a joint communique of its Contact Group, calling them âunwarranted and factually incorrectâ and asserting that the grouping has no locus standi to comment on matters that are strictly internal to India.

The ministry of external affairs said the entire Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are an âintegral and inalienable part of Indiaâ, adding that âno amount of repetition of politically motivated propaganda can change this realityâ.

The response came after Pakistanâs foreign ministry said on X that deputy prime minister and foreign minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar had addressed a ministerial meeting of the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.

According to Pakistan, Dar urged OIC member states to maintain a âunified positionâ on Jammu and Kashmir at the United Nations and other international fora. He also reiterated Pakistanâs commitment to a âjust and peaceful settlement of the dispute in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the wishes of the Kashmiri peopleâ.

The references to Jammu and Kashmir drew a strong response from New Delhi.





âIndia categorically rejects the unwarranted and factually incorrect references to India in the Joint Communique of the so-called OIC Contact Group on Jammu & Kashmir. The OIC has no locus standi to pronounce on matters that are strictly internal to India,â the MEA said in a statement.

âRepeated endorsement of such motivated narratives only raises serious questions on the credibility of OIC,â the MEA said.

India further turned its focus on Pakistan, saying the OIC should address terrorism emanating from Pakistani territory instead of providing Islamabad a platform for what New Delhi called âfabricated and motivated propagandaâ.

âInstead of offering a platform to Pakistan to peddle its fabricated and motivated propaganda, OIC will be better advised to counsel Pakistan, which has a well-documented record of supporting and sponsoring terrorism, to look inwards and address the continuing threat of terrorism emanating from territories under its control,â the MEA said.

An Israeli soldier accused of alleged war crimes in Gaza has left India weeks after the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF), a Palestinian rights group, filed a criminal complaint against him, according to a report by Middle East Eye.The soldier, whose identity has not been made public, left India in mid-September, a lawyer familiar with the case told Middle East Eye. It remains unclear whether the complaint influenced his departure or whether he left after completing his holiday.The development comes amid renewed calls for countries to uphold international law. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, speaking on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Monday, said multilateralism works best when international law, rules and norms are "scrupulously observed".The latest case marks the second incident this year in which the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF) has identified an Israeli soldier travelling in India and filed a complaint against him.In June, the Brussels-based organisation approached Indian authorities seeking the arrest of Eitan Gilboa, an Israeli military reservist who was vacationing in Himachal Pradesh. HRF accused Gilboa, who was identified as a member of the Israeli military's 271st Combat Engineering Battalion, of involvement in the demolition of civilian buildings in Khan Younis and Rafah.According to reports, HRF submitted material, including geolocated videos, social media posts and chain-of-command documentation to Indian authorities. Gilboa was subsequently traced by pro-Palestinian activists to locations including Old Manali and Gondla in Himachal Pradesh before leaving India.The latest case has followed a similar sequence, with HRF identifying an Israeli soldier through publicly available information, filing a complaint with Indian authorities and the individual subsequently leaving the country.India has long been a popular destination for young Israelis after their mandatory military service. Many undertake an extended post-service trip, commonly known as "tiul gadol", which can last several months.The trend has also contributed to the informal "Hummus Trail" followed by Israeli travellers across several Indian destinations, including Kasol, Dharamkot, Goa, Hampi, Gokarna, Kodaikanal, Rishikesh, Varanasi and Pushkar.Tourism has also featured in India-Israel bilateral cooperation. In February 2026, Israel allocated 4 million shekels for initiatives aimed at strengthening tourism ties with India.The HRF has increasingly sought to pursue legal complaints against Israeli military personnel over alleged conduct during Israel's military campaign in Gaza. The organisation's complaints have also brought attention to the presence of former and serving Israeli military personnel travelling in countries including India.Israel launched its military campaign in Gaza following the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel on October 7, 2023.

World.title: DKS writes to PM seeking immediate interim drought relief
World.content:
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighting the worsening drought situation in Karnataka, with 177 taluks now declared drought-affected and the situation likely to intensify in the coming months.

In the light of the grim situation, Mr. Shivakumar has sought immediate interim drought relief of 50% of the sum sought in an earlier memorandum to the tune of ₹ 3,705.30 crore, pending completion of the formal assessment process by a Central team. He has also sought advance release of the Central share of the second instalment of State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF).

Mr. Shivakumar has said that large-scale crop losses, likely exceeding 40 lakh hectares, is predicted in Karnataka.

"This support will help Karnataka undertake immediate relief measures for crop losses, drinking water supply, livestock protection and other essential interventions,” he has said in the letter, stating that the the prolonged rainfall deficit has severely impacted the rural economy.

World.title: MLA demands hike of ₹10 a litre in milk procurement price to help drought-hit farmers in Karnataka
World.content:
Congress member K.Y. Nanje Gowda, who is also chairman of Kolar-Chickballapur Milk Union Limited (KOMUL), on Wednesday urged the government to increase the procurement price of milk being sold by KMF by ₹10 per litre to provide succour to drought-hit milk producers.

Participating in a debate in the Assembly on drought, Mr. Gowda cautioned that the KMF’s brand value and the milk cooperative network in the State would take a hit if milk procurement price was not hiked.

Production costs

He explained that the production cost of milk had increased sharply over the years while the drought had added to woes of the dairy sector. “The cost of cattle feed has increased from ₹720 per 50-kg bag to ₹1,250 now. It is almost impossible for farmers now to get either green or dry fodder owing to the drought. In such a scenario, how do you expect milk producers to survive by selling milk at such non-remunerative prices?” he wondered.

Also, the procurement and the selling prices of milk by KMF in Karnataka are cheaper compared to other States, he pointed out. He said while the milk procurement price per litre stood at ₹35 in Karnataka, it was ₹41.5 in Andhra Pradesh, ₹41.8 in Keralam, and ₹41 in Maharashtra, he said. The average procurement prices of milk in the country is about ₹41 per litre.

Question of quality

Discounting the argument that consumers would be burdened if the procurement price of milk was increased, Mr. Gowda maintained that consumers should realise that they would not get access to quality and affordable milk if the farmers’ interests are not protected.

In fact, the KMF’s milk selling price in Karnataka that stood at ₹46 a litre was lower compared to other States, he said. The price per litre was ₹67 in Andhra Pradesh, ₹52 in Keralam, ₹59 in Maharashtra, and ₹61 in Delhi.

Milk rejected by the KMF’s procurement units owing to low quality was being procured by private milk companies and being sold at prices higher than the KMF’s selling price, he alleged.

Pointing out that educated youth were returning to villages to take up dairying, he appealed to the government to help retain them in the sector through an increase in procurement prices.

He further appealed to the government to provide a special drought package to Kolar district considering the fact that the impact of drought on this parched district would be more.

World.title: The Hindu Sustainability Summit: ‘Treat waste water as an economic resource’
World.content:
It was Chennai’s acute water shortage of 1980 that proved to be a turning point for Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL)’s attitude towards used water, pivoting from dependence on Metro Water towards the principles of reduce, reuse and recycle, according to P. Kannan, CPCL’s Director (Operations).

He was one of the senior corporates and experts pitching for wastewater to be treated as a valuable economic resources at The Hindu Sustainability Summit 2026 on Wednesday (September 23, 2026). The discussion on ‘Reimagining Water Management for a Circular Future’ was moderated by K. Lakshmi, Deputy Editor, The Hindu.

“We have optimised our water requirements and taken several measures to reduce consumption. For reuse, the water is diverted to our processing units, and wherever possible, we have maximised our reuse capability. As part of our recycling efforts, we are also producing 480 tonnes of steam,” Mr. Kannan said.

Replacing fresh water with treated water

Indian Oil Corporation Limited is another oil major that is changing the way it operates. “We operate nine refineries. Geographically, there are certain things that you cannot avoid. Refineries that are located inland face challenges in reducing their water footprint. We have been recycling almost 90% to 91% of our wastewater, but we are not stopping there,” said IOCL executive director Mukesh Mohan.

“We are looking at replacing fresh water used in our process units with treated water from sewage treatment plants (STPs) in the city. In big cities such as Vadodara and Guwahati, and at refineries in Mathura and Panipat, we have clear, concrete plans to partly replace our fresh water intake with STP treated water,” Mr. Mohan added. For this, he noted, the support of the municipality is required, and the STP has to be designed to treat wastewater from nearby households and industrial units.

The myth about desalination

Rajiv Mittal, chairman and managing director of VA TECH WABAG Limited, said that fresh water is not an answer to everything. “We have a huge coastline in Chennai. Why are we not using seawater? You don’t want to drink recycled wastewater, but why not use seawater?” he asked. “There is a myth that desalinating seawater is expensive. I believe the management of water is more important. And we should have the responsibility to conserve water,” he added.

Mr. Mittal said untreated water should not be allowed to flow out. “The only way to make this possible is to treat wastewater as an economic resource. If you give wastewater the tag of an economic resource, people will treat it differently. You don’t throw your money onto the streets, so you will not throw wastewater onto the streets or into the nalas. You will collect it, treat it and generate wealth from it.” he explained.

Monitoring groundwater

Rajesh Nair, a professor in the Department of Ocean Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology, Madras, highlighted how they are deriving geothermal energy from the sub-surface of the earth. “We are into India’s first project to derive geothermal energy from unused oil and gas wells... the ones that have been depleted,” he said.

Mr. Nair added that groundwater quality needs to be assessed and different grades should be established. He stressed the need to monitor how groundwater conditions are changing over time, adding that greater attention needs to be given to conserving wetlands.

“We need data integration and digital data analysis. Only when we have data can we manage things effectively. We should use Internet of Things (IoT) and AI-based solutions and integrate them under a common platform or a single body that can provide clear directions on what water should be used for what purpose, how much water needs to be recharged into the groundwater system, and so on. That way, we can manage our water resources much more effectively,” Mr. Nair said.

World.title: Clamour against Collegium feeble attempt to hide government ‘dereliction and failure’, says Justice Datta
World.content:
Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Datta on Wednesday (September 23, 2026) lashed out at critics in the Union government who claim that the Collegium system of judicial appointment is an insular mechanism of "judges appointing judges", saying the judiciary cannot always be at the receiving end of the Executive.

“The oft-repeated phrase that ‘Judges appoint Judges’ is a myth which people have been fed by vested interests through motivated narratives, often drawing sustenance from certain controversial decisions taken in this century in relation to appointment of judges,” Justice Datta observed.

The observations were part of his separate opinion in a split verdict on the legality of a 2023 law on appointments of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.

Justice Datta said sweeping generalisations that the Collegium acted as a law unto itself overlooked the detailed consultative process and the intrinsic role of the Executive, both at the Central and State levels, as well as intelligence and other agencies in the judicial appointment process.

The judge said every judicial appointment bore the imprimatur of the President.

Justice Datta turned the spotlight on the Union government’s “piecemeal approvals” of recommendations made by the Supreme Court Collegium for judicial appointments.

The judge said the government has calibrated the judicial appointment system to override recommendations of the Supreme Court Collegium. Names proposed by the Collegium gather dust for years. Even recommendations for transfer of judges are not acted upon by the government in many cases.

“This court is left to wonder why, even after the judiciary has been relegated to playing second fiddle to the Executive in the matter of appointment of Judges, is there still a clamour to induct an outsider at the stage of selection? Coming as it does from the side of the Executive, the argument ill-behoves its stature and is a feeble attempt to deflect attention from its own dereliction and failure,” Justice Datta said.

The judge said the Supreme Court Collegium, despite the government’s conduct, continue to do its work to “avoid a head-on conflict with the Executive, left with Hobson’s choice to keep the institution running”.

Justice Datta was responding to oral submissions made by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta during the hearing, drawing a parallel between judicial and Election Commission appointments.

Mr. Mehta had questioned the Supreme Court’s consistency, asking why it had rejected “outsiders” in judicial appointments during the NJAC ruling while insisting that the Chief Justice of India sit on the selection committee for Election Commissioners.

Justice Datta said the criticism was “unworthy”, but it was necessary to reply to Mr. Mehta “lest the silence be misunderstood as a tacit acceptance”.

“Vociferous criticism, by itself, does not offer an alternative. While the absence of an outsider in the process may invite scrutiny, Executive supremacy cannot be the cure. The constitutional quest is not to transfer primacy from one organ to another, but to secure a system that preserves institutional independence,” Justice Datta noted.

Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, however, differed with Justice Datta’s observations, saying the submissions by the Solicitor General were not meant as a criticism of the Collegium system.

“In my opinion, it was a submission to the effect that if the Constitution Bench has held that the presence of outsiders in the Collegium as violative of the Doctrine of Separation of Powers, a similar independence should be read in the Executive also… In my perspective, it was neither a criticism of the Collegium system nor initiating any debate regarding the manner in which the system of selection has worked,” Justice Sharma wrote in his opinion.

World.title: Social security, welfare fund board pension distribution from September 24
World.content:
The State government will begin the distribution of social security and welfare fund board pensions for September from Thursday, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan’s office said. The Finance department has sanctioned ₹1,068.79 crore for both categories of pensions. ₹957.93 crore has been sanctioned for the social security pensions, and ₹110.86 crore for welfare fund board pensions.

In the case of the social security pensions, ₹531.62 crore will be deposited directly in the bank accounts of beneficiaries. Pension money totalling ₹426.30 crore will be distributed to homes via primary cooperative credit societies, the Finance department order said. The pension distribution has to be completed by October 5, the order said.

World.title: Sustainability must move from awareness to measurable impact: CPCL
World.content:
Sustainability must move from awareness to action, and from action to measurable impact. “Let us continue to work together, share knowledge, build meaningful partnerships, and translate our commitments into tangible environmental outcomes,” V Sriram, Chief General Manager, HSE, Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) said while delivering the vote of thanks at The Hindu Sustainability Summit 2026.

Mr. Sriram thanked all the panellists and government officials for their insights during the panel discussion and fireside chats. He thanked V. K. Rajeev, Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Government of Tamil Nadu for being a part of the summit.

He thanked IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, MRPL, and other energy-sector organisations for being part of the summit. He thanked The Hindu for putting the event together. “A special word of appreciation to CommuniTree – our NGO partner – and all the sustainability organisations and volunteers who supported the various initiatives such as the Urban Forest Trail, Art for Awareness, and the Installation Art Event at Mathur during the last 30 days,” he said.

World.title: One Indian killed in attack on ship off Oman; Centre condemns attack
World.content:
An Indian was killed in an attack on vessel MV Cape Dao off Oman on Wednesday (September 23, 2026). The vessel was reportedly sailing towards India.

The Centre condemned the attack, calling for the end of “targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region”. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, in a statement posted on social media, said: “We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel MV Cape Dao earlier today off the east coast of Oman. Of the 20 Indian seafarers on board, 19 have been rescued, while 1 Indian national tragically lost his life. We offer our deepest condolences to the family of the deceased. Our Embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the situation and proactively coordinating with the Omani authorities for early repatriation of the Indian seafarers. We thank the Omani authorities for their support.”

“The continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. We reiterate our call for dialogue and diplomacy to de-escalate tensions and enable early return of peace to the region. The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region must be restored at the earliest,” the statement added.

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal identified the killed Indian national as Suraj Yadav from Uttar Pradesh. The Minister said that Yadav succumbed to head injuries after the attack.

The vessel had had 20 Indian seafarers on board, and all 19 surviving crew members have been safely evacuated by the Royal Navy of Oman and are currently ashore, Mr. Sonowal said, adding that directions have been issued to maritime authorities to coordinate closely with Omani authorities and the ship management company to ensure the immediate and safe repatriation of our surviving crew.
